stories.headline: Lexington Council Moves to Override Planning Commission, Gives Up Campus Rezoning First Reading
stories.text: The Lexington-Fayette Urban County Council put Ordinance 0979-26 on its Nov. 19 agenda for first reading, a zone change for Up Campus Lexington, LLC from Medium Density Residential (R-4) and Professional Office (P-1) to Downtown Frame Business (B-2A). The site is 1.134 net acres (1.414 gross) at 226, 228 and 230 E. High St., 209-211, 217 and 219 Stone Ave. and 102 Hagerman Court in Council District 3, about half a mile north of UK's main campus by map check. The ordinance text says Council disagrees with the Planning Commission, which recommended disapproval 5-0-1 at its Oct. 22 hearing, and wishes to approve the zone change. The Nov. 17 work session approved the item and sent it to the docket without a new hearing. Council action is listed for Dec. 1, ahead of the Jan. 20, 2027 deadline. The legislation page does not state units, beds or stories. Edition 26 reported the plan as a 10-story building and three townhomes with more than 750 beds, per the Herald-Leader as cited by CivicLex. Up Campus Lexington - PLN-MAR-26-00019 Applicant Up Campus Lexington, LLC Zoning R-4 / P-1 to B-2A Site 1.134 ac net / 1.414 gross Planning Commission Disapproval 5-0-1 (Oct. 22) First reading Nov. 19 Council action Dec. 1 (deadline Jan. 20, 2027)

stories.headline: Landmark Commission Clears One Demolition for 30-Story, 300-Unit West Campus Tower
stories.text: Austin's Historic Landmark Commission approved a demolition permit for one of two 1920s houses at 2307 Rio Grande and postponed the decision on 2309 to its Dec. 2 meeting. The developer's state filing describes an apartment building across the 2305 to 2309 lots with 300 student housing units on 30 floors. Earlier pipeline coverage identified the developer as University Realty. City staff recommended approval once a city documentation package is complete. Cathy Norman of University Area Partners asked for the postponement to allow talks with the developer. Details come from a search excerpt of the Daily Texan story; the full page could not be fetched. 2305-2309 Rio Grande, West Campus Units 300 student housing units Height 30 floors 2307 demolition Approved 2309 demolition Postponed to Dec. 2

stories.headline: Auburn Extends Downtown Apartment and Private Dorm Moratorium to Aug. 31, 2027
stories.text: Auburn City Council on Nov. 17 extended its freeze on multiple-unit developments and private dormitories in the Urban Core, including the College Edge Overlay District, and Urban Neighborhood-West. Staff asked for 12 months; Ward 4's Tyler Adams moved to cut it to nine, which passed 5-3, and the amended extension passed with only Connie Fitch Taylor opposed. First adopted Nov. 18, 2025, the moratorium will now run about 21 months. City Manager Megan McGowen Crouch said stormwater, sewer and traffic models are complete or under way and a consultant is writing new zoning rules for the two districts; staff plans to recommend some smaller-scale housing types. Brett Basquin of Foresite Group, which has a stake in private dormitory projects near downtown, spoke against the extension.

stories.headline: Greystar's 1,010-Bed 'Accolade' Rezone Near U of U Opens for Public Comment
stories.text: Salt Lake City posted an online open house for petition PLNPCM2026-00928, the Accolade Rezone at about 780 S. Guardsman Way. Greystar and Valley Behavioral Health, joint applicants, seek to rezone the site from Institutional (I) to Mixed-Use 6 (MU-6) for a five-story student housing community serving the University of Utah: about 345 units and 1,010 beds on the Carmen B. Pingree Autism Center of Learning site, which plans to relocate. The proposed community benefit is an on-site cafe run by nonprofit Lucky Ones Coffee. Comment runs Nov. 17 to Jan. 1, 2027, followed by Planning Commission and City Council hearings on dates not yet set. Accolade - 780 S. Guardsman Way Applicants Greystar / Valley Behavioral Health Rezone I to MU-6 Units / beds ~345 / ~1,010 Stories 5 Comment period Nov. 17 - Jan. 1, 2027

stories.school_name: University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill
stories.headline: Chapel Hill Approves Redgate's 306 W. Franklin, 7-1, Alongside New LUMO
stories.text: Chapel Hill Town Council approved Redgate's conditional zoning for 306 W. Franklin St. 7-1 on Nov. 18, with Camille Berry opposed. The seven-story mixed-use building, about 40 feet shorter than the expired Longfellow wet lab plan, would carry 200 to 250 apartments per town materials and N&O coverage, 240 parking spaces and retail on Franklin and Rosemary, including 2,000 square feet of rent-free retail on West Rosemary. There are no on-site affordable units; the developer commits $1 million to an affordable project elsewhere in town. Developer Damian Szary said the building targets adult, 12-month residents rather than undergraduates, though the site is a short walk from UNC. Groundbreaking is targeted for fall 2027. Council also adopted an updated Land Use Management Ordinance, 7-1.

stories.headline: The Samuel Tops Out: 230 Student Units, 13 Stories in Tempe
stories.text: Brinkmann Constructors topped out The Samuel, Pineview Development's mixed-use student housing tower near ASU: 230 units across 13 above-ground stories, one level of underground parking and ground-floor retail leased to Finney's Craft House and La La Land. Arris Studio Architects designed it; Tempe Mayor Corey Woods spoke at the event. Completion is anticipated in summer 2027.

stories.headline: Pittsburgh Committee Advances Central Oakland Rezoning to Open Lab Sites to Housing
stories.text: Pittsburgh City Council's standing committee on Nov. 10 advanced an ordinance amending Zoning Code Section 911.04.A.41(b)(6), Multi-Suite Residential (General) in the UC-E District, so Central Oakland sites reserved for laboratory and research use could take residential development. Council President R. Daniel Lavelle said the lab sites have not materialized and Oakland's housing shortage is spilling into other neighborhoods. Central Oakland's inclusionary overlay requires 10 percent affordable units in projects of 20 or more units. A final council vote is still required and had not been reported as of publication.

stories.headline: Athens Arena District Plan Leans Toward Student Housing as Downtown Supply Swells
stories.text: Athens-Clarke officials are working with Accenture on a master plan for the district between the Classic Center and the North Oconee River: hotel, parking deck, apartments, townhouses, bars and restaurants around a plaza. The county now plans to lease parcels individually rather than use one master developer. Consultants called the downtown student apartment market soft, with 3,000 bedrooms coming online within two years, but expect a rebound with UGA growing about 2 percent a year. Commissioner Carol Myers said the plan looks most likely to mean student housing; Commissioner Melissa Link said she prefers student housing behind the arena along the river. Consultants also project a $1 million annual arena bond shortfall starting in fiscal 2029. Separately, Printworks is rising at Broad and Thomas streets; unit count not stated.

stories.headline: Bloomington Eases ADU and Fourplex Rules, Keeps Duplex Cap
stories.text: Bloomington council voted 8-1 on Nov. 18 to adopt UDO amendments raising ADU size limits to 1,000 square feet, loosening cottage-development density and lifting street-facing entrance limits on triplexes and fourplexes. A 7-2 amendment kept the 15-per-year duplex cap and 150-foot spacing buffer in R1-R3. Public comment cited students paying $550 a bedroom in older houses versus $1,200 or more in new construction.

stories.headline: 908 Group Names Chevron Block for Downtown Tallahassee Student Housing
stories.text: The Democrat reports 908 Group plans student apartments on the 2.41-acre 'Chevron' site and a hotel on the adjacent 2.68-acre 'Johns' site; Drury separately plans a 213-room hotel nearby. Beds not stated.

stories.headline: Clemson Rezones Highway 93 Corridor; Up to 50 Townhouses Possible
stories.text: Council voted unanimously to rezone the Clemson Motel property to CP-2 and 5-1 to rezone 23 corridor parcels, which could accommodate up to 50 townhouses near Vista Drive. Developer not named.

stories.headline: Area Plan Commission Backs Pearl Place Rezoning in West Lafayette
stories.text: The commission unanimously recommended an eight-unit, 12-bedroom, three-story building at Pearl and Rusk streets, replacing a four-unit house conversion. It moves to City Council.

stories.headline: 122 State St. Rezoning Heads to Madison Council
stories.text: Legistar 94812 would convert a six-story commercial building to seven stories with 34 units and 1,375 square feet of commercial space for Cox Rentals, about 0.6 mile from Library Mall by map check.

stories.headline: Manhattan Pushes Edge 3.0 Vote to Dec. 15
stories.text: No vote on the K-State Foundation's Edge District TIF/STAR bond requests; the city and Foundation have not agreed on a development agreement, now expected Dec. 3. Residential counts not stated.

stories.headline: StudiOne Rises Half a Block From UC Berkeley
stories.text: Austin Group's eight-story, 66-studio building at 2138 Kittredge St. (five affordable) is under construction with Hawk Builders as GC; completion expected mid-2028.

stories.headline: Starkville Aldermen Approve 21-Bedroom Townhouse Infill, 4-3
stories.text: Acadian Driftwood LLC won a special exception for seven three-bedroom townhouses on 0.7 acre on Ernest H. Jones Jr. Drive; construction expected to start in January.

stories.headline: JLL Places $78.5M Takeout Loan on Tempe's 335-Unit Alyssa
stories.text: Corten Real Estate's senior credit platform lent to CrossHarbor Capital Partners on the 2024-built community. Conventional multifamily; distance to campus not stated. About $234K per unit (derived).

stories.headline: Subtext Buys 674-Bed Skyloft Off-Market, Two Blocks From UT Austin
stories.text: Subtext Living acquired Skyloft, a 212-unit, 674-bed student housing community built in 2018 in Austin's West Campus, two blocks from the University of Texas. The deal was negotiated off-market directly with the seller; the seller and price were not disclosed. Subtext plans a value-add repositioning: refreshed common-area furnishings, upgraded study lounges, fitness center and pool improvements, a new clubroom and a rebrand. The purchase was announced with the 325-bed Fifteen51 in Reno; together the two deals add nearly 1,000 beds and two new markets for Subtext. Skyloft - West Campus, Austin Buyer Subtext Living Units / beds 212 / 674 Year built 2018 Price / seller Not disclosed Strategy Value-add, rebrand

stories.headline: Monument Square JV Acquires 683-Bed Scarlet Near Texas Tech
stories.text: A joint venture of a Monument Square Investment Group affiliate and funds managed by an unnamed U.S. investment manager bought The Scarlet, a 228-unit, 683-bed community built in 2005 in North Overton, about a 15-minute walk from Memorial Circle. It has 17 residential buildings and a clubhouse, about 95 percent of beds in three- and four-bedroom layouts, and is 100 percent occupied for 2026-27. Price and seller were not in the visible text; the full article is paywalled.

stories.headline: 150-Unit Helix and Ellipse Listed in Seattle's U District
stories.text: The two-building portfolio, three blocks from U District light rail, is marketed on 28 percent year-one NOI growth plus renovation upside. Listing stage; no price stated.

stories.headline: IHL Approves Songy Highroads as P3 Partner for Vaught-Hemingway District
stories.text: The IHL board on Nov. 19 approved Atlanta-based Songy Highroads as Ole Miss's preferred development partner for a mixed-use district on the north side of Vaught-Hemingway Stadium, delivered as a public-private partnership. President and COO Todd Nocerini described stadium upgrades and expansion, retail, office, hotel, extended-stay residential and a parking deck around an outdoor plaza; the release also lists athletics and foundation offices and expanded student seating. The team includes Provident Resources Group, J.P. Morgan, Regions Bank, Brasfield & Gorrie and Cooper Carry; Brailsford & Dunlavey advised the 2025 selection committee. No unit counts or dollar figures were released. HottyToddy, citing OMSpirit, reported that work would not begin until a ground lease is signed and a bond deal closes around January 2028, and described the residential piece as condos. Vaught-Hemingway District P3 Developer Songy Highroads Approval IHL, Nov. 19 Team Provident, J.P. Morgan, Regions, B&G, Cooper Carry Units / cost Not released Bond closing ~Jan. 2028 (reported)

stories.headline: UT Pulls Creekside From Renewals, Recasts Dobie Twenty21 as Dell House
stories.text: Creekside Residence Hall (190 students) will not be offered for renewal next fall, and Dobie Twenty21 closes for 2027-28 while UT plans a redesign as Dell House, with no timeline given. Whitis Avenue Hall opens in fall 2027 for about 1,000 residents, and the first law-student residence hall takes residents in fall 2028. The new arena and adjacent student-athlete housing north of East MLK Jr. Blvd., between Robert Dedman Drive and I-35, now carry a fall 2029 date. Net on-campus bed change for 2027-28 is not stated.

stories.headline: College Station Floats Three Scenarios for Harvey Road Apartments
stories.text: A Nov. 18 workshop showed incremental, targeted and broad redevelopment options for the 1970s-80s apartment corridor from Texas Avenue to SH 6. Draft plan due spring 2027; hearings February to April.

stories.headline: UC Capital Plan Points About $2.8B to UCLA
stories.text: The proposed $29.9 billion 2026-32 plan covers housing, seismic and research work; the UCLA housing share is not broken out.

stories.headline: Baylor Undergrads Fall 2.3%; $30M Deficit Projected
stories.text: Undergraduates fell to 13,860 and first-years 6 percent to 3,340; Baylor deferred noncritical construction.

stories.headline: ASU Only Arizona University to Grow
stories.text: Up 805 students (0.6 percent) per ABOR; University of Arizona fell 7.6 percent and NAU 6.4 percent.

stories.headline: Georgia Tech Tops 58,000 Students
stories.text: Up 2.7 percent; it remains the largest USG school as the system hits a record 392,000.

stories.headline: Lexington Council Takes Up 750-Bed Up Campus Tower After Planning Commission Voted 5-0 to Deny
stories.text: The Urban County Council will review the Up Campus Student Living zone change on East High Street, between Hagerman Court and Stone Avenue in the Aylesford neighborhood, at its Tuesday, Nov. 17 work session at 3 p.m. The Planning Commission voted 5-0 in late October to recommend denial. As described by the Herald-Leader and cited by CivicLex, the plan is a 10-story building plus three townhomes with more than 750 beds, and it would require demolishing several homes. Planning Director James Duncan laid out three paths. Council can approve or deny without its own hearing, which would likely put a final vote at the Dec. 1 meeting; it can hold a second public hearing, likely in mid-January; or it can take no action, in which case the denial recommendation stands after Jan. 20, 90 days from the commission hearing. Read-through: this is a council-level test of a large near-campus tower against a unanimous commission denial. CivicLex also notes that a separate Core Spaces project has already demolished other homes in the area (per Lex18). Which option council chooses on Nov. 17 is unknown as of press time. Up Campus - East High St., Lexington Program 10-story bldg + 3 townhomes Beds 750+ Planning Commission 5-0 recommend denial Council work session Nov. 17, 3 p.m. Earliest final vote Dec. 1 (if no new hearing) Denial stands if no action After Jan. 20

stories.headline: USC Development Foundation Seeks Rezoning of Full Main/Whaley Block for Student Housing
stories.text: The University of South Carolina Development Foundation has applied to rezone 3.5 acres, the entire block bounded by Heyward, Main, Sumter and Whaley streets, to allow student housing. Agenda documents list the planned use as 'Institutional - Dormitory.' The block sits across Sumter Street from USC's Stone soccer stadium and near the 1,800-bed Campus Village. The Columbia Planning Commission vote was expected at its Nov. 12 meeting; the outcome was not in the pipeline record. City staff recommended approval, citing the university's growing needs, while acknowledging the rezoning does not align with the Mill District Plan. The foundation assembled the parcels during 2026, and the former College Quik Mart on the block was demolished in late summer. Unknowns: bed count, delivery structure (foundation-owned, P3 or otherwise) and timeline. Applicant Hunter Lambert said a construction schedule will follow city approvals. Main / Whaley Block - Columbia, S.C. Applicant USC Development Foundation Site 3.5 ac, full block Listed use Institutional - Dormitory Staff Recommend approval Planning Commission Nov. 12 (outcome not confirmed) Beds Not yet available
stories.source: Post and Courier Columbia (via Yahoo News)

stories.headline: Athens Commission Sends Cardinal Group's 660 W. Broad St. Plan Back to Planning, 6-2
stories.text: After commissioners criticized the proposal at October agenda-setting, Cardinal Group offered to drop some townhouses and add parking. On Nov. 4 the Athens-Clarke County Commission voted 6-2 on Commissioner Myers' motion to return that revised version to the Planning Commission; Hamby and Wright opposed, preferring to vote it down that night. The student apartment building would replace a strip mall between Finley and Pope streets; a decision is held until next month. Risk flag: Flagpole counts at least five commissioners (Hamby, Wright, Myers, Thornton, Link) leaning against, and rezonings need six votes. Offered benefits include a plaza commemorating the Hancock-Reese neighborhood, a housing trust fund contribution and stream remediation. Opponents cite parking at one space per two residents and extending C-D downtown zoning west of Finley.

stories.headline: Charlottesville Council Unanimously Approves LV Collective's Eight-Story West Main Building
stories.text: City Council on Nov. 2 pulled the special exception permit for 835, 843 and 847 West Main St. (PL-26-0126) off the consent agenda at Councilor Michael Payne's request, discussed it and passed it unanimously. The eight-story LV Collective building, between West Main and CRHA's Westhaven, is approved for 182 units plus a cafe and public plaza under CMU-8 zoning (up to 156 feet with bonus). The five exceptions cover ground-story height, active depth, finished floor elevation, street-facing entry spacing and two-tier bike racks. The project still needs major site plan approval: a fourth comment letter went out Oct. 22 and LV Collective was granted one more review cycle Nov. 4. Bed count not stated.

stories.headline: Core Spaces Floats 300-Unit 'Hub Columbia' on Downtown Katy Station Site
stories.text: Core Spaces has submitted a preliminary concept to the City of Columbia for Hub Columbia - Fourth and Broadway: two six-story residential buildings with 300 units and 371 parking spaces on land now holding Shiloh Bar and Grill (the 1909 Katy Station depot), Ice House and Broadway Diner. The filing seeks feedback before a formal plan. The depot is on the National Register; a Save Katy Station group has raised $20,000 to move it and says Core Spaces is helping work toward a resolution. Core Spaces bought The Collective (318 units, now State on Campus Columbia) in March. Bed count and distance to campus not stated.

stories.headline: Starkville Grants Height Variance for 500-Bed Student Housing and Hotel Project
stories.text: The Board of Aldermen on Nov. 3 approved a variance and special exemption for York Developments (Hattiesburg) and partner Desai Companies (Ridgeland) on a roughly $45 million project: a 100-room Home2Suites and a 500-bed student housing development on 21.6 acres off Highway 12 and Pat Station Road. The variance lets the student buildings exceed the height cap by about six feet; the exemption allows more than 25 percent four-bedroom units. A November 2025 TIF authorized up to $3.35 million in bonds for a 1,367-foot road and Pat Station Road upgrades, due early 2027. Site plans are expected by year-end, with construction starting early 2027 and student housing complete before fall 2028, the same delivery year as College View Phase 2 (see P3).

stories.headline: Bloomington Plan Commission Backs Hilltop Court Switch to 24 One-Bedroom Rentals
stories.text: The Plan Commission on Nov. 9 voted 7-0 to send Dwellings LLC's PUD amendment at 1237 W. Allen St. to council with a positive recommendation, after a 4-3 motion for a December second hearing failed. Two unbuilt townhome buildings (10 three-bedroom condos) become one three-story building of 24 one-bedroom rentals, taking the 5.32-acre site from 114 to 128 units and from 166 to 160 bedrooms. Developer Mark Lauchli said costs rose from about $160 to over $210 per square foot since 2021 and new units would likely rent under $1,000. Findings say the project targets non-undergraduate renters. Council date not stated.

stories.headline: Evanston Approves 26-Story, 360-Unit 900 Clark St. Tower, 8-1
stories.text: City Council on Nov. 9 approved CSP Evanston Land's amendment to the Lot B planned development (900 Clark St., 1701-1765 Maple Ave., 901-921 Church St.) for a 26-story mixed-use building with 360 units, about 2,484 square feet of retail and 112 off-site parking spaces in the Research Park district. The project needed a Site Development Allowance for 298 feet against a 150-foot cap. The city is awaiting a building permit submission. Not described as student housing.
stories.source: City of Evanston, Proposed Development Projects

stories.headline: Dwight Capital Writes $42M HUD Loan for 184-Unit One Salem
stories.text: A nonrecourse 40-year HUD 221(d)(4) construction loan funds Cheferkon Partners' eight-building garden complex at 4033 Vestmill Road, four miles south of Wake Forest. First building Q3 2027; completion 2028. Loan per unit about $228K (derived).

stories.headline: Athens Raises Downtown Height Cap to 130 Feet
stories.text: The commission lifted the downtown maximum from 100 to 130 feet, with Tiffany Taylor opposed. It also extended the inclusionary payment option to more zones and dropped a reduced-parking incentive outside downtown.

stories.headline: Milledge/Springdale Rezone Clears Planning
stories.text: Planning approved C-O to RM-1 for two-bedroom condos over ground-floor office; historic review also required. Possibly the 710 S. Milledge case on the Nov. 17 agenda (zoning label conflicts; unverified).

stories.headline: Oakland UC-E Residential Bill on Nov. 17 Council Agenda
stories.text: Bill 2026-0714 would allow 50-100 percent multi-suite residential on UC-E lots within 100 feet of an EMI district, for monthly-or-longer rentals. Hearing held Nov. 4; vote not yet posted.

stories.headline: Near-Campus Rezoning Reaches Ann Arbor Planning
stories.text: Item 26-1884, 'Near Downtown and Central Campus Rezoning,' is on the Nov. 17 agenda with a staff memo and a Leaf proposal. No addresses or recommendation listed.
stories.source: Ann Arbor City Planning Commission (Legistar agenda)

stories.headline: 2900 S. Main Adds a Story, 61 Units
stories.text: SP25-0013 rezones Office to TC1 and adds a fifth floor and 16 units. Staff recommends approval; Council next.
stories.source: Ann Arbor City Planning Commission (Legistar agenda)

stories.headline: Hill Church Site Eyed for 12 Student Units
stories.text: A filing proposes a three-story, 17,000-square-foot building with 12 for-rent student units at 965 Broadway (Citipointe Church). Applicant and hearing date unconfirmed.

stories.headline: Back Nine Acquisitions Buys 108-Unit Madison Portfolio From Flad for About $30 Million
stories.text: Back Nine Acquisitions has bought a two-property, 108-unit apartment portfolio in Madison's West submarket from Flad Development & Investments for about $30 million. CBRE's Gretchen Richards, Matson Holbrook and Sean Beuche represented the seller. The portfolio is The Tradition at Smoky's Club (59 units, 3007 University Ave.) and The Whitney Reserve (49 units, 5201 Old Middleton Rd.), about 1.4 miles apart with roughly 2,400 square feet of ground-floor retail. Neither is described as student housing; distance to campus not stated. Madison West Portfolio Buyer / seller Back Nine / Flad Broker CBRE Units 108 (59 + 49) Price ~$30M Price per unit (derived) ~$278K

stories.headline: Stalled Turtle Lane Playhouse Site in Newton Sells at Auction
stories.text: The Turtle Lane Playhouse redevelopment site sold at a McLaughlin & Co. auction on Oct. 22, with a listed price of $8.25 million; the buyer is not yet public. Developer Stephen Vona had planned housing, commercial space and a new theater, but the bank sued in 2023 over a $9.4 million 2018 construction loan and the city issued a stop-work order on an unpermitted building. The lot is zoned VC2 in the Village Center Overlay, allowing 3.5 stories by right. Distance to campus not stated.

stories.headline: IHL Revives College View Phase 2: Greystar Affiliate to Add 527 Upperclassman Beds at MSU
stories.text: The Mississippi IHL Board of Trustees on Oct. 26 approved a second phase of College View on the northwest edge of campus, adding 527 upperclassman beds on 16 adjacent acres. A new entity, EDR College View II, will build it; Phase 1 was developed under a 2018 lease with EDR College View MS, a Greystar affiliate. MSU VP Regina Hyatt put the cost at around $60 million. The Phase 2 ground lease runs 40 years with options to extend up to 25 years, and EDR pays MSU a base rent of 5 percent of gross revenue each fiscal year. IHL also approved easements and shared parking and amenity agreements. Phase 2 stalled during COVID-19 and is now projected for fall 2028. Phase 1 (fall 2019, $67 million) has about 650 beds and 50,000 square feet of retail. College View Phase 2 - Mississippi State Developer entity EDR College View II (Greystar affil.) Beds / site 527 / 16 ac Est. cost ~$60M Cost per bed (derived) ~$114K Ground lease 40 yrs + up to 25 Rent to MSU 5% of gross revenue Delivery Fall 2028

stories.headline: UW-Madison Files City Master Plan Amendments for 1,690 P3 Dorm Beds
stories.text: UW-Madison has filed Campus Master Plan amendments with the City of Madison for two dormitories: about 1,000 beds at 115 N. Mills St. (LNDUSE-2026-00060, filed Oct. 23) and about 690 beds at 919 W. Dayton St. (LNDUSE-2026-00061, filed Nov. 3). Plan Commission is set for Dec. 14 and Common Council for Jan. 12, 2027. These are the sites of the PRG Badger Properties public-private residence halls already approved at the state level; this is the first city land-use step. The city listing does not name the developer.
stories.source: City of Madison Planning, Current Development Proposals

stories.headline: Brackenridge Agreement Goes to Austin Council Nov. 19
stories.text: The amended agreement sets parameters for UT's 190 acres (65-foot height cap from Lake Austin Blvd., 75 percent impervious cover, 200-foot lake setback) and updates UT's Mueller lease. Regulating plan and TIRZ return in spring 2027. Unit counts not stated.

stories.headline: Radford Court Residents Press UW on Greystar P3
stories.text: A Nov. 3 letter asks UW to review rents (some about $3,000 a month vs. about $1,500 for similar units) and staffing at the Greystar-managed family complex. Management says it hired a full-time staffer.

stories.headline: UMD Undergraduates Rise to 32,304
stories.text: Fall 2026 undergraduates rose 429 (1.3 percent) from 31,875, with 10,584 freshmen and 25.2 percent out of state. Publication day not stated.

stories.headline: UIUC Leads State in International Losses
stories.text: Illinois public enrollment rose just 287 (0.15 percent) for fall 2026; international enrollment fell 14.2 percent, with UIUC posting the largest headcount loss. No UIUC total given.

stories.headline: Affinius Writes $100.3 Million Construction Loan for Starwood-Trinitas 672-Bed Tower in Oakland
stories.text: Affinius Capital has provided $100.3 million in construction financing to Starwood Capital Group and Trinitas Ventures for Atmosphere Pittsburgh, a 12-story mixed-use student housing building at 217 Halket St. in Oakland, near the University of Pittsburgh. Commercial Observer reported no broker on the loan. Plans call for 326 units, 34 of them affordable, and 114 parking spaces. Cardinal Group will manage the property. Completion is targeted for summer 2028, in time for the 2028-29 academic year. The article gives two different construction start dates ('last month' and 'in July'), and the bed count conflicts with earlier coverage: Commercial Observer says 672 beds, while TribLive previously reported 627. Read-through: a nine-figure construction loan from a debt fund on a Pitt-adjacent tower is a direct read on lender appetite for Oakland. The same week, City Council held a hearing on a zoning change that would open more of Oakland's UC-E district to majority-residential buildings (see brief below). Atmosphere Pittsburgh - 217 Halket St. Sponsors Starwood Capital / Trinitas Lender / loan Affinius Capital / $100.3M Stories / units / beds 12 / 326 / 672 (TribLive: 627) Affordable units 34 Loan per bed (derived, 672 beds) ~$149K Manager / delivery Cardinal Group / summer 2028

stories.headline: Greystar Files to Rezone Pingree Center Site South of Campus for 1,010-Bed Student Community
stories.text: Greystar has applied to Salt Lake City to rezone the Carmen B. Pingree Autism Center of Learning site at 780 S. Guardsman Way, 5.33 acres on two parcels at the northwest corner of Guardsman Way and Sunnyside Avenue, from Institutional (I) to Mixed Use 6 (MU-6). Owner Valley Behavioral Health joined as co-applicant on Oct. 28. The plan is a five-story, roughly 56-foot student housing community of about 345 units and 1,010 beds in one- to five-bedroom layouts, with two courtyards, a pool, spa, rooftop lounge and an interior garage of about 500 stalls, or about 65 units per acre. A Snell & Wilmer narrative letter is dated Oct. 26, a city-requested traffic study is underway, and the proposed community benefit is subsidized space for Lucky Ones Coffee. No hearing date is set. Risk flag: the application does not say whether Greystar is under contract, and the Utah Board of Higher Education had approved the university's request to bid up to $21 million in state capital funds for the same parcels. Building Salt Lake notes campus housing was 86 percent occupied in early October. 780 S. Guardsman Way - Greystar Site 5.33 ac, two parcels Rezone request I to MU-6 Units / beds ~345 / 1,010 Beds per unit (derived) ~2.9 Parking ~500 stalls (~0.5 per bed, derived) Competing interest U. approved to bid up to $21M

stories.headline: Fort Sanders Upzoning at 1625 Clinch Ave. Goes to Knoxville Council for First Reading Nov. 10
stories.text: Knoxville City Council takes up case 10-I-26-RZ on first reading Nov. 10, with second reading Nov. 24. The request would rezone 1.04 acres at 1625 Clinch Ave., 0 Clinch Ave. and 1634 Laurel Ave. in Fort Sanders from RN-5 to RN-6 Multi-Family Residential, keeping the NC overlay, with companion sector plan and plan amendments (MDR to MDR/O). Heyoh Architecture is the applicant for owner Brighton Developers LLC. Staff recommended approval and the Knoxville-Knox County Planning Commission approved the request Oct. 1. The staff report places the site within 500 feet of campus, about 0.2 mile from Cumberland Avenue. Units, beds and height have not been specified.

stories.headline: Ann Arbor Council Adopts Dean II Rezoning, Adding Fifth Avenue Parcel to 15-Story Student Project
stories.text: Ann Arbor City Council adopted the Dean II rezoning on second reading, moving 548 S. Fifth Ave. (0.17 acre) from R4C Multiple-Family to D1 Downtown Core with Midtown Character and Secondary Street designations, and approved the Dean II area plan at the same meeting. The Planning Commission had recommended approval 7-0 on Aug. 18. The minutes do not record a tally, applicant or unit count. Citizen Portal's coverage reports a 9-0 vote over neighborhood opposition and cites staff describing about 240 apartments in a 15-story building.
stories.source: City of Ann Arbor Council minutes

stories.headline: Lawrence Approves Up to $100 Million in STAR and CID Bonds for Gateway Phase Two
stories.text: The Lawrence City Commission voted unanimously Nov. 3 to authorize up to $100 million in bonds for the second phase of KU's Gateway district: up to $75 million in STAR bonds and up to $25 million in Community Improvement District bonds, both repaid from project-generated tax revenue. The CID adds a new 2 percent special sales tax. Bond counsel said the city would not be liable if revenues fall short. The Gateway, tied to KU's new football stadium, already includes a convention center and will add a hotel, student housing, retail and a plaza. KU CFO Jeff DeWitt said the roughly 150-room hotel could open by the end of 2028; no guaranteed maximum price is set for it. A Student Senate representative and Commissioners Sellers and Courtney raised concerns about the CID tax falling on students living in the district.

stories.headline: Provo Rezones Park Plaza for Cole West's 523-Bed Project East of BYU
stories.text: Provo City Council voted unanimously Nov. 3 (7-0 per KUTV) to rezone the vacant Park Plaza property at 910 N. 900 East from Residential Conservation to Campus Residential. Cole West plans a six-story, 146-unit, 523-bed student complex, and the approval caps the project at those counts. The development agreement sets 0.75 parking spaces per bed (390 stalls, 130 of them stacker spaces), 247 indoor bike stalls, contracted parking agreements, no parking charge for residents without cars, and a parking study one year after opening. Cole West expects a 30-month build and an opening for the 2029 or 2030 school year. Park Plaza - Cole West Units / beds 146 / 523 (capped) Beds per unit (derived) ~3.6 Parking 0.75/bed; 390 stalls Opening 2029 or 2030 school year

stories.headline: Athens Commission Holds Reese and West Broad Downtown Rezoning Over Parking
stories.text: After nearly two hours of debate on Nov. 4, the Athens-Clarke County Mayor and Commission voted 6-2 to hold for up to 40 days a request to rezone a proposed mixed-use site at Reese Street and West Broad Street to 'downtown.' Residents cited thin parking near downtown student housing, and District 8 Commissioner Carol Myers said she would not approve the plan as it stands. The commission also voted 7-1 to let qualifying projects in Mixed Density Residential and Commercial districts pay a fee in lieu of on-site inclusionary units, with fees going to an affordable housing fund. That change bears directly on student housing pro formas in those districts. The next regular session is Dec. 1.

stories.school_name: University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill
stories.headline: Chapel Hill Council to Hear 200-250 Unit Rewrite of Franklin Street Lab Site Nov. 18
stories.text: Chapel Hill Town Council will consider conditional zoning application CZD-26-2 on Nov. 18. McAdams, for owner Chapel Hill Franklin Street Labs 1, LLC, proposes to redevelop six parcels at 306 W. Franklin St. as a mixed-use project with 200 to 250 dwelling units over ground-floor commercial space, under Town Center-3 conditional zoning. The site was previously approved (CZD-23-7) for the roughly 380,000-square-foot Chapel Hill Life Sciences Center, so the filing swaps lab space for housing on a downtown block. A Planning Commission meeting was listed for Oct. 20; its outcome was not found. Distance to campus is not stated in the notice.
stories.source: Town of Chapel Hill legal notice

stories.headline: Council Hears Bill to Allow Majority-Residential Buildings in Oakland's UC-E District
stories.text: City Council held a Nov. 4 hearing on Bill 2026-0714, which would let UC-E lots within 100 feet of the EMI district, which covers parts of Pitt and two UPMC hospitals, devote 50 to 100 percent of floor area to monthly-or-longer multi-suite residential. Today UC-E permits residential only in fully affordable projects or below 50 percent of floor area. Oakland holds the city's only UC-E zoning. No vote has been reported.

stories.headline: ZBA Grants Setback Relief for 64-Unit Building at 700 N. Main
stories.text: The Ann Arbor Zoning Board of Appeals voted 6-1 to grant side and rear setback variances for a 68-foot multifamily building at 700 N. Main St., finding the floodplain cut usable area by more than 20 percent; the relief allows 64 units. The neighborhood association filed opposition. Minimum setbacks differ between the agenda and the motion.
stories.source: City of Ann Arbor ZBA minutes

stories.headline: 710 S. Milledge Ave. Seeks Multifamily Zoning
stories.text: The Athens-Clarke Planning Commission heard ZONE-2026-10-2088, a request to rezone 710 S. Milledge Ave. (owner Greg Waddell, Hodges on Milledge) from Commercial-Office to RM-2 multifamily. The draft agenda gives no acreage, unit count or staff recommendation, and no outcome has been posted.

stories.school_name: University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill
stories.headline: 701 MLK Blvd. Modification Set for Nov. 18 Hearing
stories.text: Council will also hear MOD-26-8, a modification to the approved 7-8 story, 175-200 unit multifamily building at 701 Martin Luther King Jr. Blvd. (applicant Thomas and Hutton), rezoned to Mixed Use-Village in 2025. The project is in permitting; the town page does not describe the requested change.

stories.headline: Demolition Permits Pulled on Three East John St. Lots
stories.text: Legacy 1943 LLC pulled Champaign demolition permits for 105, 107 and 109 E. John St. in Campustown ($50,000 to $65,000 each), a week after seven-story multifamily permits were filed for 105 and 106 E. John St. (Wells & Wells Construction). Project name and bed count were not disclosed.

stories.headline: 1906 Stadium Road Special Exception on Nov. 10 Agenda
stories.text: The Charlottesville Planning Commission is scheduled to act Nov. 10 on a special exception for 1906 Stadium Road (PL-26-0120). The agenda names no applicant or program, and residential use is not confirmed.

stories.headline: Joaquin Townhome Rezone Passes 4-3 With Rental Ban
stories.text: Provo council also voted 4-3 to rezone 313 E. 200 North in the Joaquin neighborhood to Medium Density Residential for 10 townhomes, each deed-restricted against rentals for five years.

stories.headline: Monument Square Venture Buys 962-Bed Social Block in Starkville
stories.text: A joint venture between an affiliate of Monument Square Investment Group and funds managed by an undisclosed investment manager has acquired The Social Block and Townhomes, a 385-unit, 962-bed student housing community near the Mississippi State University campus. The property offers two- and four-bedroom apartments and townhomes. Seller, price and financing were not released, so per-bed pricing cannot be derived. The Social Block and Townhomes Units / beds 385 / 962 Beds per unit (derived) 2.5 Buyer Monument Square JV Seller / price Not disclosed

stories.headline: Hackberry Lane Adds 1,650 Shadow-Market Beds in Gainesville and Tuscaloosa
stories.text: Hackberry Lane, the student housing investor-operator founded in 2023 by Reid Marks, Nick Helfand and Cameron Koffman, completed multiple acquisitions near the University of Florida and the University of Alabama totaling about 1,650 beds, bringing its portfolio to about 4,000 beds. The firm targets townhomes, single-family homes and smaller apartment buildings in walkable campus-adjacent neighborhoods. Property names, prices, sellers and the split between the two markets were not disclosed.

stories.headline: Meadowbrook's 627 Units Trade in Largest Lawrence Multifamily Sale
stories.text: Northmarq's Kansas City team (Casey Wilhm, Jeff Lamott, David Belpedio) closed the sale of Meadowbrook Apartments, 627 units on more than 41 acres at 2601 Dover Square just west of KU, plus an adjacent 4.3-acre development tract. Sellers were Meadowbrook Investors LC and M-10 Holdings LC; buyers were The Meadow KS LLC and The Lawn KS LLC. Price was not disclosed. Northmarq calls it the largest multifamily sale in Lawrence history by units, beds and total consideration; the property serves both students and conventional renters.

stories.headline: Alegre Park Sells for $3.5 Million at a 6.24% Cap
stories.text: Matthews' Kyle Inman and Brad Skenderian sold Alegre Park, a 1961-built, 24-unit property at 1827 E. Lemon St. next to ASU, to an unnamed local buyer for $3.5 million ($145.8K per unit, $263 per square foot) against a $3.8 million ask. The in-place cap rate was 6.24 percent. The buyer financed with a 7-year fixed credit union loan at 5.87 percent, 64 percent LTV, recourse.

stories.headline: Rovers Landing Pays $6.3 Million for U District's Ponderay
stories.text: Rovers Landing LLC bought the 1963-built, 40-unit Ponderay Apartments at 5625 15th Ave. NE for $6.27 million (about $156,625 per unit) from Ponderay LLC, represented by Cushman & Wakefield's Jacob Odegard. Units rent to households at about 50 to 60 percent of AMI. Connect CRE reported $6.26 million; publication day not confirmed.

stories.headline: Axium Takes 95% Stake in KU Gateway's 482-Bed On-Campus P3
stories.text: A fund managed by Axium Infrastructure has agreed to acquire a 95 percent interest in an on-campus student housing project under construction in the University of Kansas Gateway District. The undergraduate community comprises two buildings with 199 units and 482 beds, under a 99-year air rights lease with the university and its affiliates. Edgemoor/Sunflower is named as the developer partner, and Asset Living will manage and lease the property. Price was not disclosed. Construction began in June 2026, with opening targeted for the 2028-29 academic year. The same Gateway district received up to $100 million in STAR and CID bond authority from Lawrence on Nov. 3 (see Development News). KU Gateway Housing P3 Investor Axium Infrastructure (95%) Units / beds 199 / 482 Structure 99-year air rights lease Developer / manager Edgemoor/Sunflower / Asset Living Opening 2028-29 academic year

stories.headline: $145 Million Drackett-Taylor Overhaul Underway; Jones Tower Comes Down in 2027
stories.text: Renovation of Drackett and Taylor Tower on Ohio State's north campus has begun, with reopening targeted for autumn 2028. Trustees approved $145 million for the two buildings on Sept. 3. Taylor closed in January after a burst pipe displaced 700 students. Jones Tower will be fenced at semester's end and demolished in 2027. Before the flood, all three towers were to reopen by August 2030. Renovated bed counts were not given.

stories.headline: California Voters Pass $11.25 Billion Housing Bond With $350 Million for Student Beds
stories.text: Proposition 1 passed Nov. 3 with 59.3 percent of the vote as of election night (AP, unofficial). It sets aside $350 million for affordable student housing, split evenly between UC and CSU and expected to fund up to 1,200 beds. A UCLA Lewis Center expert said UCLA's share is unclear given its existing housing capacity.

stories.headline: Ole Miss Posts Fourth Straight Record: 28,960 Students
stories.text: Fall 2026 enrollment rose 2 percent to 28,960 across all campuses, the sixth straight year of growth. The 5,363-student freshman class is the third-largest on record; freshman retention was 87.6 percent.

stories.headline: University Park Hits Record 43,010 Undergraduates
stories.text: University Park enrolled a record 43,010 undergraduates (42,822 in fall 2025) and a record 9,907 first-year students toward a 10,000-a-year goal. Systemwide enrollment fell 3,058 to 83,499, with 1,518 of the decline at the seven closing Commonwealth Campuses.

stories.headline: Charlottesville Weighs Special-Permit Rule for Student Housing
stories.text: Residents are pushing code changes to curb by-right student housing in Fifeville, 10th and Page and Rose Hill. Councilor Michael Payne wants a special permit required in high-displacement-risk areas. Technical amendments could take effect by March; larger changes fall to the five-year code review begun in October, expected to take about a year. LV Collective says its eight-story 843 W. Main St. project has been approved.

stories.headline: UT, Austin Near Brackenridge Deal With East Austin Housing Lease
stories.text: UT and the city are negotiating amendments covering about 190 acres of the west Austin Brackenridge Tract that would allow residential and retail development, plus an updated Central East Austin ground lease that could host future affordable student and faculty housing near the Dell Pediatric Research Institute. A resolution is expected before Nov. 19, then Regents review. Bed counts not stated; the tract is not in West Campus.

stories.headline: Jury Overturns Fayetteville Council, Reviving Trinitas' 611-Bedroom Dickson Street Tower
stories.text: A Washington County jury voted 11-1 on Oct. 29 to overturn the Fayetteville City Council's rejection of Trinitas Ventures' seven-story, 611-bedroom student housing project on Dickson Street between Block and Church avenues. Trinitas sued the city after the council turned the proposal down. City Attorney Kit Williams said logistical concerns remain over vehicles backing out of the building, but that Trinitas appears willing to work with the city on them. The city has 30 days to decide whether to appeal to the Arkansas Court of Appeals. The Fayetteville Flyer and the NWA Democrat-Gazette also reported the verdict. Read-through: the verdict reverses a council denial on one of the most visible student housing sites near the University of Arkansas, but the project is not clear until the 30-day appeal window closes without a filing. Unit count, cost and delivery schedule were not reported. Dickson Street - Trinitas Ventures Stories / bedrooms 7 / 611 Location Dickson St., Block to Church aves. Council action Denied Jury verdict (Oct. 29) 11-1 to overturn Appeal window 30 days (city decision) Units / cost / delivery Not reported

stories.headline: RPM Living Widens 2060 N. High Site to Take In PJ's Grill; 866-Bed Plan Still Not Approved
stories.text: RPM Living's updated proposal for a seven-story apartment and retail building at North High Street and East Woodruff Avenue now includes the former PJ's Grill building at 15 E. Frambes Ave., which closed in September. Earlier plans left that building out. The neighboring Donatos building stays outside the demolition area. University Impact District Review Board records cited by The Lantern put the project at 228 units, 866 beds and 4,000 square feet of retail, including a coffee and juice bar. The Ohio Stater apartments and a Dunkin' at 2060 N. High St. were slated to close for the redevelopment. The city lists the certificate of approval application as continued, so there is no final approval. The Lantern did not say at which meeting it was continued, and RPM did not respond to questions about the larger footprint. Derived: about 3.8 beds per unit, a four-bedroom-heavy mix consistent with purpose-built student housing. 2060 N. High St. - RPM Living Stories 7 Units / beds 228 / 866 Beds per unit (derived) ~3.8 Retail 4,000 SF Site change Adds 15 E. Frambes (PJ's Grill) Status UIDRB application continued

stories.headline: Ann Arbor Council Denies Woodbury Gardens Rezoning, Stalling 342-Unit 1310 Wisteria Plan
stories.text: Ann Arbor City Council denied the Woodbury Gardens conditional rezoning at second reading on Oct. 19, according to the city's project timeline. The request would have moved the 41.3-acre complex on Astor, Wisteria and Woodbury drives from R3/R4 and Public Land to TC1 Transit Corridor, with conditions capping height. The companion 1310 Wisteria site plan called for three seven-story buildings with 342 units and a five-level garage. The Planning Commission denied the rezoning in January, then recommended approval in July. The vote count was not found, and a separate Legistar record for the site plan shows conflicting statuses until minutes post.
stories.source: City of Ann Arbor (Engage Ann Arbor)

stories.headline: Athens Commission Hears Cardinal Group's 465-Bedroom West Broad Rezoning Nov. 4
stories.text: The Athens-Clarke Mayor and Commission will hold a public hearing Nov. 4 on rezoning 2.47 acres at 363 Reese St. and 600 and 660 W. Broad St. from C-G and RM-2 to C-D (PD) in the West End Downtown Design Area. The owner is Gamma Holdings, LLC. The Planning Commission recommended the future land use change 5-3 and the rezoning 5-4. Flagpole identifies the project as Denver-based Cardinal Group Investment Management's student apartment complex plus townhomes, with 465 bedrooms and 211 parking spaces under an inclusionary density bonus. Open items include creek restoration permits, fire access, a sewer line and Reese Street Historic District review. The agenda itself gives no unit or bed count and no staff recommendation.

stories.headline: Auburn Staff Will Seek Extension of Downtown Multifamily and Private Dorm Moratorium
stories.text: Auburn City Manager Megan McGowen Crouch told council on Oct. 20 that staff will recommend extending the moratorium on certain multifamily and private dormitory projects in the Urban Core and Urban Neighborhood-West districts. The moratorium was adopted Nov. 18, 2025 and expires Nov. 30 unless extended. Stormwater review and policy changes need another five to six months; sewer modeling is due late November with a final report in early January; Kimley-Horn is studying traffic. Zoning density recommendations, including letting small parcels redevelop without assembly, could take four to six months, with final amendments possibly running into spring 2027. The length of the proposed extension was not stated.

stories.headline: University Temple Church Drops 933-Bed U District Towers With American Campus
stories.text: University Temple United Methodist Church is cancelling the permits for its 933-bed student housing redevelopment with American Campus Communities, eight years after agreeing to trade its century-old sanctuary for a pair of student towers. The cleared, upzoned corner beside the University of Washington, tagged 1415 NE 43rd St., is left with no partner and no plan. The article is paywalled beyond its summary, so the reason for the cancellation and the site's next step were not available.

stories.headline: Charlottesville Council Takes Up Special Exceptions for West Main Student Building
stories.text: Charlottesville City Council has a special exception permit for 835, 843 and 847 West Main St. (PL-26-0126) on its Nov. 2 agenda, placed on consent in the packet text. Charlottesville Community Engagement describes the request as special exceptions for a student housing building at 843 West Main and reports the Planning Commission recommended approval Oct. 13 with no conditions. The agenda gives no applicant, unit count or list of exceptions, and the council result was not yet posted.

stories.headline: South Oakland Pipeline: Caroline Pre-Leases From $1,390, Boulevard Flats Opens in December
stories.text: Walnut Capital's The Caroline, a 160-unit building on McKee Place, is pre-leasing for 2027-28 with three-bedroom rents advertised from $1,390 per person. 3 Rivers Living's Boulevard Flats at Ward Street and Boulevard of the Allies opens in December with one-bedrooms from $2,195. Trinitas said pricing for Atmosphere, its 326-unit Halket Street project due summer 2028, will be set when pre-leasing begins next fall, and confirmed it will participate in inclusionary zoning. OPDC's Andrea Boykowycz said Pitt enrollment is growing faster than new supply. Boulevard Flats' unit and bed count were not stated.

stories.headline: Subtext and FrontRange Open 697-Bed VERVE Columbia
stories.text: Subtext and FrontRange Capital opened VERVE Columbia, 697 beds in 223 units over four stories at 450 Blossom St., about two blocks from USC. CIBC arranged construction financing through a syndication; W.M. Jordan Co. built it. A second Subtext project is under construction at 931 Senate St.

stories.headline: Rambler College Park North Targets Fall 2027
stories.text: Rambler College Park North, nearly 300 units from studios to five-bedrooms at 8145 Baltimore Ave., has been under construction since January on the former Campus Village Shoppes site, about a four-minute walk from UMD's north campus. It is set to open for 2027-28.

stories.headline: Athens Weighs 130-Foot Downtown Height Limit
stories.text: A text change would raise C-D heights from 100 to 130 feet and C-G from 65 to 95 feet, except next to single-family areas. Commissioners asked for more time Oct. 20. Since 2022, developers paid $9.6 million in lieu while only five on-site affordable bedrooms were approved. No vote date set.

stories.headline: Ann Arbor Orders Denser Zoning Near Central Campus
stories.text: Council on Oct. 19 directed the Planning Commission to draft zoning amendments allowing more housing density south and east of downtown and U-M's Central Campus, in line with the new comprehensive plan. Vote tally and timeline not stated.

stories.headline: Northmarq Places $24M Loan on 166-Bed Berkeley Project
stories.text: Northmarq arranged $24 million in construction financing for 2372 Ellsworth St., 166 beds in 49 units at Ellsworth and Channing Way near UC Berkeley, for an undisclosed borrower. Derived: about $145,000 of loan per bed.

stories.headline: Fountain's 319-Bedroom Lawrence Duplex Project Fences Up
stories.text: Fencing went up Oct. 22 at 2300 Crestline Drive, where Fountain Residential Partners plans 57 duplexes and six homes with 319 bedrooms. The 2021 approval stalled in a church lawsuit that the developer and city won on appeal.

stories.headline: Williams Village II Lists 427 Units on Baseline
stories.text: George Williams LLLP plans five buildings with 427 units at 2952 Baseline Road in Boulder, 122 of them student-oriented apartments from studios to six-bedrooms, plus 58,365 SF of commercial space.

stories.headline: Xavier and Strategic Facility Partners Buy 608-Bed Norwood Community for $73.1 Million
stories.text: Strategic Facility Partners, a Columbus-based nonprofit, acquired a 608-bed mixed-use student housing community next to Xavier University's campus in Norwood, Ohio, for $73.1 million in partnership with Xavier. The purchase is bond-financed, keeping it off the university's balance sheet. The partners plan a $20 million rehabilitation and will fold the property into Xavier's housing system. It is about 65 percent occupied. Xavier's incoming freshman class of about 920 is roughly a third larger than last year's. Derived: about $120,000 per bed at purchase, or about $153,000 per bed including the planned rehab. The asset serves Xavier, not the University of Cincinnati; distance to UC's campus was not stated. The item comes from a Student Housing Daily recap of Cincinnati Business Courier reporting dated Oct. 16. Norwood, Ohio - Xavier University Beds 608 Price $73.1M Per bed (derived) ~$120K Planned rehab $20M Occupancy ~65% Buyer / structure SFP with Xavier / bonds

stories.headline: Article Student Living Buys 280-Bed Signature Apartments in Lexington
stories.text: Article Student Living acquired Signature Apartments, a 280-bed community near the University of Kentucky campus delivered in 2024 with one-, two- and four-bedroom units. Seller and terms were not released.

stories.headline: Redstone Sells 264-Bed Orchard Corners in Lawrence
stories.text: Redstone Residential sold Orchard Corners and Suites, 139 units and 264 beds serving KU, with Berkadia representing the seller. Buyer and price were not disclosed.

stories.headline: JLL Lists 195-Bed HERE Minneapolis
stories.text: HERE Minneapolis at 2813 4th St. SE, 169 units and 195 beds built in 2020 near the University of Minnesota, is listed for sale with JLL. Not a closed trade; asking price and seller not stated.

stories.headline: 24-Unit Brighton Building Trades for $8.875M
stories.text: 15 Euston Road, a 1962 four-story building with 24 units, sold from a private family to a partnership through Marcus and Millichap. Derived: about $370,000 per unit. Conventional multifamily near BC and BU.

stories.headline: UT Trustees Approve Phase Three of Knoxville Housing P3: Nearly 600 Beds by Fall 2028
stories.text: The University of Tennessee Board of Trustees approved phase three of UT Knoxville's on-campus student housing public-private partnership: an eight-floor residence hall of nearly 600 beds on the south side of Caledonia Avenue, next to Presidential Court, expected to open in fall 2028. Phase three also includes demolition of Reese Hall and North and South Carrick Halls. A fourth phase, two more halls adding 980 beds, is expected to go to the board in 2027. The release did not name the private partner, the project cost or the beds lost to the three demolitions, so the net bed gain from phase three cannot be calculated from this source. UT Knoxville housing P3 Phase 3 beds / floors ~600 / 8 Site S. side of Caledonia Ave. Opening Fall 2028 Demolitions Reese, N. and S. Carrick Phase 4 980 beds; board 2027 Partner / cost Not stated

stories.headline: Mizzou Still Weighing On-Campus Housing, Hotel in Land Development Push
stories.text: UM System President Mun Choi told the faculty council Oct. 22 that MU remains in the discussion phase on commercial development of university land: an entertainment district, a hotel near Memorial Stadium and student housing on university property. No selections have been made. The bid portal closed Jan. 9 with eight sites in three zones, and proposals may not require MU capital or MU-issued or underwritten bonds. Undergraduate enrollment is 29,500 (up 500), with 6,050 freshmen.

stories.headline: UK Enrollment Growth Slows to 3% as Lexington Housing Fight Widens
stories.text: UK enrolled about 39,541 students this fall, up 3 percent and the smallest gain in at least four years; VP Kirsten Turner said limited housing and infrastructure held enrollment steady. Kirwan-Blanding Hall, UK's first new dorm in nine years, opened this summer, and UK says it has added more than 7,500 beds in 15 years. The Up Campus plan the planning commission rejected last week was a 751-bed complex with $1,200 to $1,700 rents and no on-site parking for about 80 percent of residents.

stories.headline: UW-Madison Headcount at 50,595
stories.text: Tenth-day fall 2026 headcount at UW-Madison is 50,595. Systemwide enrollment fell 0.7 percent to 164,579, driven by a 1,134-student drop in international enrollment.

stories.headline: College Park Points to Discovery District as Route 1 Fills
stories.text: Mayor Fazlul Kabir called Route 1 north of campus saturated and named the Discovery District on campus's east edge for future housing. Prince George's County, not the city, holds zoning authority.

stories.headline: California's 2027 Laws Add Student Housing Density Bonus, UC/CSU CEQA Exemption
stories.text: AB 2480 creates a stackable density bonus for qualifying student housing in campus development zones; AB 1732 extends the CEQA exemption to UC, CSU and community college housing through 2037. Statewide, not campus-specific.

stories.headline: Wake Forest Plans 6,000 Students by 2030, Collins Hall to Come Down
stories.text: The campus space plan targets 6,000 students by 2030, up from 5,500. Babcock is offline until January 2027 and Collins Hall comes down next summer, leaving upperclassmen on Deacon Place or off-campus partners.

stories.headline: State Filing Puts a 30-Story, 300-Unit Student Tower at 2307 Rio Grande, $97.3 Million, 2028 Delivery
stories.text: A Texas Department of Licensing and Regulation registration filed Oct. 23 describes a 30-story student housing tower at 2305-2309 Rio Grande St. in Austin's West Campus. Registration TABS2027004314 lists 300 student housing units, 466,000 square feet, three levels of below-grade parking and two above grade, and an estimated cost of $97,345,948. The owner is 2307 Rio Grande, LLC, and Rhode Partners is the design firm. Projected start is Feb. 1, 2027, with completion July 14, 2028. The state filing is not a city approval. The related city site plan cases, filed July 8, 2025 and Aug. 19, 2026 under the name Ventnor Avenue, remain In Review, and no building permit has been issued. Earlier reporting put the project at 219 units; the TDLR filing says 300, and the difference has not been explained. The neighboring Atlantic Avenue tower at 2301 Rio Grande (212 units in earlier reports) is also In Review, with no TDLR filing yet. Derived: about $209 per square foot and $324,000 per unit of estimated construction cost. Bed count was not disclosed. A July 2028 completion would target the 2028-29 leasing year if the city review closes on the filing's schedule. 2307 Rio Grande St. - West Campus Stories / units 30 / 300 (beds not stated) Gross SF 466,000 Est. cost (TDLR) $97,345,948 Cost per SF / unit (derived) ~$209 / ~$324K Owner / design 2307 Rio Grande, LLC / Rhode Partners Schedule (TDLR) Start 2/1/27; done 7/14/28 City status Site plans In Review; no permit

stories.headline: Lexington Planners Recommend Denial of Up Campus's 10-Story Tower on East High Street
stories.text: Lexington's planning commission on Oct. 22 voted against Up Campus Student Living's rezoning for a 10-story student apartment building on East High Street in the Aylesford neighborhood, after hours of public comment. WKYT reported the vote as 5-0 with one abstention and the project at 225 units. LEX18 described it as a unanimous recommendation of denial, and the Urban County Council makes the final decision. Up Campus attorney Branden Gross told the commission that UK's student population has grown by 7,800 over the last five years and that the university houses only about 20 percent of students. Opponents cited the scale of the building, neighborhood character, loss of historic buildings, traffic and affordability. City studies cited in the coverage point to a possible shortage of nearly 30,000 housing units within four years. Read-through: the commission's action is a recommendation, not a final denial. The council hearing date was not reported. Bed count and unit mix were not disclosed. The same day, council gave final approval to a six-story condominium project also in the Aylesford area (see brief below). Up Campus - East High St., Lexington Height / units 10 stories / 225 units (WKYT) Beds Not disclosed Planning commission Denial recommended 10/22 (5-0, 1 abst.) Final authority Urban County Council (date TBD) Developer claim +7,800 students in 5 yrs; UK houses ~20%

stories.headline: Columbia Council Votes Down 720-Bedroom Retreat at Columbia, 5-1
stories.text: Columbia's City Council on Oct. 5 rejected the rezoning of 32.7 acres off Rock Quarry Road and Grindstone Parkway for The Retreat at Columbia, a student-oriented multifamily plan. The request was an A to PD rezoning for up to 204 units, with the plan shown at about 194 units and 720 bedrooms. The vote failed 5-1, with Ward 1's Valerie Carroll the only yes and Ward 6's Betsy Peters not voting. The planning commission had recommended denial over Rock Quarry Road safety, the scenic overlay and traffic, after lacking the votes in June to recommend it. Access was planned through a new Retreat Way with right-turn-only movement onto Rock Quarry. The owner is listed as Grindstone Acres, represented by Crockett Engineering. Derived: about 3.7 bedrooms per unit.

stories.headline: INTRO Columbus Tops Out at 13 Stories; Mass Timber Framed the Upper 12 in 16 Weeks
stories.text: Harbor Bay Ventures' INTRO Columbus, a 13-story student housing tower at 1497 N. High St., has reached full height, according to Columbus Business First. Construction started about a year ago and the building topped out in early September. A crew of six to eight workers built the top 12 stories in about 16 weeks using mass timber. It is described as the tallest building on High Street north of downtown. Earlier trade coverage, outside this edition's window, put the project at 186 units, 493 beds and 242,000 square feet, with completion expected in summer 2027. DLR Group is the architect and Elford Construction the general contractor. Derived: about 2.65 beds per unit and 491 square feet per bed. The Business First article is paywalled; details come from the excerpt posted on UrbanOhio. INTRO Columbus - 1497 N. High St. Developer Harbor Bay Ventures Stories / structure 13 / top 12 floors mass timber Units / beds (prior reports) 186 / 493 Gross SF (prior reports) 242,000 SF per bed (derived) ~491 Status Topped out; delivery summer 2027

stories.headline: New Site Plan Filings on Acton School Lot Follow 381-Unit PUD on East Riverside
stories.text: Two site plan filings have landed on the 2.6-acre Acton School lot at 1404 E. Riverside Dr., about 500 feet east of I-35. An Aug. 20 revision to the approved multifamily site plan SP-2021-0451C, listed by the city as Modera Town Lake, has been in review since Oct. 14. An Oct. 22 extension of a previously approved site plan was filed by Drenner Group and shows intake pending. Council approved PUD C814-2025-0111 on July 23, allowing about 381 apartments (15 affordable on site) at up to 180 feet, versus 222 units under the prior approved plan. Neither new record lists a unit count or names a builder. The article notes Mill Creek was copied on a PUD letter; that link is unconfirmed. Distance to the UT campus was not stated, and the project is not marketed as student housing.

stories.headline: GMH's Dean II Rezoning Heads to Second Reading, Adding a Tenth Lot on South Fifth
stories.text: Ann Arbor City Council has The Dean II on its agenda for second reading (ORD-26-27, file 26-1519). The ordinance would rezone 0.17 acres at 548 S. Fifth Ave. from R4C multiple-family to D1 Downtown Core, and a companion item approves The Dean II area plan. Petitioner GMH Communities would add the parcel as a tenth lot, growing the site from 41,461 to 49,060 square feet for a high-rise apartment building one story shorter than the original 16-story Dean plan. City Planning Commission recommended approval 7-0 on Aug. 18. Units and beds are not stated in the record, and the council result was not yet available. Derived: the added parcel enlarges the site by about 7,600 square feet.
stories.source: City of Ann Arbor City Council (Legistar)

stories.headline: Eugene Briefing Tallies 2,136 Bedrooms Across Three Near-Campus Towers
stories.text: A Eugene City Council work session reviewed the near-campus pipeline. The Ellis, at 780 E. 13th Ave., is 14 stories with 304 units and 682 bedrooms and is nearing completion. Chapter Alder, at 811 E. 13th Ave., is 15 stories with 133 units and 491 bedrooms and is under construction for fall 2027 move-in. The Mark Building One, five stories with 262 units and 963 bedrooms on the former PeaceHealth University District site, is slated for summer 2028, per city business liaison Michael Bradley. Building Two has not started. Derived: 2,136 bedrooms across the three projects, with deliveries running from now through summer 2028. Bedrooms per unit run about 2.2 at The Ellis and 3.7 at both Chapter Alder and The Mark. Eugene Near-Campus Pipeline The Ellis (14 st.) 304 units / 682 BR; nearing completion Chapter Alder (15 st.) 133 units / 491 BR; fall 2027 The Mark Bldg. One (5 st.) 262 units / 963 BR; summer 2028 Total (derived) 699 units / 2,136 BR

stories.headline: Evanston's 26-Story, 360-Unit 900 Clark Goes to Committee and Council Today
stories.text: CSP Evanston Land's 900 Clark St. proposal, a 26-story, roughly 298-foot tower with 360 rental units (72 affordable), is scheduled for Planning & Development Committee review and introduction at City Council on Oct. 26. It needs a height allowance in the Research Park district, where the standard maximum is 150 feet. The Land Use Commission recommended approval 4-1 on Sept. 23. The plan includes about 2,484 square feet of ground-floor commercial and 112 off-site spaces in the Maple Avenue garage. The article names Northwestern graduate students and employees among likely renters; distance to campus was not stated. A final vote could come Nov. 9 per a separate report whose date could not be confirmed. Derived: 20 percent of units affordable.

stories.headline: Madison Adopts 578-Unit Westfield Road Rezoning
stories.text: Madison's Common Council on Oct. 20 unanimously adopted the rezoning and CSM for 301 S. Westfield Rd. (owner RFA Asset Management): three five-story buildings with 257, 138 and 183 units, about 1,960 sf of commercial, under CC-T and a TOD overlay. Outside the campus area; distance not verified.

stories.headline: Council Approves Cowgill's Six-Story Condo Rezoning on East Main
stories.text: Lexington's council gave final approval Oct. 22 to Cowgill Development's P-1 to B-2A conditional rezoning at 512 and 518 E. Main St. (0.509 net acres): a six-story, 16-unit owner-occupied condominium building plus a one-story commercial building. The planning commission had recommended approval 7-1. Not student housing.

stories.headline: College Station Floats Middle-Housing Rezoning; Neighbors Warn of 'Mini Dorms'
stories.text: College Station is weighing a city-initiated middle-housing rezoning (duplexes, townhomes) and held an input meeting Oct. 20. A neighborhood association officer warned it would bring '6-6 mini dorms.' Staff say homeowners decide whether their area is rezoned. No council vote yet.

stories.headline: Nashville Policy Would Bar Dorms Next to Vanderbilt Innovation SP
stories.text: Metro Planning's Oct. 22 agenda carried a supplemental policy for about 62 acres along 31st and 32nd avenues and Blakemore beside the Vanderbilt campus that deems dormitories, Greek housing and higher-education uses not appropriate. Staff recommended approval after three deferrals; the outcome was not reported.

stories.headline: Midtown East Subdistrict Would Set 15-Story Base Near Music Row
stories.text: A Downtown Code text amendment would create a Midtown East subdistrict over the Music Row North area at 15 stories and 5.0 FAR, with bonus height tools and an attainable-housing bonus to come. It was deferred to the Nov. 12 commission; council hearing expected Dec. 1. Distance to campus not stated.

stories.headline: McGrath's 736-Bed Wyatt Hits 100 Percent Occupancy in Lubbock
stories.text: McGrath Real Estate completed lease-up of The Wyatt, a 736-bed project near Texas Tech, now 100 percent occupied. It was fully preleased for 2026 by May and is more than 30 percent preleased for fall 2027.

stories.headline: Yardi: FSU, UCF and South Carolina Absorbed New Beds Best
stories.text: Yardi Matrix's Tyson Huebner said Florida State, UCF and South Carolina absorbed new deliveries more successfully than other supply-heavy markets, while Purdue, Arizona State and NC State saw rent declines. Yardi 200 preleasing hit 93 percent in August; leasing-season rent growth averaged 1.1 percent.

stories.headline: Business First: High-Rises Remake the University District
stories.text: Columbus Business First traces the University District's shift to luxury high-rises to longtime local owners selling, density-friendly zoning and OSU enrollment growth. The portfolio sale it references is not named in the excerpt. Paywalled; details from an UrbanOhio excerpt.

stories.headline: University of Cincinnati Cleared to Buy 293 Off-Campus Beds for $33.2 Million
stories.text: The University of Cincinnati has state approval to buy 293 student housing beds near its Uptown campus for $33.2 million from VP4 LLC and Aristo Properties II BV. The properties sit in a main student housing corridor next to campus. Pipeline research notes identify them as 101 E. Corry St. and 130 W.H. Taft Rd., with 127 units. The state approval is dated Sept. 16; this is in-window trade coverage of that approval, and a closing date was not reported. Derived: about $113,000 per bed and 2.3 beds per unit. Read-through: a university buying existing private beds adjacent to campus removes those beds from the competitive off-campus supply. UC Uptown Acquisition Beds / units 293 / 127 (per research notes) Price $33.2M Per bed (derived) ~$113,300 Sellers VP4 LLC; Aristo Properties II BV Status State approval 9/16; close not reported

stories.headline: Pearlmark Lends $81 Million on Empira's 160-Unit Aurelian in Coral Gables
stories.text: Empira Group secured an $81 million construction loan from Pearlmark for Aurelian, a 12-story, 160-unit multifamily building on 1.2 acres at 114 Calabria Ave. in Coral Gables. CBRE arranged the financing. Empira paid $18 million for the site in 2025 and has broken ground; completion is expected in 2028. Derived: about $506,000 of loan per unit and $112,500 of land per unit. Conventional multifamily; distance to campus not stated.

stories.headline: Foreclosure Auction Set for 30-Unit Selkirk Place Near Cleveland Circle
stories.text: A lender will auction the 30-unit Selkirk Place Apartments in Brighton at 10 a.m. Oct. 28. Blackstar Capital paid $12.8 million in 2022; the city assesses it at $7.24 million (derived: about 43 percent below the 2022 price).

stories.headline: WVU Buys Former Sorority House on University Avenue
stories.text: WVU closed Oct. 5 on the 11,492-sf former sorority house at 1493 University Ave. after a recovery-housing buyer's contract fell through on zoning denials. Price and plans were not disclosed.

stories.headline: Arete Closes on South Bryan Lot for Eight Units
stories.text: Arete Development Partners closed Sept. 24 on land at 1809 S. College Ave. in Bryan for an eight-unit apartment complex. Price, beds, timeline and target tenants were not stated.

stories.headline: UCF Shortlists ACC, Greystar, Pinnacle and RISE for 61-Acre Mixed-Use P3
stories.text: UCF posted its shortlist for ITN No. 2026-01NC, Developer for University Mixed Use P3, on Oct. 20, the day its evaluation committee met. Four of the 10 proposers advance to Stage II: American Campus Communities, Greystar (GS Development Services Northeast), Pinnacle Real Estate Development Group and RISE Knights. The posting period ran through 1:30 p.m. Oct. 23, and protests are governed by Board of Governors regulations 18.002 and 18.003. Six proposers were cut: Capstone Development Partners, Development Ventures Group, Gilbane Development, Maslow's Campus Communities, Regency Centers and Servitas. The P3 covers three UCF sites totaling 61.4 acres with Alafaya Trail frontage, for student housing, workforce housing and ground-floor retail. Stage II asks shortlisted firms for project concepts. Read-through: all four finalists are student housing developers or operators, and the one retail REIT in the field (Regency) did not advance. Bed targets, ground lease terms and the Stage II schedule have not been published. UCF ITN 2026-01NC - Shortlist Sites 3 sites, 61.4 ac, Alafaya Trail Uses Student + workforce housing, retail Proposers / shortlisted 10 / 4 Shortlist ACC; Greystar; Pinnacle; RISE Posted Oct. 20 (protest window to Oct. 23) Beds / lease terms Not published

stories.headline: Regents Book Lays Out UW-Madison's 1,690-Bed Ground Lease: $1 a Year, 62 Years, $338M GMP
stories.text: Materials for the Universities of Wisconsin Board of Regents' Oct. 19 special meeting detail the terms of the UW-Madison residence hall P3. The resolution authorizes demolition of 72-bed Merit Hall and a ground lease allowing privately owned residence halls at 917-921 W. Dayton St. (1.20 acres, the dining hall site) and 115 N. Mills St. (1.78 acres). The lessee and owner is PRG Badger Properties LLC, chosen from 11 proposals to a May 2026 state RFP. The ground lease runs 62 years at $1 a year from May 1, 2027. The state leases the buildings back under a 30-year triple-net lease with no escalation and a purchase option at year 10 and each year after. The guaranteed maximum price is $337,982,121 ($751.65 per square foot on 450,255 square feet), or $189,467 per bed for about 1,690 beds excluding dining. Base rent is $29.7 million a year, and total projected annual cost is $43.6 million. Occupancy is set for July 1, 2029. Derived: base rent equals about 8.8 percent of GMP. UW-Madison Residence Hall P3 Developer / owner PRG Badger Properties LLC Beds ~1,690 (Merit Hall, 72 beds, razed) GMP $337,982,121 ($751.65/SF) Per bed (excl. dining) $189,467 Ground lease 62 yrs at $1/yr from 5/1/27 Building lease to State 30-yr NNN, 0% esc.; option yr 10+ Base rent / total cost $29.7M / $43.6M per yr Occupancy July 1, 2029
stories.source: Universities of Wisconsin Board of Regents (meeting book)

stories.headline: State Building Commission Approves the $338M Plan; Joint Finance Review Still Ahead
stories.text: The Wisconsin State Building Commission on Oct. 22 approved the nearly $338 million plan for two UW-Madison residence halls and a 400-seat dining hall adding nearly 1,700 beds. University Housing revenues back the partnership, and UW-Madison will manage and operate the halls. Construction is expected to start in summer 2027 for a fall 2029 opening. The university estimates the P3 model delivers about two years sooner and saves about $55 million. The Legislature's Joint Committee on Finance still has to review it. University Housing is running at about 115 percent of design capacity after a record 3,920 Wisconsin-resident first-years this fall.

stories.headline: Clemson Trustees Fund Design of $175M, 560-Bed Johnstone Replacement
stories.text: Clemson's board approved $3.1 million in Phase One design funds for a 185,000-sf, roughly 560-bed first-year complex on the Johnstone Hall site. Construction is planned for January 2028 to July 2030, with Phase Two approval expected June 2027. Derived: about $312,500 per bed.

stories.headline: LSU Triples Upperclass Beds and Moves Selection to November
stories.text: LSU will open East and West Campus apartments to returning students for 2027-28, lifting upperclass beds from about 1,000 to 3,000. Housing selection moves from February to November, ahead of off-campus preleasing.

stories.headline: TCU Opens Two East-Side Upperclass Developments for Fall 2027
stories.text: TCU will open Site C (suites) and Site D (townhomes on 12-month leases) for juniors and seniors in fall 2027, with applications opening Nov. 2 to reach students before they sign off-campus leases. Bed counts not stated.

stories.headline: Bloomington Sets Oct. 28 Hearing on HEA 1001 Zoning Review
stories.text: Bloomington's Plan Commission holds a special hearing Oct. 28 on its UDO under state law HEA 1001, covering density, housing types, setbacks, parking, height and permit timelines. The Common Council has final authority.

stories.headline: 30-Story, 227-Unit Tower Filed for 2008 San Antonio Street Would Tie Icon as West Campus's Tallest
stories.text: A 300-foot, 30-story residential tower with 227 units has been filed for 2008 San Antonio St. in Austin's West Campus. The site plan went in Sept. 28 under case folder 13779590 and shows a status of Intake Pending, with no permit number assigned. Jones|Carter is the applicant, with Justin Cadieux listed as applicant of record. The filing does not name the owner. Travis Central Appraisal District records list an Aydam trust, with a 2026 assessed value of $3.49 million.
