The lot is about 0.31 acres and now holds Lantern Lane, a two-story garden apartment complex built in 1982. At 300 feet the tower would reach the height cap for the Inner West Campus subdistrict of the University Neighborhood Overlay. It would tie Icon at 2200 San Antonio as the tallest building in West Campus. Underwriting read: 227 units on 0.31 acres works out to roughly 730 units per acre, and the assessed value is about $15,400 per proposed unit (both derived; assessed value is not a sale price). The filing as reported does not give a bed count, unit mix, parking, developer or whether the building will be leased by the bed. Intake-pending status means it has not been through site plan review. Timing to delivery cannot be estimated from the filing. 2008 San Antonio St. - West Campus Height / stories 300 ft / 30 Units 227 (beds not stated) Site ~0.31 ac (Lantern Lane, 1982) Units per acre (derived) ~730 Applicant Jones|Carter Owner of record (TCAD) Aydam trust; $3.49M assessed Status Site plan filed 9/28; intake pending

stories.headline: Hub College Station Phase II Needs a 218-Foot Crane Over Northgate; Staff Backs Airport-Height Variance
stories.text: College Station's Zoning Board of Adjustment heard a request for a temporary tower crane that would reach 556 feet above sea level, or 218 feet above ground, to build an eight-story student housing project at 403 Cherry St. in Northgate. The crane would rise 85.4 feet above the Easterwood Airport height limit. The roughly one-third-acre site at College Main and Cherry Street is zoned NG-3 Residential Northgate. Kimley-Horn is the applicant and Core College Station Cherry LLC is the owner. Staff recommended approval. A Texas Department of Licensing and Regulation filing registered Sept. 3 identifies the project as Hub College Station Phase II, owned by Chicago-based Core College Station Cherry LLC. It shows eight stories, 241,584 square feet and an estimated construction cost of $53.6 million, with a start date of Nov. 2, 2026 and completion on June 1, 2028. The building is planned at about 107 feet. Derived: about $222 per square foot of estimated construction cost. A June 2028 completion targets the 2028-29 leasing year. The board's vote was not reported, and units and beds were not disclosed. This item comes from news previews of the hearing, not the city's official agenda, which could not be read. Hub College Station Phase II - 403 Cherry St. Owner Core College Station Cherry LLC Stories / height 8 / ~107 ft Gross SF (TDLR) 241,584 Est. construction cost $53,596,456 Cost per SF (derived) ~$222 Schedule (TDLR) Start 11/2/26; done 6/1/28 Units / beds Not disclosed

stories.headline: Trinitas and Starwood Break Ground on 627-Bed Atmosphere Pittsburgh on Halket Street
stories.text: Trinitas Ventures of Carmel, Ind., broke ground Oct. 13 on Atmosphere Pittsburgh, on the 200 block of Halket Street in Oakland, across from UPMC Magee-Womens Hospital and next to the Pitt campus. Starwood Capital Group is Trinitas' partner. The 12-story building will have 326 apartments and 627 beds, vehicle and bicycle parking and more than 30,000 square feet of clubhouse and amenity space. The cost is put at more than $100 million. About a dozen single-family homes were razed for the site. Completion is expected in summer 2028. Derived: about 1.92 beds per unit and at least $159,000 per bed on the reported cost floor. It is the second Trinitas Atmosphere groundbreaking in this edition, after Norman (below).

stories.headline: 908 Group Breaks Ground on 684-Bed Chapter House UF at 920 SW Depot Avenue
stories.text: 908 Group has broken ground on Chapter House UF, a 684-bed Class A student housing community at 920 SW Depot Ave., next to the University of Florida campus. Batson-Cook Development Company is the development partner, and Pacific Life is providing construction financing. The project has 219 units, more than 9,000 square feet of amenity space and a structured parking garage. It is set to finish the summer before the fall 2028 term. ARCO/Murray is general contractor and Humphreys & Partners Architects is architect. Derived: about 3.12 beds per unit on average (the unit mix was not published). This is the second Pacific Life-financed UF project to start in October, after LV Collective's 659-bed Rambler Gainesville (Edition 21). That brings 1,343 announced beds near UF with fall 2028 deliveries. The pipeline previously reported Liberty Group's co-GP equity in the deal. Loan amount and total cost were not disclosed.

stories.headline: Madison Council Takes Up Student-Affordability Covenant That Unlocks Height for Landmark's 986-Bed Standard on West Gilman
stories.text: The Madison Common Council has a resolution on its Oct. 20 agenda (Item 64, Legistar File 95130) approving a land use restriction agreement for 411-433 W. Gilman St. The developer entity is The Standard at Madison, LLC, and Landmark Properties submitted the land use application (File 90614). The agreement is tied to the Downtown Height Map story bonus, which grants added stories in exchange for affordable units rented to postsecondary students. The project has 986 beds. Under the agreement, 99 beds would rent at a 40 percent discount, applied to two-bedroom units leased to four individuals. That is about 10 percent of beds (derived). The Finance Committee recommended adoption Oct. 12. Underwriting read: this is a template for trading below-market student beds for height. The number of bonus stories gained and the base rent the discount is measured from were not stated.

stories.headline: New York Developers Pitch $170M First Phases of Up-to-500-Unit Hill District Plan, Citing Pitt Housing Crunch
stories.text: JK Equities and Manor Park Ventures hold exclusive negotiation rights with Pittsburgh's Urban Redevelopment Authority to buy 90 vacant, publicly owned parcels on and around Herron Avenue in the Hill District. The four-phase plan calls for up to 500 apartments. The first two phases, which were presented to the URA board earlier in October, are estimated at about $170 million. Phase 1 is a 195-unit building with ground-floor commercial space. Phase 2 is two six-story towers with 60 and 80 units. Council President R. Daniel Lavelle said Oakland's shortage is pushing students into subdivided Hill District homes. No construction timeline, financing or formal approvals have been disclosed. Phases 1-2 total 335 units; whether the $170 million estimate includes the commercial space was not stated.

stories.headline: Lexington Planning Commission Approves 594-Unit White Farm; Up Campus's 225-Unit East High Street Plan Heads a Heavy Oct. 22 Docket
stories.text: On Oct. 8 the Lexington Planning Commission approved the White Farm development plan at 3515 Richmond Road, with 114 townhomes and 480 multifamily units and 14 conditions. The vote was by voice with one abstention, and distance to campus was not stated. Andover Commons (1,240 units at 4200 Todds Road) was postponed to Oct. 22, its third postponement. The Oct. 22 docket includes Up Campus Student Living's 225-unit East High Street project, Ball Homes' 560 units, Andover, Turner Property 4 and Regency Holdings Three, plus downtown zoning and Urban Growth Master Plan text amendments. The Oct. 8 agenda also carried a waiver of Newtown Pike Extension design and access standards covering the Hayman Subdivision (The Standard at Lexington). That outcome was not reported.

stories.headline: Yardi Matrix: ASU Rents Fall 6 Percent, Purdue 8.2 Percent as 31,000 Off-Campus Beds Deliver in 2026
stories.text: Yardi Matrix's October national student housing report shows Arizona State's leasing-season rents down 6 percent, among the weakest results alongside Purdue (-8.2 percent) and NC State (-3.3 percent). Preliminary September occupancy across the Yardi 200 schools was 94.5 percent. An alternative estimate puts it at 92.1 percent. More than 31,000 off-campus bedrooms were delivered in 2026, up 20 percent from 2025. Supply-heavy markets show the pressure. NC State reached 81.3 percent occupancy after 2,195 beds were delivered. UC Berkeley was at 89.7 percent after adding 1,430 beds. On the strong side, Oklahoma State rents rose 11.4 percent to $671 per bed, Louisville 9 percent to $756 and Mississippi State 6.3 percent to $720. Oklahoma, Washington and Virginia Tech were estimated fully occupied in September. Note: these are survey figures, not trades. Yardi Matrix - October 2026 selected markets Yardi 200 Sept. occupancy (prelim.) 94.5% 2026 off-campus deliveries 31,000+ beds (+20% YoY) Purdue / ASU / NC State rent -8.2% / -6.0% / -3.3% Okla. State / Louisville / MSU rent +11.4% / +9.0% / +6.3% NC State occupancy 81.3% (2,195 beds added) UC Berkeley occupancy 89.7% (1,430 beds added)

stories.headline: Champaign Permits Twin Seven-Story Buildings on John Street, Nearly $49M Combined
stories.text: Champaign issued permits to Wells & Wells Construction for new seven-story multifamily buildings at 106 E. John St. ($24.58 million) and 105 E. John St. ($24.14 million), or $48.72 million combined. The permit list does not give unit or bed counts, the developer or the owner, and distance to campus is not stated.

stories.headline: Atmosphere Norman Breaks Ground Next to OU
stories.text: Trinitas Ventures broke ground Oct. 7 on Atmosphere Norman, a seven-story student building at 310 E. Boyd St. on the former Ray Apartments site. Cowen Construction is general contractor. The project has 13,700 square feet of indoor amenities, a rooftop pool and two parking levels with 265 spaces, with units from studios to five bedrooms. Opening is set for summer 2028. Earlier Hoodline coverage put it at 677 beds with Starwood Capital as JV partner.

stories.headline: Clemson Adopts Student Housing District on Second Reading
stories.text: Clemson City Council unanimously approved the second reading of the Student Housing (SH) District text amendment on Oct. 5. The case was listed as 2026-R-04 at the Sept. 8 hearing. The outcome comes from draft minutes that were set for approval Oct. 19. Which parcels will be mapped into the district has not been reported.
stories.source: Clemson City Council (agenda and draft minutes)

stories.headline: Fayetteville Plat Review Weighs 282-Unit Chicago Way Project and Dickson Street Infill
stories.text: Fayetteville's Technical Plat Review Committee took up LSIP-2026-0013 on Oct. 14. That project is 282 multifamily units and 45,000 square feet of commercial space on about 11 acres west of 111 N. Chicago Way, zoned CS, submitted by Blew & Associates and previously tabled. The same agenda carried Flintlock's 33-unit mixed-use building at 215 W. Dickson St. and its 12-unit building west of 355 N. College Ave., plus a multifamily building at 309 S. School Ave. and a rezoning of 104 S. Duncan Ave. from RMF-40 to Urban Neighborhood. Separately, the City Council takes up a 0.19-acre right-of-way vacation on an RMF-24 site near Center Street and Razorback Road on Oct. 20 (VAC-2026-0014). The purpose of that vacation was not stated.

stories.headline: Oberlin Village Rezoning Z-30-26 Would Lift Two-Story Cap; Applicant Cites Student Housing
stories.text: Z-30-26 would rezone 2402-2408 Clark Ave. and 300 Horne St. in Raleigh to RX-3-CU and remove the Oberlin Village NCOD's two-story, 28.7-foot height cap so buildings can reach three stories. According to a DTRaleigh forum post, the applicant's Comprehensive Plan essay states an intent to build student housing, but that use is not a formal condition. Planning Commission review is set for Oct. 20 or Oct. 27 (forum post; not confirmed on an official agenda), and the Historic District Commission meets Nov. 12.
stories.source: DTRaleigh Community (links City of Raleigh case Z-030-26)

stories.headline: Ann Arbor Council Resolution Would Start Zoning Amendments Near Downtown and Central Campus
stories.text: Ann Arbor City Council's Oct. 19 agenda adds File 26-1743, a resolution to start zoning amendments near Downtown and Central Campus, sponsored by Akmon, Cornell, Eyer, Harrison and Taylor. The interim amendment attachment could not be read, so the scope and any effect on residential density are not verified. Separately, the Planning Commission hears a PUD-to-Office rezoning at 709 W. Huron on Oct. 20, with a staff recommendation to approve.

stories.headline: Berkeley Approves 11-Story, 242-Unit 2900 Shattuck, 90 Percent Studios
stories.text: NX Ventures won approval for an 11-story, 125-foot building at 2900-2920 Shattuck Ave. with 242 units: 219 studios, 9 one-bedrooms, 13 two-bedrooms and 1 three-bedroom. Thirty units are affordable, and the project uses state density bonus waivers. It has 13 car and 68 bike spaces, and construction is expected to start early next year. Distance to campus not stated.

stories.headline: BPDA Approves Wu's $31.5M in Tax Breaks; Three of Four Projects Are in Allston-Brighton
stories.text: On Oct. 15 the BPDA board approved an estimated $31.5 million in property tax abatements for four stalled market-rate projects totaling more than 1,400 units. Three are in Allston-Brighton: Nordblom's 333 units at 83 Leo M. Birmingham Pkwy., New England Development's 341-unit Allston Yards building and Hines' 316 units at 22-24 Pratt St. Developers must start construction within 12-15 months. Distance to BC not stated.

stories.headline: 686-Bed Cove at State Street Hits the Market in Baton Rouge
stories.text: The Cove at State Street, a 402-unit, 686-bed student property in Baton Rouge, was listed for sale in Student Housing Daily's Oct. 6 for-sale roundup. The asset has 311,156 square feet on 11 acres. It was built in 1971 and renovated in 2026. Derived: about 1.71 beds per unit and about 454 square feet per bed. The asking price, broker, seller, occupancy and distance to LSU were not stated. The 1971 vintage puts capital-expenditure history and the scope of the 2026 renovation at the center of any diligence. The Cove at State Street - Baton Rouge Units / beds 402 / 686 Building SF / land 311,156 / 11 ac Built / renovated 1971 / 2026 Beds per unit (derived) ~1.71 SF per bed (derived) ~454 Asking price Not stated

stories.headline: 71-Unit Park West Apartments in Westwood Trades for $14.2M, $200K per Unit
stories.text: Park West Apartments at 1441 S. Beverly Glen Blvd. sold for $14.2 million, or $200,000 per unit. The 1953 property has 63 studios and eight one-bedrooms on 0.67 acres in the Westwood submarket. The seller was 1441 S Beverly Glen Investment, LLC, and the buyer was not named. Marcus & Millichap's Michael Sterman cited proximity to UCLA. The property is not marketed as student housing, and distance to campus is not stated.

stories.headline: Three Months On, UC Still Silent on Plans for $50M Westwood Village Buy
stories.text: UC Investments bought at least 15 Westwood Village commercial properties worth about $50 million in July. Chancellor Julio Frenk has said they would be used for classrooms and graduate student housing. UC and UCLA declined to give specific plans. Meanwhile tenants including Urban Outfitters and Corner Bakery have closed, and Aahs! closes Nov. 3.

stories.headline: Ten Developers Chase UCF's 61-Acre Mixed-Use P3; Evaluation Committee Sets Stage II Shortlist Oct. 20
stories.text: The evaluation committee for UCF's ITN No. 2026-01NC, Developer for University Mixed Use P3, meets at 9:30 a.m. Tuesday, Oct. 20, in the Student Union's Charge On Chamber. The committee will score proposals by consensus and pick the proposers who advance to Stage II. Ten firms responded by the Sept. 23 opening: American Campus Communities, Capstone Development Partners, Development Ventures Group, Gilbane Development Company, Greystar, Maslow's Campus Communities, Regency Centers, RISE, Servitas and The Pinnacle Real Estate Development Group. The P3 covers three UCF sites totaling 61.4 acres along Alafaya Trail. Planned uses include student housing, workforce housing and ground-floor retail. Rieth Jones Advisors is development advisor, and CBRE is retail advisor. Read-through: the field mixes student housing specialists (ACC, Capstone, Servitas, Pinnacle, RISE, Greystar) with a shopping-center REIT (Regency Centers) (interpretation: consistent with the retail component in the scope). The size of the Stage II shortlist, the ground lease structure and the bed targets have not been published. The committee is meeting publicly, so its scoring outcome should be available after Tuesday. stories.headline: Morehouse-Spelman P3 Celebrates 793-Bed Den at Eight50 West, Financed With $146.8M in Bonds
stories.text: Atlanta Mayor Andre Dickens and the presidents of Morehouse and Spelman marked the Oct. 15 groundbreaking of The Den at Eight50 West, a 305-unit, 793-bed student housing project at 850 West End Ave. SW. Work actually began July 1. The unit count has been revised from 290 to 305, and all units are affordable. The project serves Morehouse and Spelman, not Georgia Tech; it is filed under the Atlanta market. Madrone Community Development Foundation is the developer. $146.8 million in Development Authority of Fulton County bonds closed July 1, and the deal runs on a 50-year lease with West End Avenue P3 LLC, a Morehouse-Spelman joint venture. A Clark/C.D. Moody JV is building it, with completion expected at the end of 2028. Derived: about $185,000 of bond proceeds per bed (bond amount, not total cost).

stories.headline: UA Housing Master-Leases 1,000+ Off-Campus Beds for Returning Students
stories.text: The University of Arkansas' Best of Both program will offer more than 1,000 off-campus beds to returning and transfer students for 2027-28, with contracting opening at 10 a.m. Nov. 17. The beds are at the Atmosphere, the Locale and the Marshall (four-bedroom units), with limited availability at the Cardinal and Duncan Avenue Apartments. On-campus priority goes to first-year students. Room selection runs in late February 2027, and rates will be set at the UA System board's late-May meeting. Underwriting read: university master leases take a large block of off-campus demand away from the open market. The lease terms were not disclosed.

stories.headline: Arkansas Posts Official Fall 2026 Enrollment of 33,990
stories.text: The University of Arkansas posted official fall 2026 enrollment of 33,990 on Oct. 14, with first-year retention of 85.81 percent and a six-year graduation rate of 73.07 percent. UA Quick Facts lists 29,207 undergraduates and 4,388 graduate students, which totals 33,595. The 395-student gap to the headline figure is not explained in the source. No prior-year figure was provided for comparison.
stories.source: UA Office of Strategic Analytics & Insights

stories.headline: TCU Enrollment Now About 64 Percent Women
stories.text: Institutional Research data cited by TCU 360 shows women at about 64 percent of TCU's fall 2026 student body, up from 58 percent five years ago. Some sorority new-member classes top 100, while fraternity pledge classes run 30 to 40. That has potential implications for unit-mix and roommate-matching assumptions. Total enrollment was not given.

stories.headline: Cardinal Group Wins Narrow Planning Commission Nod for 425-Bedroom Block at 660 West Broad, Pushing Athens' Student Corridor West
stories.text: Denver-based Cardinal Group is seeking to rezone the block bounded by West Broad, Finley, Reese and Pope streets in Athens to C-D (commercial-downtown) and change the future land use map. The plan is a six-story building with 181 units and 425 bedrooms, plus eight five-bedroom townhouses. The Athens-Clarke County Planning Commission narrowly voted at its Oct. 1 meeting to recommend approval to the Mayor and Commission. Staff had recommended RM-3 multifamily zoning instead. Cardinal has already given ground to get there. It dropped a seventh story and moved parking underground, with 211 spaces for 465 residents. It also offered Tanyard Creek restoration and a $2.2 million payment to the county's affordable housing trust fund. Army Corps of Engineers and Georgia EPD stream permits are still needed, as is a Historic Preservation Commission sign-off. Flagpole notes that other student apartment buildings already sit west of Pulaski Street. The article does not give the exact distance to campus. Underwriting read: the program works out to about 2.35 bedrooms per unit in the main building and about 0.45 parking spaces per resident (both derived). A $2.2 million trust-fund payment is a material entitlement cost, and it is now a reference point for later downtown-edge rezonings in Athens. Unit mix, rents, capital stack, construction cost and the Mayor and Commission hearing date have not been reported. Cardinal Group - 660 West Broad, Athens Developer Cardinal Group (Denver) Request C-D rezoning + FLUM change Staff position Recommended RM-3 instead Program 6 stories; 181 units / 425 BR Townhouses 8 five-bedroom Parking 211 underground (465 residents) Affordable housing payment $2.2M PC vote Narrow approval rec., Oct. 1 Next Mayor & Commission (date TBD)

stories.headline: LV Collective and Peninsula Unveil 659-Bed Rambler Gainesville on SW Eighth Street, Financed by Pacific Life
stories.text: LV Collective and Peninsula Investments announced Rambler Gainesville, a seven-story student housing mid-rise at 420 SW Eighth St. near the University of Florida. The building has 240 units and 659 beds in 423,060 square feet, with floor plans from studios to five bedrooms. Sitework began in April, and opening is set for fall 2028. Pacific Life is providing construction financing, and Juneau Construction Co. is general contractor. Neither the loan amount nor the total development cost was disclosed. This is LV Collective's second UF-area project after Sweetwater, completed in 2023, and its second Rambler-branded announcement in recent weeks after Rambler College Park North in Maryland (covered in Edition 19). Derived metrics: about 2.75 beds per unit and roughly 640 gross square feet per bed. A fall 2028 delivery puts the project into the 2028-29 leasing cycle. Rents and parking count were not reported. stories.headline: LV Collective's Eight-Story West Main Student Building Goes to Charlottesville Planning Commission Tuesday as By-Right Debate Simmers
stories.text: The Charlottesville Planning Commission will take up five special exception permits on Tuesday, Oct. 13, for LV Collective's planned eight-story student housing building at 843 West Main St. The project has 182 residential units and a cafe on a parking lot between West Main and the Charlottesville Redevelopment and Housing Authority's Westhaven public housing community, with a public plaza between the building and a redeveloped Westhaven. The requested exceptions include reductions to ground-story height and 'active depth' requirements on part of the site. Under the 2024 Development Code, special exceptions need a public meeting but no public hearing. The code eliminated the old special use permit route for added height and density. Opposition is shifting to process. During public comment at the Oct. 5 City Council meeting, an MSC Apartments resident opposed proposals to restore case-by-case Council approval for large projects, which aim to stop the by-right West Main building. The same resident said his landlord did not raise rent for next year and attributed that to competition from VERVE and Blume on Ivy, both under construction. Bed count, unit mix and timing for 843 West Main have not been reported.

stories.headline: Brighton Developers Seeks RN-6 Upzoning on Fort Sanders Site Within 500 Feet of UT; Staff Cites Enrollment Growth
stories.text: The Knoxville-Knox County Planning Commission's October agenda includes item 30 (cases 10-I-26-RZ, 10-C-26-SP and 10-C-26-PA), a request to rezone about 1.04 acres at 1625 Clinch Ave. and 1634 Laurel Ave. in Fort Sanders from RN-5/NC to RN-6 multifamily/NC. Brighton Developers LLC is the owner and Heyoh Architecture is the applicant. Companion sector plan and one-year plan amendments would change the designation from MDR to MDR/O. The site, west of Sixteenth Street, now holds multifamily housing and a parking lot. Staff recommends approval and cites UT enrollment growth. The staff report places the site within 500 feet of campus. No project or unit count is in the filing, and the case page did not show the commission's vote. If the case is approved, City Council readings are set for Nov. 10 and Nov. 24.

stories.headline: Ann Arbor Advances Two Large Residential Projects: The Dean II Lot Rezoning for a ~240-Unit, 15-Story Tower, and a $29.8M Brownfield Plan at University Inn
stories.text: Ann Arbor City Council gave first reading on Oct. 5 to an ordinance (File 26-1519) rezoning 0.17 acres at 548 S. Fifth Ave. from R4C to D1 Downtown Core. The lot would be folded into the adjacent The Dean site, growing it from 41,461 to 49,060 square feet for 'a 15-story residential building with approximately 240 apartments.' The memo does not name the applicant. Planning Commission recommended approval 7-0 on Aug. 18, and second reading is set for Nov. 5. On the same night, Council passed on consent the development agreement for 2424 E. Stadium Blvd. (University Inn). Developer Stadium Investors 1 LLC plans a six-story, 295-apartment building plus 12 townhomes, for 307 units, with 417 vehicle and 156 bicycle spaces and a $177,375 park contribution. A companion Brownfield Plan goes to a public hearing Oct. 19. It would reimburse $29,763,724 in eligible costs to the developer, plus $5.5 million for city intersection work, through about 17 years of tax capture, against about $135.4 million of private investment. Derived: about $441,000 of private investment per unit, with the reimbursement equal to about 22 percent of private investment. Distance to campus was not verified for either site.

stories.headline: College Station Council Weighs a Northgate Overlay That Would Cap Building Heights Across From Texas A&M
stories.text: At an Oct. 8 workshop, College Station City Council discussed a possible overlay district that would limit building height in Northgate. The area is generally bounded by First Street, Lodge Street, University Drive and Church Avenue, directly across University Drive from campus. Staff presented results from property-owner engagement that Council ordered in June. Community Impact reports that staff were also directed to develop a grants and incentives program to test the market. No height limit was proposed and no vote was taken. For developers holding or pursuing Northgate sites, a height overlay is the main entitlement risk to watch. Council's next regular meeting is Oct. 22. The official agenda could not be read, so this account relies on the city's live meeting blog and Community Impact's coverage.
stories.source: City of College Station (Live From City Hall)

stories.headline: Salt Lake Student Pipeline Builds Despite Studio Glut: Kayne Anderson Takes Over Trolley Square Site, Landmark Eyes Rowland Hall Campus
stories.text: Building Salt Lake's pipeline review counts several new purpose-built student projects near the University of Utah. Cole West's Chapter SLC on 400 South is under construction with nearly 700 beds in 252 units next to a TRAX Red Line stop, with completion due by June 2028. Kip Paul of Cushman & Wakefield said the long-planned site north of Trolley Square at 500 South and 700 East will be student housing, now handled by Kayne Anderson rather than Alta Terra. He also said Landmark Properties will develop the Rowland Hall 9th & 9th campus as off-campus student housing. Yugo The Summit, formerly The Landing/Charlston, was recently converted to student use. Supply is building on campus too. Trailhead (American Campus Communities) added more than 1,400 beds and Ivory University House more than 600 apartments. The university reported 86 percent on-campus occupancy, with just over 900 beds available as of August, and cited heavy apartment concessions in the market. That is a caution for lease-up underwriting on 2028 deliveries.

stories.headline: Mansfield PZC Rejects 8-1 Plan to Triple Carriage House to 198 Units Near UConn, Citing Well Water
stories.text: Mansfield's Planning and Zoning Commission voted 8-1 on Oct. 5 to deny SR UConn Owner LLC's Master Development Plan and its zone change to a Planned Housing Design District at Carriage House Drive. The plan would have redeveloped Carriage House Apartments from 65 to 198 units, including several four-bedroom units. Commissioners cited concerns about the neighborhood's well-water supply. The complex has a UConn shuttle stop and is within walking distance of campus. The applicant must file a new application to proceed. The Mansfield Environmental Trust is working on a request for a moratorium on PHDD applications. If adopted, a moratorium would close the zoning path this project used. Edition 6 (June 22) reported the $14.15 million sale of a 65-unit Carriage House Townhomes complex at 183 Huntington Lodge Rd. The Dispatch has not confirmed whether that is the same property.

stories.headline: Subtext Opens 626-Bed VERVE Orlando 0.2 Miles From UCF
stories.text: Subtext opened VERVE Orlando at 3133 N. Alafaya Trail: five stories, 200 units, 626 beds and 446,078 square feet about 0.2 miles from UCF. It was developed with FrontRange Capital Partners and Nuveen Real Estate and financed by Simmons Bank. First residents moved in in August 2026. It is Subtext's first delivered student housing community in Florida. Disclosure: Subtext publishes The Dispatch.

stories.headline: Uncommon Revises 12-Story, 88-Unit Strathmore Tower in Westwood
stories.text: Uncommon is taking an updated design for a 12-story, roughly 168-foot building with 88 apartments and 43 parking spaces at 11027-11045 W. Strathmore Dr. to the Westwood Design Review Board. The project uses stacked state density bonuses with a 15 percent moderate-income set-aside. Urbanize LA places it alongside Landmark Properties' similar 12-story Landfair Ave. proposal and UCLA's 901 Levering Ave. high-rise dorm.

stories.headline: Eastern Sunrise Seeks Phased Permit for $18M, 155-Room Student Building on The Ave
stories.text: Eastern Sunrise is seeking a phased permit so it can start demolition early on a fire-damaged University District site, ahead of a six-story, 155-room student housing project on University Way NE. The project is reported at $18 million, about $116,000 per room (derived). Article tags reference 4224 and 4234 University Way NE, Jackson Main Architecture and Mortenson. The source is paywalled beyond its summary.

stories.headline: Demolition Starts on Williams Village II Site Next to CU Dorms
stories.text: The Williams family has begun demolishing the Dark Horse bar and nearby buildings on Baseline Road to clear the site for Williams Village II at 2952 Baseline, next to CU Boulder's Williams Village dorms. The plan, approved by Council in November 2025, calls for five buildings with 427 units. Of those, 122 are student-oriented apartments ranging from studios to six bedrooms. The plan also includes about 58,365 square feet of commercial space.

stories.headline: Delta Zeta Clears Approvals for 55-Resident House in Greek Village; Antique Apartments Seeks Four More Units
stories.text: Columbia's Board of Zoning Appeals and Urban Design Review Commission approved replacing the 11,000-square-foot Delta Zeta house at 514 Lincoln St. with a three-story, 31,000-square-foot building for 55 residents. No further city approvals are needed before permits. Separately, the Oct. 8 Planning Commission consent agenda included a request to raise the six-story Antique Apartments at 602 Huger St. from 174 to 178 units. The outcome was not seen and distance to campus was not verified.

stories.headline: Fayetteville Tables Camden Court Until January Over Parcel Ownership; Two Rezonings Split
stories.text: Fayetteville City Council voted 7-0 on Oct. 6 to table the revised Camden Court mixed-use plan (52 units, 148 parking spaces, about $20 million) until Jan. 5, 2027, over a question about who owns part of the parcel. Staff had changed its recommendation to approval. Council passed a 4.8-acre W. 22nd St. rezoning to RI-12 by 7-0 and rejected the W. Wedington Dr. RI-U rezoning 2-5.

stories.headline: Auburn Council Approves Sterling Auburn Cottages Infrastructure Deal With $368,500 Traffic Contribution
stories.text: On Oct. 6, Auburn City Council approved an infrastructure development agreement with TDC Pacific Properties for Sterling Auburn Cottages. The agreement includes $368,500 toward traffic improvements near Kent Drive, limits on construction traffic and stormwater obligations. The developer agreed to return with a landscaping addendum after neighbors raised buffering concerns. Unit and bed counts were not stated.

stories.headline: 122 State Street Conversion to 34 Apartments Heads to Madison Plan Commission Oct. 19
stories.text: A planned development would convert a six-story commercial building at 122 State St. into a seven-story mixed-use building with 34 apartments and 1,375 square feet of commercial space (Knothe & Bruce Architects). The Urban Design Commission reviewed it Oct. 7. The Plan Commission hearing is Oct. 19, followed by Council on Oct. 20. The site is about 0.7 miles from Library Mall via State Street (map check).

stories.headline: Clemson Staff-Initiated Rezoning Would Open 13 Acres on Cambridge Drive to Duplexes
stories.text: Clemson's Planning Commission takes up RZNE-00589-2026 on Oct. 13. The rezoning moves 16 parcels (about 13 acres) on Cambridge Drive from R-20 single-family to RM-1, which allows patio homes, zero-lot-line housing and duplexes. There is no applicant: the rezoning was initiated by the city. Six of the parcels are taxed as rentals. No unit count or staff recommendation is given, and distance to campus was not verified.

stories.headline: Audubon Capital Takes Over 322-Unit Crest at Midtown by Assuming Debt, Heading Off Foreclosure
stories.text: Liquid Capital Real Estate Investment has transferred Crest at Midtown, a 322-unit property at 215 North Ave. built in 2001 by Equity Residential, to Audubon Capital. Audubon assumed the remaining unpaid loan balance, and the asset changed hands as an outright sale rather than through foreclosure. Liquid Capital bought the property for $85.2 million in November 2021 with a $70.9 million Berkshire Residential loan. The 2021 basis works out to about $264,600 per unit (derived), and the original loan was about 83 percent of the purchase price. The assumed balance and any new equity were not disclosed, so the 2026 pricing cannot be calculated. Distance to the Georgia Tech campus was not stated in the source. The deal is a marker of 2021-vintage capital stacks in Midtown Atlanta being recapitalized at or near the debt. Crest at Midtown - 215 North Ave. Buyer Audubon Capital Seller Liquid Capital RE Investment Units / vintage 322 / 2001 Structure Loan assumption; pre-foreclosure 2021 purchase $85.2M (~$264.6K/unit, derived) 2021 loan $70.9M (Berkshire Residential) 2026 price Not disclosed

stories.headline: Coverse Capital Pays $17.5M for 88-Unit 6700 Roosevelt Across From Light Rail
stories.text: Coverse Capital paid $17.5 million, about $198,900 per unit, for the 88-unit 6700 Roosevelt apartments at 6700 Roosevelt Way NE, across from Seattle's Roosevelt light rail station. The Registry tags the article University District, but the distance to the UW campus is not stated and the article is paywalled beyond its summary.

stories.headline: Russell Hall Owner Lands $16M Life-Company Refinance in the U District
stories.text: The owner of Russell Hall, a 62,400-square-foot mixed-use building at 1414 NE 42nd St. near The Ave, closed a $16 million life-company refinance despite a looming office vacancy. Tags reference Gantry and Kidder Mathews. The residential unit count is not stated and the article is paywalled beyond its summary.

stories.headline: deChase Miksis and Edlen Close on Former LCC Downtown Center in Eugene
stories.text: The City of Eugene and developers deChase Miksis and Edlen & Co. closed Sept. 30 on the former Lane Community College downtown center at 1059 Willamette St. They plan a 133-unit mixed-use building with 68 below-market units, backed by more than $10 million from the city and its urban renewal district. Demolition is set for the end of 2026. This is not student housing, and distance to campus was not stated.

stories.headline: Purdue Trustees Approve Leasing All 984 Beds at 3rd & West Through 2029-30
stories.text: Purdue's Board of Trustees on Oct. 9 approved leasing all 401 apartments (984 beds) at 3rd & West, at Third Street and McCormick Road in West Lafayette, for the 2027-28 through 2029-30 academic years. The board cited the 2018 Giant Leaps Campus Master Plan. Trustees also approved 2027-28 housing rates. Nearly 80 percent of beds will rise by less than $300, a 3.2 percent increase. 3rd & West opened in August 2025, and South Hall opened this August. Together they added 1,900 beds to West Lafayette capacity. A three-year whole-building master lease by the university shows continued bed demand beyond what Purdue's own halls supply. It is also a precedent for university master leases of private or third-party product. The release does not disclose the lease rate, counterparty terms or renewal options. Derived: about 2.45 beds per apartment. Purdue - 3rd & West Lease Apartments / beds 401 / 984 Term AY 2027-28 through 2029-30 Approved Board of Trustees, Oct. 9, 2026 Opened August 2025 2027-28 rate change ~80% of beds Lease economics Not disclosed

stories.school_name: University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill
stories.headline: UNC Plans to Convert Baity Hill to Undergrad Beds, Push Upperclassmen Off Campus and Buy an Apartment Complex
stories.text: UNC-Chapel Hill plans to convert Baity Hill graduate and family housing to undergraduate housing to absorb enrollment growth. CFO Nathan Knuffman told trustees there are 2,400 apartment vacancies within 5 miles of campus and 4,500 within 10 miles, with about 2,000 apartments under construction. He outlined a preliminary plan to move upperclassmen into the community. Knuffman said the university is in the process of buying an apartment complex, which he did not name. UNC also plans 1,000 graduate beds at Carolina North, with groundbreaking possibly in 2027, and expects a two- to three-year gap between the Baity Hill conversion and Carolina North's opening. Graduate students are asking administrators not to take away the housing. For private owners, the plan points to more upperclass demand moving into the off-campus market during that gap.

stories.headline: StanfordNext GUP Seeks 2,500 Student Beds; County Is Said to Prefer Built Housing Over a $100M Fund
stories.text: Stanford's General Use Permit application, submitted to Santa Clara County in September, proposes 1.8 million square feet of additional academic space and 2,500 new student beds over two decades. It also offers a $100 million community fund focused mainly on regional affordable housing. The current GUP, approved in 2000, caps academic space at 2,035,000 net square feet. The application is in county review, and a vote could come in 2028. At the Undergraduate Senate's Oct. 7 meeting, Senator Ashton Dolce said the county wants Stanford to build housing itself rather than pay into a fund.

stories.headline: UA Faculty Challenge Explanation for 18.5% Drop in First-Year Class
stories.text: The University of Arizona's fall 2026 first-year class fell 18.5 percent. Enrollment VP Kristina Wong Davis said the decline returns the class to pre-COVID size. A faculty senator countered that it is nearly 650 students smaller than fall 2017. New undergraduates, including transfers, fell from 10,272 in 2023 to 8,498. Total enrollment is 67,714 (49,104 excluding Global Campus). This is a demand-side flag for Tucson freshman-heavy product.

stories.headline: UC Posts Record 54,437 Enrollment as First-Year Class Jumps 10.6%
stories.text: The University of Cincinnati's official fall 2026 headcount hit a record 54,437, up 1.4 percent (755 students). New first-year enrollment rose 10.6 percent across Uptown, Blue Ash and Clermont. UC credited part of the growth to the Bearcats Affordability Grant, which covers tuition for qualifying Ohio students with family income under $75,000.

stories.headline: Up Campus Seeks B-2A Rezoning for a ~750-Bed Tower on East High Street as Lexington Neighbors Push Back
stories.text: Up Campus Student Living has asked Lexington to rezone 1.134 acres bounded by E. High St., Stone Ave. and Hagerman Ct. from R-4 and P-1 to B-2A, a change that would allow a building of up to 10 stories and roughly 750 beds near the University of Kentucky. Planning committees recommended postponement, and the full Planning Commission is scheduled to hear the case Oct. 22, according to The Lexington Times' review of the week's planning filings. Opposition surfaced first. At a Sept. 30 neighborhood meeting, Aylesford residents objected to what WEKU described as a nine-story, 220-unit, approximately 750-bed complex, with rents of about $800 per bed; one resident called it "a lot of greed." The two reports differ on height (nine stories per WEKU; up to 10 stories under the requested zoning per The Lexington Times), and The Dispatch has not seen a site plan that resolves the difference. On the same filing list, Gilbane's Maxwell project recorded a plat that merges its land into one 1.8-acre lot. Underwriting read: the request works out to roughly 660 beds per acre (derived from the reported ~750 beds on 1.134 acres) and about 3.4 beds per unit (derived from WEKU's 220 units). Postponement at committee and an organized neighborhood response both raise the odds of conditions or a reduced program. Unit mix, parking count, capital stack and delivery year have not been reported. Up Campus Lexington (E. High St. / Stone Ave.) Developer Up Campus Student Living Site 1.134 acres Zoning request R-4 / P-1 to B-2A Height 9 stories (WEKU) / up to 10 (filing) Units / beds 220 / ~750 Quoted rent ~$800 per bed Beds per acre (derived) ~660 Next hearing Planning Commission, Oct. 22

stories.headline: RPM Living Grows Its High Street Project to 866 Beds, Absorbing the PJ's Sandwiches Block on Frambes
stories.text: RPM Living has expanded its seven-story student project at N. High St. and Woodruff Ave. to take in 15 Frambes Ave., assembling roughly two acres across four parcels north of Ohio State's campus core. The revised plan calls for 228 units and 866 beds, about 4,000 square feet of ground-floor retail and a 235-space garage. The University Impact District Review Board is scheduled to hear the project Oct. 22. Derived from the reported program, that is about 3.8 beds per unit and 0.27 parking spaces per bed. Total cost, financing, acquisition price for the added parcels and target delivery have not been reported. RPM Living - High St. / Woodruff Ave. Stories 7 Site ~2 acres, 4 parcels Units / beds 228 / 866 Beds per unit (derived) ~3.8 Retail ~4,000 SF Parking 235 spaces (~0.27 / bed, derived) Review University Impact District board, Oct. 22

stories.headline: Gainesville Commission Votes 5-1 to Draft Removal of Historic-District Height Buffers in University Heights
stories.text: The Gainesville City Commission voted 5-1 to direct staff to draft a code change that would remove the 100-foot buffers around the University Heights historic districts. Inside those buffers, buildings are held to three or four stories even where the underlying U9 zoning allows up to eight stories with bonuses. A draft is due by January 2027. For sites adjoining the historic districts near UF, the vote is direction to staff, not an adopted ordinance. Developers should treat added height as a 2027 possibility, not current entitlement, until the text amendment clears hearings.

stories.headline: Aspirant Development Breaks Ground on $288M, 533-Unit Revelry Towers in Tempe With $299M From Mavik
stories.text: Aspirant Development, the development arm of Empire Group, has started construction on Revelry, a 533-unit community in 15- and 17-story towers in Tempe. The project is reported at $288 million. Mavik provided $299 million of financing, arranged by WAY Capital. The reported loan exceeds the reported project cost, and the source does not reconcile the two figures. The Dispatch has not confirmed whether the project is purpose-built student housing, its bed count or its distance from ASU's Tempe campus. Derived cost is about $540,000 per unit. WAY Capital) Beds / student focus Not reported

stories.headline: Georgia Square Mall Overlay Hits Another Snag Over Apartment Share
stories.text: Athens-Clarke planning commissioners raised concerns that the proposed overlay for the 80-acre Georgia Square Mall site could produce a project that is mostly apartments. As drafted, the overlay could allow about 4,000 multifamily bedrooms, or nearly 6,000 with inclusionary bonuses. At that scale, the mall site would be a large potential supply source for the UGA market. A changed overlay could cap residential share or tie residential to other uses. The Dispatch has not located a revised schedule or vote date.

stories.headline: Columbia Council Votes Tonight on 32.7-Acre Rezoning for 194-Unit 'The Retreat at Columbia'
stories.text: The Columbia City Council is scheduled to vote Monday, Oct. 5, on rezoning 32.7 acres off Rock Quarry Rd. and Grindstone Pkwy. for The Retreat at Columbia, a 194-unit student multifamily development in south Columbia. The outcome was not known at press time. Bed count, developer and delivery year were not reported in the source. Derived density is about 5.9 units per acre.

stories.headline: EVER Knoxville Opens 498 Beds Across Lake Avenue From UT
stories.text: Subtext has opened EVER Knoxville, a 14-story, 136-unit, 498-bed student community at 1919 Lake Ave., directly across from the University of Tennessee. The project was developed with FrontRange Capital and TPG Real Estate Partners; Brinkmann Constructors was general contractor and FNBO provided construction financing. Derived average is about 3.7 beds per unit. Opening occupancy and rents were not disclosed. (Disclosure: Subtext publishes The Dispatch.)

stories.headline: Berkeley's 23-Story, 1,625-Bed Bancroft-Fulton Dorm Is Under Construction
stories.text: Construction is underway on UC Berkeley's Bancroft-Fulton residence hall at 2200 Bancroft Way, a 23-story tower with 1,625 beds and a 500-seat dining hall. Clark Construction is general contractor and KieranTimberlake is the architect. Completion is targeted for summer 2028. Berkeleyside's campus construction map, published the same day, reports Cal will have added more than 4,000 dorm beds within a decade. That count comes from a search summary, because the map page did not load for verification.

stories.headline: Clemson Off-Campus Beds 95.8% Preleased; Rents Flat at $959
stories.text: Yardi Matrix data reported by The Post and Courier show Clemson's off-campus beds 95.8 percent preleased for 2026-27, up 4.4 points year over year, with an average August rent of $959 per bed (-0.1 percent). The market counts 12,790 beds with 2,052 under construction, a pipeline equal to about 16 percent of existing stock (derived).

stories.headline: USC Off-Campus Rents Up 6.7% as 3,177 Beds Rise
stories.text: Per Yardi Matrix, USC's off-campus beds were 95.4 percent preleased for 2026-27 (16th among power-conference schools), with August rents averaging $937 per bed, up 6.7 percent year over year. Columbia has 14,762 beds and 3,177 under construction, about 22 percent of existing stock (derived).

stories.headline: Plan Board Splits 4-3 Against Cottages at Depot Park
stories.text: Gainesville's City Plan Board voted 4-3 to recommend denial of a land-use and Urban 6 zoning change for the two-acre, roughly 37-unit Cottages at Depot Park, citing loss of affordable housing. The City Commission makes the final decision; no date reported.

stories.headline: Bryan P&Z Recommends Denial of Traditions Condo Rezoning
stories.text: After resident protests, Bryan Planning & Zoning on Oct. 1 recommended denial of a condominium rezoning on a 2.57-acre lot in the Traditions community. The case goes to Bryan City Council Oct. 13.

stories.headline: Raleigh Hears Western Blvd. Upzoning Tuesday
stories.text: Raleigh City Council holds an Oct. 6 public hearing on Z-07-26 at 3911 Western Blvd., west of NC State, which would raise allowable height from three to seven stories along the planned Western BRT corridor. Planning Commission recommended approval 7-0. No development plan is attached.

stories.headline: The Arc Opens Fully Leased in Mount Auburn
stories.text: The Arc, a five-story, 56-unit, roughly 200-bed building near UC, opened fully leased, per Local 12 via Hoodline; it is not block-leased to UC. Cost was about $24 million per the Business Courier (~$120,000 per bed, derived). Hoodline flags its article as AI-assisted.

stories.headline: New State Law Closes Density-Bonus Route Around Berkeley Labor Rules
stories.text: Gov. Newsom signed a bill by Assemblymember Arreguin barring large projects from using the state density bonus to avoid local labor mandates. It was prompted by Collab Home's 20-story student project at 2425 Durant Ave. and Laconia's 23-story 2029 University Ave.

stories.school_name: University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill
stories.headline: Walde Buys Carrboro's Collins Crossing for $31.45M, 18% Below Laramar's 2019 Basis
stories.text: Walde Enterprises has acquired Collins Crossing, a 270-unit apartment community in Carrboro, for $31.45 million, or $116,481 per unit, from Laramar. The buyer assumed an existing Fannie Mae loan; Cushman & Wakefield brokered the sale. Laramar paid $38.5 million for the asset in 2019, so the trade is about $7.05 million, or roughly 18 percent, below the prior basis before any capital spent during the hold (derived). Collins Crossing is conventional multifamily in Carrboro, not purpose-built student housing. It is included as an in-market valuation marker for Chapel Hill. Loan balance, rate and remaining term on the assumed debt were not disclosed. Collins Crossing (Carrboro, N.C.) Buyer / seller Walde Enterprises / Laramar Units 270 (conventional MF) Price $31.45M Per unit $116,481 Seller basis (2019) $38.5M Change vs. basis (derived) -$7.05M / ~-18% Debt Assumed Fannie Mae loan (terms n/d) Broker Cushman & Wakefield

stories.headline: Capright: Q2 Student Housing Sales Fell More Than 20% to $1.5B; Landmark Narrows Its Build List
stories.text: At Bisnow's Georgia Student Housing Conference, Capright reported second-quarter student housing sales volume down more than 20 percent year over year to $1.5 billion. Landmark Properties said it is concentrating new development at top-tier schools such as Georgia Tech. Lower trade volume makes pricing evidence thinner for buyers and appraisers. Capright's report as covered by Bisnow does not give per-bed pricing or cap rates.

stories.headline: Mon County Adds $150K to East End Village as a $2.4M Land Payment Comes Due
stories.text: The Monongalia County Commission approved another $150,000 for the East End Village/Richwood redevelopment beside WVU's downtown campus, where 58 former by-the-bed rentals have been cleared. That brings the county's total to $990,000 toward a roughly $120 million envisioned investment. Per WAJR, the money, drawn from ARPA interest, lets the Morgantown Community Development Authority refinance site debt on the 9.5 acres it bought for $11.8 million in 2020 (~$1.24 million per acre, derived). The former owner says $2.4 million was owed by Oct. 1. Nonpayment could jeopardize the project, and the master developer role is unresolved.

stories.headline: Commissioners Press K-State Foundation on $304M Edge 3.0 Financing
stories.text: The K-State Foundation presented its $304 million Edge 3.0 North Campus Corridor (Champions Gate condos, a roughly 140-room hotel, research space and housing). Manhattan commissioners asked for more detail on the city's TIF share; no vote reported.

stories.headline: Yardi: UMN 93% Preleased as National Rent Growth Slows to 1.1%
stories.text: Citing Yardi Matrix's September report, REJournals notes University of Minnesota properties were 93 percent preleased in August for 2026-27, up 9.3 points year over year. National 2026-27 rent growth slowed to 1.1 percent as international enrollment softened.

stories.headline: Coral Gables Approves UM's 30-Year Campus Deal 5-0, Raising the Enrollment Trigger to 17,500
stories.text: The Coral Gables City Commission voted 5-0 on Sept. 29 to approve the University of Miami's development agreement together with comprehensive plan, land-use and zoning changes and a revised Campus Master Plan. The fixed 6.8 million-square-foot development cap is replaced with a 1.0 FAR, which Coral Gables Gazette puts at roughly 10.5 million square feet. The enrollment threshold that triggers mitigation rises from 13,000 to 17,500, and UM conveys 5.52 acres for Centennial Park. The deal also secures a site for a future hospital. On housing, Miami Today ties the approval to the 1,458-bed Gables Village, targeted for mid-2029, which will replace the Mahoney-Pearson residence halls. The net bed gain after the Mahoney-Pearson demolition was not reported. A higher enrollment trigger leaves room for UM to grow headcount. Separately, a student op-ed in The Miami Hurricane says nearly two-thirds of undergraduates live off campus or commute, and that a Centennial Village double runs about $1,687 a month, roughly 62 percent above the prior Stanford double. Both figures are the writer's, not the university's. UM / Coral Gables Agreement Vote 5-0, Sept. 29, 2026 Term 30 years Density 6.8M SF cap -> 1.0 FAR (~10.5M SF) Enrollment trigger 13,000 -> 17,500 Park conveyance 5.52 acres (Centennial Park) Housing Gables Village, 1,458 beds, mid-2029 Net new beds Not reported

stories.headline: Arkansas Adds 1,300+ Beds Through Maple Hill Central and North
stories.text: The University of Arkansas is responding to enrollment growth with two residence halls, Maple Hill Central and Maple Hill North, that together add more than 1,300 beds. Central is under construction for fall 2028. North is in design with no announced date. The university is also building an approximately 100,000-square-foot Walton College Dillard Hall, targeted for summer 2029. Delivery method (P3 or university-financed), per-bed cost and the bed split between the two halls were not reported.

stories.school_name: University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill
stories.headline: UNC Trustees Push In-State Freshman Growth and Keep 2,200-Bed Carolina North Plan on the Capital List
stories.text: UNC trustees urged an in-state first-year class of 4,750 to 5,000 for fall 2027. The Carolina North plan targets 2,200 undergraduate beds plus graduate housing, and Carolina North infrastructure is listed as a six-year capital priority. Whether the beds would be delivered through a P3 has not been stated. A timeline for an RFQ or RFP has not been located.

stories.headline: Four New California Laws Exempt Public-College Student Housing From CEQA and Speed Approvals
stories.text: Gov. Newsom signed four student housing bills that apply across the UC and CSU systems, including UC Berkeley and UCLA. AB 1732 exempts public-college student housing from CEQA. SB 916 curbs bad-faith lawsuits. AB 2118 streamlines approvals. AB 2480 adds density and parking incentives for projects with at least 24 percent low-income units. For P3 partners in California, CEQA exposure has been a major schedule risk on campus housing. Effective dates and the exact scope of each exemption should be confirmed against the chaptered text.

stories.headline: Illinois Housing Moves to Lottery After ~350 Started in Temporary Rooms
stories.text: University Housing adopted lottery-based room selection after record freshman classes. As of Aug. 31 there was a waitlist of about 200, and roughly 350 students began the semester in temporary housing, including about 100 displaced by Trelease Hall construction delays.

stories.headline: UW-Madison Undergrads Near Record Despite Total Dip
stories.text: Total enrollment fell to 50,965, but undergraduate enrollment of 37,133 is the second highest on record; 8,587 first-years enrolled from a record 75,234 applicants. Graduate enrollment fell to 9,101.

stories.headline: ASU International Headcount Falls 21% to 11,500
stories.text: ASU enrolled about 11,500 international students this fall, down 21 percent from 14,600, which the university attributes to visa delays and denials.

stories.headline: Lexington Enters a Student Housing Blitz: VERVE Breaks Ground at 784 Beds as the City Says 5,000 More Could Be Approved by Spring
stories.text: Subtext has started construction on VERVE Lexington at 185 E. Maxwell St., a 275-unit, 784-bed community near the University of Kentucky with delivery targeted for summer 2028. Pacific Life is providing the construction financing; equity comes from Clarion Partners, investing through a Qualified Opportunity Zone structure, and Peninsula Investments. The site sits inside a designated QOZ. (Disclosure: Subtext publishes The Dispatch.) The groundbreaking lands in the middle of what WEKU describes as a developer blitz. Its survey of near-campus projects lists Stavroff at 656 beds, Subtext at 799, Landmark at 972 and Core Spaces at 717, and Lexington's planning director told the station more than 5,000 student-oriented bedrooms could be approved over the next six months. Council members and neighbors raised affordability and displacement concerns in the same coverage. Note the discrepancy: WEKU's 799-bed Subtext figure does not match the 784 beds in the Lane Report groundbreaking release, and the reporting does not say whether WEKU is counting a different Subtext project or a different program. The Dispatch has not reconciled it. The approval queue is also slowing. Planning staff recommended postponing all eight rezonings on the Sept. 24 Planning Commission docket, including Up Campus Student Living's 225-unit building at E. High St. and Stone Ave. (B-2A) and The Dean's 262-unit mixed-use project at 1021-1069 S. Broadway. The Lexington Times did not report the reason for the blanket postponement or new hearing dates. UK's preliminary fall 2026 enrollment is a record 39,541 (+3 percent), with a first-year class of just over 6,700 that the university describes as roughly flat by design - meaning the demand growth is not coming from a bigger freshman class. High St. 225 units - postponed The Dean, S. Broadway 262 units - postponed Beds possibly approved, next 6 mo. 5,000+ (planning director) UK fall 2026 enrollment 39,541 (+3%, preliminary)

stories.headline: Champaign Stacks 1,977 Private Beds on Green and Chalmers While 350 Students Start the Year in Temporary Rooms
stories.text: Two private projects anchor the Campustown pipeline. Core Spaces' Hub Champaign Green Street at 201 E. Green St. is a 15-story, 1,577-bed tower with 129 parking spaces and 790 bike spaces, and it is drawing union protests over its contractor, PC Treehouse. Bromley Commons at 310 E. Chalmers St. is a six-story, 400-bed project targeting fall 2027. Hub's parking ratio works out to roughly 0.08 spaces per bed (derived). The demand side is not in question. Illinois enrolled a record 9,332 freshmen this fall, the third straight record, on total enrollment of 61,060. University Housing reported about 200 students on its waitlist as of Aug. 31 and roughly 350 starting the semester in temporary housing - including off-campus apartments and Wassaja Hall - partly because of construction delays at Trelease Hall and renovation delays at FAR. Gaps: the Daily Illini coverage does not give a delivery date for Hub Green Street, and neither project's developer financing, rents or unit counts are reported. The labor dispute is a schedule risk to watch; the reporting does not indicate whether it has affected work. stories.headline: Raleigh Approves Gilbane's 308-Unit Tower - Into a Market Yardi Has at 78.8% Preleased
stories.text: Raleigh City Council approved Gilbane Development's seven-story, 308-unit student housing project on 3.61 acres near NC State, replacing the Rhyne's Gate apartments; existing tenants get 120 days' notice and $2,500 per unit in relocation assistance. Coverage also cites a 713-bed Peerless proposal on Crest Road and a 130-unit RPM Living project on Horne Street. Edition 16 covered this project while it was still pending, when the concern was the 86 naturally affordable units it would remove. The approval runs into weak leasing. Yardi Matrix's September report puts NC State at 78.8 percent preleased as of August, among the weakest markets in the Yardi 200, and attributes it to 2,195 beds delivered in August (Hub Raleigh) with 970 more under construction for 2027. Bed count, delivery date and capital stack for the Gilbane project are not reported.

stories.headline: Trinitas Suit Over Rejected Dickson Street Tower Survives the City's Motion to Dismiss
stories.text: A judge denied Fayetteville's motion to dismiss Trinitas Ventures' lawsuit over the city's rejection of a seven-story, 185-unit student housing project on Dickson Street, so the case moves forward. This summary rests on the Democrat-Gazette's lead paragraph; the ruling's grounds, the claims that survived and the next court date were not available to The Dispatch. The demand backdrop is softening at the margin: preliminary fall figures show a record 7,118 freshmen but total enrollment of 33,990, down 0.5 percent from 34,161 - the first year-over-year decline since 2019 - while graduate enrollment rose to 4,779.

stories.headline: Mizzou's 14,666 Off-Campus Beds Are 99.9% Preleased at $839 a Bed, Up 7.6%
stories.text: Citing Yardi Matrix, KOMU reports Columbia's 14,666 off-campus student beds were 99.9 percent preleased for 2026-27, with average rent of $839 per bed, up 7.6 percent year over year. Yardi's September national report ranks Mizzou among the tightest Yardi 200 markets against a 93 percent national average, and operators including TODD told KOMU they expect fall 2027 leasing demand to arrive early. Separately, the new owners of three Eighth Street lots near Lyon Street, sold by Columbia College at a June auction, filed a concept review proposing fourplexes or attached single-family homes. Their price was not reported.

stories.headline: ASU Preleasing Falls to 87.3%, 5.9 Points Behind Last Year, as Tempe Enrollment Drops 7.4%
stories.text: Yardi Matrix data cited by CRE Daily shows ASU-Tempe fall 2026 enrollment down 7.4 percent, partly on international students, and ASU-area student housing 87.3 percent preleased, 5.9 points behind the prior year. Nationally, the Yardi 200 is at 93 percent preleased with leasing-season rent growth slowing to about 1.1 percent. Tempe delivered new supply into that softness this fall, including Subtext's 769-bed VERVE Tempe (Edition 17). The report does not split enrollment losses by undergraduate, graduate or online status, which determines how much of the drop affects near-campus beds.

stories.headline: State Backs $651M Arbor South With Up to $110.7M in Brownfield Tax Capture
stories.text: The Michigan Strategic Fund approved an Act 381 brownfield work plan for Arbor South, the Oxford Companies / Crawford Hoying mixed-use development in Ann Arbor, allowing up to about $110.7 million of state tax capture on a project of more than $651 million. The plan calls for about 1,069 units, 200 of them permanently affordable. The release does not say whether any units are student-oriented, and it gives no phasing or delivery dates.

stories.headline: Madison's Height-for-Affordability Swap Has Yielded 212 Lower-Rent Beds; Pipeline Could Reach 645
stories.text: Madison has gotten 212 lower-cost student beds by pairing a city height-bonus incentive with a UW income-verification agreement, according to the Cap Times. The pipeline includes 165 more at Core Spaces' oLiv, the Villas on Frances Street, Core Spaces' Saxony site (about 1,347 beds total) and Landmark's Master Hall site (986 beds), which could bring the program to 645 lower-cost beds by fall 2029. Rent levels and the share of each building set aside are not in the pipeline record. Separately, preliminary Universities of Wisconsin fall enrollment was about 163,260 (roughly -1 percent), driven by about 1,100 fewer international students; UW-Madison hit its freshman target.

stories.headline: LV Collective Plans 1,000-Plus Beds at Rambler College Park North as the City Regulates Early Lease Renewals
stories.text: LV Collective's Rambler College Park North, on the former Campus Village Shoppes site at Route 1 and Navahoe Street, will have 288 units and more than 1,000 beds over roughly 15,000 SF of retail, targeting fall 2027 (about 3.5 beds per unit, derived). The Hyattsville Wire flags visa-screening risk to international graduate enrollment. At the same time, College Park passed an Early Lease Ordinance limiting when landlords can offer renewals or give non-renewal notice - aimed directly at the early-signing pressure student housing leasing depends on. Effective date and penalties were not in the pipeline record.

stories.headline: Bryan Rezones Woodson and College Main Lot for Six-Story Student Building
stories.text: Bryan City Council unanimously rezoned a vacant lot at Woodson Drive and College Main near Midtown for a student-oriented apartment building of up to six stories. Final plans and permits are still required; developer, unit and bed counts were not reported.

stories.headline: Up Campus Refiles 165-Unit Seminole Trail Rezoning; Spy Rock Revises 267 Units Next Door
stories.text: Up Campus Properties has refiled its 165-unit rezoning (ZMA-2026-00006) at 1195 Seminole Trail in Albemarle County, next to Spy Rock's 267-unit project at 1185 Seminole Trail, where design revisions were approved. Bed counts and hearing dates were not reported.

stories.headline: Evanston Commission Recommends 26-Story, 360-Unit 900 Clark on a 4-1 Vote
stories.text: Evanston's Land Use Commission voted 4-1 to recommend Continuum Development's 26-story, ~298-ft tower at 900 Clark St.: 360 units (72 affordable) aimed at students and young couples, with no on-site parking and 112 spaces reserved in a garage across the street. It goes to City Council next; no date set.

stories.headline: Provo Planners Split 4-3 Against 491-Bed Park Plaza Rezone Over Parking
stories.text: The Provo Planning Commission voted 4-3 on Sept. 23 to recommend denial of Cole West's rezone for a six-story, 157-unit, 491-bed student project at 910 N. 900 E.; it proposes 278 stalls against 530 required (0.57 per bed, derived). Council date TBD. Source is a local civic blog.

stories.headline: CRG Seeks Height Waiver to Put an Amenity Deck on Half-Built 491-Bed Alder Chapter
stories.text: CRG is requesting an SB 1537 height waiver to add a rooftop amenity to its half-built Alder Chapter tower at 13th and Alder (133 units, 491 beds), taking it to about 169 ft against a 150-ft cap. The architect says the project's financing depends on the rooftop amenity.

stories.headline: Landmark Goes Under Contract for Rowland Hall's 4.62-Acre Lincoln Street Campus
stories.text: Landmark Properties is under contract to buy Rowland Hall's 4.62-acre Lincoln Street campus at 843 S. Lincoln St. in Salt Lake City, according to a memorandum filed with the county recorder, with off-campus student housing the likely use. Follow-up reporting confirms Landmark and 843 Place LLC are behind the deal, and Rowland Hall will lease the campus back through the end of 2026. The purchase price is not disclosed. County assessor values are about $28.5 million for the building and $5.9 million for the land; those are assessed values, not a trade price. The site is zoned Institutional with about 29 percent lot coverage today. Whether Landmark's plan needs a rezoning, and at what density, has not been reported and is the main entitlement unknown. For context, the University of Utah reported more than 900 empty beds this fall after its P3 delivered (Edition 16), and this week launched up to $3,500 in early-booking discounts for 2027-28 - a buyer is committing to this site while the on-campus product is discounting. 843 S. stories.headline: Liberty Group Takes Co-GP Equity in $300M-Plus of 908 Group Projects at UF and FSU
stories.text: Tampa's Liberty Group is providing co-GP equity alongside Society Hill Capital in three 908 Group / Batson-Cook student housing projects totaling more than $300 million. Two are named: the 219-unit, 684-bed Chapter House at UF (2029) and the 129-unit, 511-bed Chapter House FSU at 601 W. Madison / 506 W. Gaines St. in College Town (2027), which carries Pacific Life debt and Marble Capital preferred equity. The third project is described only as near 'UT'; the school is not identified in the pipeline record. Equity amounts per deal are not disclosed. stories.headline: BC Pays $40M for EF's 18-Acre Lake Street Campus, Uses Undecided
stories.text: Boston College bought EF Education First's roughly 18-acre, 89,000 SF campus at 200 Lake St. in Brighton, across from BC's Brighton Campus, for $40 million - about a 4 percent addition to its physical plant. BC has not set plans; uses are under evaluation, and housing has not been named. That is about $2.2M per acre or $449 per SF (derived).

stories.headline: State Sells 2.5 Downtown Acres to the Binkowskis for $12.65M, ~74% Below Appraisal
stories.text: The Joint Finance Committee voted 13-1 to sell the GEF-2 and GEF-3 sites at 101 and 125 S. Webster St. to Mark and Brad Binkowski for $12.65 million (~$5.06M per acre, derived) for market-rate mixed-use housing; the price is about 74 percent below the average appraisal. Closing is expected this fall.

stories.headline: Dwight Lends $42M Bridge on 1720 at Harvey Ahead of HUD Takeout
stories.text: Partin Development closed a $42 million cash-out bridge refinancing from Dwight on 1720 at Harvey, a 288-unit community opened in 2023 about a mile from Texas A&M, ahead of a planned HUD takeout; Greystone arranged it. That is about $145,800 per unit (derived). Rate and term not reported.

stories.headline: Near-Campus Bloomington Trades: Two Dunn Street Houses to One Buyer for ~$3.27M
stories.text: Monroe County records show 403 and 319 N. Dunn St. selling to Bloomington Builders LLC for about $1.67M and $1.60M (Sept. 16), 400 E. 19th St. sold by University Village V LLC for $1.175M (Sept. 18) and 302 N. Jefferson for $1.45M. The list also shows 701 N. College to BPG Station 11 for $16.35M, recorded Aug. 27.

stories.headline: Illinois Plans a $195M, 670-Bed Replacement for Taft-Van Doren - and Leans on Private Partners First
stories.text: University Housing plans a 670-bed residence hall with a 320-seat dining facility to replace Taft-Van Doren, at about $195 million with a fall 2029 target; the existing halls are to be demolished in May 2027. That works out to roughly $291,000 per bed including dining (derived). The more useful line for private developers: officials said added capacity will come first from existing Private Certified Housing partners. With about 350 students starting this term in temporary housing and a record freshman class (see Development News), the university is signaling it will lean on the PCH program before adding its own beds. Delivery method, financing and whether the new hall is a net addition after Taft-Van Doren comes down were not reported. Taft-Van Doren Replacement Beds 670 Dining 320 seats Budget ~$195M Cost per bed incl. dining (derived) ~$291,000 Demolition of existing halls May 2027 Target opening Fall 2029 Delivery method / financing Not reported

stories.headline: UVA Adds ~1,100 Beds by Fall 2027 and Sets Darden Rates at ~$1,534 a Bed
stories.text: UVA says its 780-bed Ivy Corridor housing (fall 2027) and Darden graduate housing (April 2027) will add about 1,100 beds, while the private Blume and VERVE projects add roughly 3,000 more next summer. The Board of Visitors Finance Committee set Darden's 216-unit, 338-bed complex at about $1,534 per bed per month. The treasurer said UVA holds AAA ratings and approved capital projects could need about $750 million in additional debt. Note a timing inconsistency across sources: Darden is described as opening in April 2027 in one report and fall 2027 in the rate approval coverage.

stories.headline: FSU Prices $289.69M of Dormitory Bonds at a 4.6677% TIC
stories.text: The Florida Board of Governors sold $289.69 million of Series 2026A dormitory revenue bonds for Florida State to BofA Securities at a 4.6677 percent true interest cost on seven bids. The bonds are dated Sept. 24, 2026, mature 2027-2056 and fund Phase 1 of FSU's Northwest Campus housing (Edition 17). The sale was priced before the 10Y moved from 5.01 to 5.17 percent.

stories.headline: Syracuse Adds 1,872 Sophomore Beds for Fall 2027 in a Market Yardi Has at 77.9% Preleased
stories.text: Syracuse's three new North Campus halls will add 1,872 sophomore beds for fall 2027: 544 University Place (568 beds), 315 Waverly Ave. (765 beds plus a 590-seat dining hall) and 501 Comstock Ave. (539). Room selection opens March 2027. Yardi Matrix has Syracuse at 77.9 percent preleased as of August, one of 21 Yardi 200 schools below 80 percent. Moving sophomores on campus takes a class year out of the off-campus renter pool.

stories.headline: RISE Delivers 1,024-Bed Torchbearer Hall, Phase II of UT's P3
stories.text: RISE and the University of Tennessee completed 1,024-bed Torchbearer Hall, bringing the campus housing P3 to about 3,000 beds. Team: Niles Bolton, Blaine Construction, Brailsford & Dunlavey, RBC Capital Markets and Provident Resources Group. UTK enrolled a record 7,205 first-years this fall.

stories.headline: Arizona Freshmen Fall 18.6% for a Second Year as 1,300-Bed Catalina Rises
stories.text: Arizona's first-year class fell from 7,506 to 6,111 (-18.6 percent), a second straight steep drop, partly because the Schedule for Success program ended; the faculty chair warned of budget impacts. The university's 1,300-plus-bed Catalina hall remains under construction for fall 2028 (Edition 17).

stories.school_name: University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill
stories.headline: UNC Trustees Push for 6,250 In-State Freshmen by 2030; CFO Warns on Housing
stories.text: After a record 5,319-student first-year class, UNC trustees passed a resolution seeking up to 5,000 in-state first-years next fall and 6,250 by 2030. The CFO warned the growth would strain housing and push more upperclassmen off campus.

stories.headline: Ole Miss Runs 170 Active Projects Worth $1.3B; Kincannon Goes Modular for August 2027
stories.text: The University of Mississippi has roughly 170 construction projects worth about $1.3 billion underway, a program that now includes two distinct student housing efforts - the Kincannon Site and West Row - moving in parallel on the Oxford campus. The Kincannon north building is nearing its top floor, and the south building is set to be built with modular units, with occupancy targeted for August 2027. The modular decision on the south building is the detail worth tracking: a university electing volumetric modular on the second half of a two-building housing site, while the first half tops out conventionally, is running a live schedule-and-cost comparison that most owners never get. Any developer bidding Mississippi labor should be watching which building hits its date. The reporting does not break the $1.3 billion figure down by project, does not give bed counts for Kincannon or West Row, and does not identify the modular manufacturer, the general contractor or the funding structure. Those four gaps are the difference between a headline and an underwritable comp, and The Dispatch has not filled them. Ole Miss Capital Program Active projects ~170 Program value ~$1.3B Housing projects named Kincannon Site; West Row Kincannon north Nearing top floor Kincannon south Modular units Target occupancy August 2027 Bed counts Not disclosed Contractor / financing Not disclosed

stories.headline: Auburn Signs a $349,154 Zoning Rewrite and Extends the Private-Dorm Moratorium
stories.text: Auburn City Council approved a $349,154 professional services agreement with the law firm White Smith Cousino to draft a comprehensive rewrite of the city zoning ordinance. The firm will start with the Urban Core and Urban Neighborhood-West districts - the two districts tied to the November 2025 moratorium on multi-unit developments and private dormitories - and the work is expected to take more than 24 months. This is the entitlement story of the week in the SEC footprint. Auburn has now attached a paid consultant, a scope and a multi-year clock to a moratorium that was already a year old, and the council simultaneously delayed action on the downtown lounge moratorium. For anyone holding an Auburn land position inside the Urban Core or Urban Neighborhood-West, the practical read is that the moratorium is not a pause to be waited out over a season; the rewrite is the exit, and it is a 24-month-plus exit. The reporting does not state the moratorium's current expiration date, whether it will be extended to match the rewrite timeline, or what density and use standards the draft will propose. Anyone underwriting an Auburn site should be pulling the engagement scope directly rather than waiting for the draft to surface in coverage. Auburn Zoning Rewrite Contract value $349,154 Firm White Smith Cousino First districts Urban Core; Urban Neighborhood-West Tied to Nov. 2025 multi-unit / private dorm moratorium Expected duration 24+ months Moratorium expiration Not stated in reporting

stories.headline: Trinitas Closes on Norman Site for 677-Bed Atmosphere, First Institutional Product Near OU in a Decade
stories.text: Trinitas Ventures closed on the site for Atmosphere Norman at the southwest corner of Boyd Street and the BNSF railroad corridor, replacing the Ray Apartments with a seven-story, 209-unit mixed-use community. Trinitas puts the bed count at 677 and says it will be the first new institutional student housing near the University of Oklahoma in more than a decade, with completion in summer 2028. The program includes studios through five-bedroom units, more than 13,700 square feet of indoor amenity space, two courtyards, a pool and two parking levels with 265 spaces. Derived from those figures: 3.24 beds per unit and 0.39 parking spaces per bed - a ratio that only works in a walk-to-campus location and is a useful benchmark for anyone arguing parking reductions in a Big 12 or SEC college town. Demand evidence cited in the local reporting: more than 900 students were waitlisted for the university's Traditions Square apartments in early 2026. No total development cost, capital structure, general contractor or preleasing target has been disclosed.
