stories.headline: Katy Station Goes Under Contract in Columbia as a Preservation Fight Forms Around It
stories.text: Maher Real Estate president Jack Maher III confirmed that the Katy Station building at 402 E. Broadway and the adjacent Broadway Diner location in downtown Columbia are under contract. The commercial listing combining the two properties describes the assembly as positioned for student housing or mixed-use redevelopment. The site is already generating friction ahead of any filing. Shiloh Bar and Grill, a tenant at Katy Station since 2009 and in business 28 years, will close in December because of the pending sale. A petition led by former Boone County Southern District Commissioner Fred Parry is circulating to save the building from demolition, and the property carries a preservation profile - it was added to the Columbia Historic Register in 1979 and originally served as a Missouri-Kansas-Texas Railroad depot. Organizers say no developer has publicly presented a concept for the site. That is the operative fact: buyer identity, price, unit or bed program and entitlement path are all undisclosed, and opposition is organizing against a project that does not yet exist on paper. A designed-in preservation response to the 1979 register listing is likely to be the price of entitlement here.

stories.headline: Radnor Advances Ground-Leased Oakland Tower With a Grocery Anchor on Pitt Land
stories.text: Radnor Property Group advanced plans for a mixed-use building with hundreds of apartments and a ground-floor grocery store at 3401 Boulevard of the Allies in Oakland, on land owned by the University of Pittsburgh under a 75-year ground lease. The eight-story project replaces the former Quality Inn site. Radnor is targeting the first quarter of 2027 for demolition and site work, with construction running two to two and a half years and an opening in mid-2029. The structure is the point of interest: a 75-year university ground lease on a campus-adjacent parcel, with a grocery anchor solving the retail amenity gap that Oakland has carried for years. Unit count, bed count, rent positioning, grocer identity and the ground rent economics have not been disclosed.

stories.headline: Landmark and W5 Deliver 635-Bed Standard at Syracuse With a Synagogue Sanctuary as Amenity
stories.text: Landmark Properties and W5 Group delivered The Standard at Syracuse, a 635-bed, 210-unit community at 910 Madison Street one block north of campus, which welcomed its first residents in August 2026. The seven-story project preserved the historic Temple Concord sanctuary as a 4,750-square-foot amenity space, and preleasing for 2027-2028 is underway. Derived: 3.02 beds per unit. The adaptive-reuse amenity solution is the transferable idea - a preserved sanctuary converted to program space is a template for any infill site where a historic structure would otherwise be a demolition fight. No development cost, capital structure or fall 2026 occupancy figure has been published.

stories.headline: Fayetteville Council Splits Three Ways on Rezonings, Mayor Breaks a 4-4 Tie
stories.text: Fayetteville's council produced an unusually mixed set of land-use outcomes. On Sept. 15 it approved a 7-1 rezoning that staff said would add redevelopment flexibility and housing options on a 0.20-acre site, and an 8-0 rezoning of about 0.66 acres at 710 North Frisco Avenue, while a rezoning appeal covering 0.55 acres at 1845 W. Wedington Drive failed 5-3. Two weeks earlier, the council approved a 26.6-acre residential rezoning to single-family at eight units per acre only after a 4-4 vote was broken by Mayor Molly Rawn, and only after the applicant amended the request to drop a 9.6-acre parcel. The pattern across both meetings: small infill rezonings clear easily, larger acreage draws organized neighbor opposition and requires either a mayoral tiebreak or a reduction in scope. Applicants in Fayetteville should assume the land-area threshold, not the use, is what triggers the fight.

stories.headline: Ann Arbor Planning Commission Clears 66-Unit State Street Flats at 60% AMI
stories.text: The Ann Arbor Planning Commission unanimously approved the site plan and rezoning for State Street Flats, a four-story, 66-unit project on an undeveloped lot just south of I-94, restricted to households at or below 60 percent of area median income. Developer Lockwood Development says it will pursue National Green Building Standards Silver certification. The project now goes to City Council for a final vote. A unanimous commission vote on a deed-restricted affordable project in Ann Arbor is a useful read on which product type currently clears entitlement friction in this market. No total development cost, subsidy sources or delivery date have been reported.

stories.headline: Penn State Trustees Approve $107.1M in Construction, None of It Housing
stories.text: Penn State's Board of Trustees approved four construction and renovation projects totaling $107,127,000, three of them at University Park: a state-funded addition to the Animal Diagnostic Lab, Henderson Building renovations and additional Applied Research Lab build-out. No residential component was included in the approved slate - notable in the same meeting at which the board moved on campus dispositions.

stories.headline: Iowa State Breaks Ground on Remaining CyTown, a $175M-$225M District
stories.text: Iowa State broke ground Sept. 2 on the remaining portion of CyTown, a mixed-use entertainment district between Hilton Coliseum and Jack Trice Stadium carrying a reported $175 million to $225 million range and featuring a 200-room Marriott hotel, restaurants, retail and gathering spaces, with completion slated for August 2028. The reporting describes no residential component; the $50 million spread between the low and high cost figures has not been explained.

stories.headline: Illinois Puts $371.7M Into Two Academic Rebuilds Through Spring 2028
stories.text: Facilities and Services updated the status of the $306.5 million Illini Hall replacement and Altgeld renovation, projected to finish in late fall 2027, and the $65.2 million Undergraduate Library conversion to an Archives and Special Collections building, due spring 2028. Combined, $371.7 million of Urbana-Champaign construction capacity is committed to non-residential work through spring 2028 - relevant to trade availability and pricing for any private housing start in Champaign County over the same window.

stories.headline: Tech Square Phase 3 Opens: Two Towers, 416,500 SF, $200M
stories.text: Georgia Tech's Tech Square Phase 3 - the 14-story Scheller Tower and 18-story George Tower, 416,500 square feet combined at a reported $200 million - opened for the fall 2026 semester with a ribbon-cutting on Sept. 18. This is academic and mixed-use campus product, not student housing, and is carried here for Midtown Atlanta market context only.

stories.headline: Raleigh Weighs a Parking-Free Mixed-Use Rezoning at Ashe Avenue
stories.text: A roughly 0.3-acre rezoning at 111 and 113 Ashe Avenue and 0 Wakefield Avenue, between Pullen Park and NC State, would swap residential zoning for mixed-use allowing small-scale retail with no off-street parking requirement. The Raleigh Planning Commission is expected to review it before a City Council decision. Small site, but the no-parking condition on a campus-edge parcel is the precedent worth tracking.

stories.headline: Evanston Townhomes Clear Inclusionary Rules With One Large Affordable Unit
stories.text: A 10-unit townhome project at 3233-3249 Central St. was cleared for construction with one affordable unit and no major fee-in-lieu, using an incentive in Evanston's inclusionary housing ordinance that credits larger affordable units. The mechanism matters more than the project: it shows how Evanston's inclusionary requirement is actually being satisfied on small residential sites, and what a developer can trade unit size against to avoid the fee.

stories.headline: Scion Closes Student Quarters, Reaching 117,000 Beds and 92 Markets
stories.text: The Scion Group closed its acquisition of the operating business of Atlanta-based Student Quarters, a platform Scion puts at roughly $1.3 billion of assets under management, and will run Atlanta as an additional operating hub. The transaction was announced in June and has now closed. Scion's post-close scale figures: 187 communities and nearly 117,000 beds across 92 university markets, with more than $4.7 billion of capital deployed and bed count up 45 percent over 24 months. For owners in the 30 priority markets, the operating implication is concentration - a single manager now touches 92 markets, which compresses the pool of independent third-party managers and strengthens Scion's hand on management fees, revenue-management data and staffing in every market where it operates at scale. Note one discrepancy against prior reporting: the June announcement described the Student Quarters platform as roughly $1.5 billion and about 13,000 beds across 21 markets, while the closing release puts it at roughly $1.3 billion of AUM. The Dispatch has not reconciled the two figures and does not know whether assets were carved out before closing. Purchase price was not disclosed in either release. stories.headline: GMH and Invesco Buy Two Purdue-Adjacent Assets - But the Bed Count Does Not Agree
stories.text: A joint venture of GMH Communities and Invesco Real Estate acquired Grant Street Station and South Street Station in West Lafayette, both less than a quarter-mile from Purdue and both fully leased for the current academic year. TSB Realty brokered the sale. The two trade publications covering the deal do not agree on the size. Multi-Housing News reports the portfolio at 540 beds; Institutional Real Estate Inc. reports 176 units and 364 beds. The unit count appears only in the IREI account. The Dispatch is not reconciling the difference or picking a number: at 540 beds the assets carry 3.07 beds per unit, at 364 beds they carry 2.07, and those are materially different products. Anyone comping this trade needs the rent roll, not the press coverage. No purchase price, cap rate, seller or debt structure has been disclosed in either account. stories.headline: Bloomington Housing Authority Moves to Buy 924 Units for ~$81M to Block Student Conversion
stories.text: The Bloomington Housing Authority plans an approximately $81 million purchase of five apartment complexes totaling 924 units - Basswood, Kingston Manor, Northcrest, Woodland Springs and Summit Pointe - funded by up to $100 million in revenue bonds. The stated purpose is to preserve workforce housing from luxury student redevelopment. Derived: roughly $87,662 per unit. That is the number to hold against any Bloomington value-add underwriting, and the transaction removes 924 units from the pool of conversion candidates in a market where student redevelopment has been the dominant bid. A public authority outbidding private capital on explicitly anti-conversion grounds is a political signal as much as a trade. Closing date, seller identity, bond pricing and the spread between the $81 million purchase and the $100 million authorization have not been reported. stories.headline: Ohio Controlling Board Clears UC to Buy 293 Uptown Beds for $33.2M
stories.text: The University of Cincinnati received state approval to acquire nearly 300 student housing beds across three contiguous parcels totaling 2.23 acres adjacent to its Uptown campus for $33.2 million. The properties at 101 E. Corry St. and 130 William Howard Taft Road contain 127 housing units with 293 beds; the state request identified the seller entities as VP4 LLC and Aristo Properties II BV. Derived: approximately $113,311 per bed, $261,417 per unit and $14.9 million per acre. The per-bed figure is the comp that matters - a university paying six figures per existing bed to take private product off the market, on contiguous parcels, is buying land control as much as beds. Any owner of campus-adjacent Uptown product now has a state-documented price point to negotiate against. stories.headline: Penn State Sells Two Closing Campuses for $6.25M After Deed Restrictions Were Quietly Erased
stories.text: Penn State trustees approved the sale of the 12.74-acre Shenango campus to JCL Development LLC for $1 million and the 57.31-acre Wilkes-Barre campus to HGC Development LLC for $5.25 million. Both campuses close at the end of the 2026-27 academic year, and the transactions are part of a wider plan affecting seven locations by 2027. Derived: roughly $78,493 per acre at Shenango and $91,608 per acre at Wilkes-Barre. The enabling event was legislative - Pennsylvania lawmakers removed longstanding deed restrictions on the seven closing commonwealth campuses, which is what made disposition possible at all. Five more campuses remain to be sold under the same cleared restrictions, and these two trades set the opening marks. Buyer development plans have not been disclosed. stories.headline: Alta Lists 675-Bed SoMi Walk Mid-Construction to Beat the Opportunity Zone Deadline
stories.text: Alta Development listed its under-construction SoMi Walk project at 5959 SW 71st Street in South Miami, a 16-story building with 675 beds across 173 units - 3.90 beds per unit derived. The site sits in a federal Opportunity Zone and the listing is timed to capture the tax benefit before the program's year-end expiration. Expect more mid-construction OZ listings in the fourth quarter for the same reason; asking price was not disclosed.

stories.headline: Morgan Properties Buys 288-Unit Buckstone Flats on a $42.6M Fannie Loan at 5.24%
stories.text: Morgan Properties acquired Buckstone Flats, a 288-unit community delivered in 2024 in the Columbus suburb of Obetz, from JBM Development. Newmark issued a $42.6 million Fannie Mae acquisition loan at 5.24 percent - roughly $147,917 of loan proceeds per unit, derived. The 5.24 percent coupon is the most useful data point in the trade: a dated, agency-executed Columbus cost of debt to check bridge quotes against. Purchase price and cap rate were not disclosed.

stories.headline: Waco 1978-Vintage Northwind Trades on a Loan Assumption and Preferred Equity
stories.text: The Multifamily Group brokered the sale of Northwind Apartments, a 71-unit 1978-built community along Interstate 35 in Waco, less than a mile from Texas State Technical College. The transaction used a loan assumption paired with a preferred equity structure - the capital-stack workaround that keeps small value-add trades moving with the 10Y above 5 percent. Price was not disclosed, and the asset is not campus-adjacent to Baylor.

stories.headline: IU and Buckingham Open the Beverly on University Ground Lease - and Draw Rent Backlash
stories.text: Indiana University and Buckingham Companies celebrated the grand opening of the Beverly Apartments, built on IU-owned land at the former Poplars site at Seventh and Dunn streets under a ground lease, alongside a new Buckingham Scholarship. The six-story building carries 158 units. Rents range from $1,275 to $2,060 per bed and have drawn student and parent backlash. That reaction is the part of this deal every P3 sponsor should study: the ground-lease structure and the named scholarship were the public-benefit package, and they did not insulate the project from a rent-affordability fight at opening. The scholarship is a mitigation mechanism whose size relative to the rent premium has not been disclosed. Bed count, ground rent terms, lease duration and the scholarship's annual funding have not been published. The opening lands in the same week Bloomington's housing authority moved to buy 924 units specifically to keep them out of the luxury student pool - the two stories are the same local politics from opposite directions. stories.school_name: University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill
stories.headline: UNC Sets a Construction Master Plan to 2034 Against a 5,000-Student Enrollment Increase
stories.text: Carolina Housing executive director Allan Blattner outlined a Construction Master Plan running through 2034 built to support Chancellor Lee Roberts' plan to grow enrollment by 5,000 students. The plan includes replacing Parker and Teague halls and renovating Hinton James, Ehringhaus and Craige. The sentence with the most commercial content: Blattner frames Carolina North as enabling the private market to build additional student housing. A university that is simultaneously adding 5,000 students, taking existing halls offline for replacement and renovation, and pointing private capital at a specific district is describing a bed gap it does not intend to fill entirely itself. No bed counts, phasing sequence, offline-bed schedule or budget figures were published for the master plan.

stories.headline: Gainesville Opens the First Study of 913 Acres Next to UF Since 2003
stories.text: The Gainesville City Commission launched a land use and zoning study of the 913-acre Southwest Study Area near the University of Florida and Butler Plaza, the first comprehensive review of the area since 2003. The scope covers housing and affordability, transportation and transit, and sidewalks. A 23-year-old zoning framework on 913 acres adjacent to a flagship campus is the single largest entitlement variable in the Gainesville market, and it is now formally in play. Study outcomes - not individual project approvals - will set density, use and parking standards across the entire area. Timeline, consultant, public hearing schedule and whether an interim development moratorium will apply during the study have not been reported. Anyone with a Southwest Gainesville site should be tracking the study calendar now rather than filing into an unsettled framework.

stories.headline: USC Carries ~$1.8B of Buildout Into Record Enrollment Under the USC Next Plan
stories.text: University of South Carolina leadership highlighted roughly $1.8 billion of construction underway or planned alongside continued enrollment growth, tied to the USC Next 10-year master plan. At the Sept. 9 State of the University address, President Amiridis cited record enrollment and named Woodrow student housing renovations and the completed Thornwell renovation, previewing new STEM research, civil rights history and brain health facilities. Preliminary fall 2026 undergraduate enrollment in Columbia topped 33,000, with total campus population near 41,650, up 2.5 percent over fall 2025, and system enrollment at a record 60,300. Two named housing items in a $1.8 billion program are both renovations, not new beds - against a 2.5 percent enrollment increase, that is a widening private-market opportunity unless USC has unannounced new construction. The housing share of the $1.8 billion has not been broken out.

stories.headline: Purdue Adds ~500 Indianapolis Beds by May 2027 After 1,900 Came Online in West Lafayette
stories.text: Purdue's Academic Success Building in Indianapolis will add nearly 500 residential beds and is set to complete in May 2027, following the August opening of the 252,500-square-foot South Hall which, with 3rd & West, added 1,900 beds to West Lafayette capacity. Purdue's incoming freshman class rose 13 percent over fall 2025 to 10,818 across both campuses, with system enrollment at a record 111,047 - the university is adding beds and students simultaneously, and has not published a net capacity position.

stories.headline: TCU Tops 13,000 Students With $500M of Outside Capital Building Four Residential Communities
stories.text: TCU surpassed 13,000 students for the first time, with four new residential communities and a five-story parking garage under construction and student housing expected to open before the fall 2027 semester, funded by more than $500 million of outside investment. The outside-capital structure on a private university's residential program is the item to chase - counterparty, bed counts and deal form have not been reported. Separately, UT Arlington reported a record 5,332 first-time-in-college students.

stories.headline: Boulder Starts Flood Work That Unlocks CU Boulder South Housing
stories.text: The city of Boulder will begin construction on the South Boulder Creek Flood Mitigation project at CU Boulder South in roughly six weeks; completion of the flood work is the precondition for CU Boulder to develop student, faculty and staff housing on the site. Meanwhile CU Boulder's fall 2026 enrollment is estimated at 38,510, down 298 students or 0.8 percent year over year, as systemwide CU enrollment fell 1.4 percent on international declines. Flood project duration, cost and the housing program's bed count and timeline were not reported.

stories.headline: Subtext Opens 769-Bed VERVE Tempe, 15 Stories on South Terrace Road
stories.text: Subtext has opened VERVE Tempe, a 15-story, 769-bed purpose-built community at 1047 S. Terrace Road within walking distance of Arizona State. The building carries 240 units across 479,388 square feet and more than 1,800 square feet of street-level retail. The derived figures are worth logging: 3.20 beds per unit and roughly 623 gross square feet per bed. Both are high-density high-rise metrics, consistent with a Tempe parcel where land basis forces vertical density and shared-bedroom plans carry the rent roll. It is Subtext's second ASU-serving development after Canvas, delivered in 2021. VERVE Tempe lands in the single most heavily supplied student market in the country. Yardi Matrix's August report puts Arizona State first nationally for beds under construction, with Tempe absorbing multiple 700-plus-bed high-rise deliveries in the same leasing season. No lease-up, occupancy or rent data for the fall term has been published. VERVE Tempe — Arizona State Address 1047 S. stories.headline: Arizona Breaks Ground on The Catalina, a $247M, 1,300-Bed Residence Hall
stories.text: The University of Arizona broke ground on The Catalina, a nine-story residence hall budgeted at $247 million that will house more than 1,300 students when it opens in fall 2028. It is the largest single institutional housing commitment in the Tucson market this cycle. At $247 million across more than 1,300 beds, the project computes to roughly $190,000 per bed — a figure that sits at the top of the institutional range and above the per-bed pricing seen in this edition's private portfolio trades. The university has not published a financing structure, so whether this is system revenue bonds, state appropriation or a hybrid remains unconfirmed, and that distinction drives the credit read. The groundbreaking arrives in the same month the university confirmed its Arizona-Sonora residence hall will not house undergraduates in 2026-27, converting instead to graduate overflow. Adding 1,300 beds for 2028 while pulling an existing hall out of the undergraduate pool for 2026-27 is a two-directional signal about where Tucson demand is actually concentrated. No contractor, architect or delivery contingency has been disclosed. stories.headline: Clemson Drafts a Standalone Student Housing Zoning District
stories.text: Clemson City Council held a public hearing on Text Amendment 2026-R-04, which would create a standalone Student Housing District in the city's zoning ordinance — establishing definitions, permitted uses, density limits and parking requirements specific to student-oriented development. This is a structural change, not a project approval. A purpose-built student housing use class, once codified, determines whether future Clemson projects are entitled by right within the district or forced into rezoning and conditional-use fights parcel by parcel. The density caps and parking ratios written into the amendment become the effective ceiling on every unbuilt site in the city. The text of the amendment — the actual density limit, the parking ratio, the district's mapped boundaries and whether it is an overlay or a base zone — has not been published in the reporting reviewed. Anyone with a Clemson land position should be pulling the ordinance draft directly rather than waiting for coverage. No adoption vote date has been reported.

stories.headline: Subtext Lands 520-Bed EVER Lexington on South Limestone With UMB Debt
stories.text: Subtext is developing EVER Lexington, a 520-bed, 149-unit seven-story community at 565 S. Limestone near the University of Kentucky, with roughly 4,000 square feet of ground-floor retail and a pool-deck amenity package. Construction is set to begin in fall 2026 for a summer 2028 delivery. The capital stack is unusually well disclosed for a deal this size: FrontRange Capital and Larson Capital Management are equity partners, UMB is project lender, and the site sits inside a qualified opportunity zone. The QOZ overlay is the detail that matters — it implies a ten-year hold assumption baked into the equity, not a merchant-build exit. At 520 beds in 149 units the plan runs 3.49 beds per unit, the densest bed-per-unit ratio in this edition. That is a shared-bedroom-weighted program built for rent-per-bed efficiency on an expensive infill parcel. Total project cost and the loan amount were not disclosed. stories.headline: INTRO Columbus Tops Out 10 Weeks Early as Tallest U.S. Mass Timber Student Tower
stories.text: Harbor Bay Ventures topped out INTRO Columbus on Sept. 8, a 13-story, 242,000-square-foot mass timber student housing tower at 1497 North High Street near Ohio State. The building reached its full 48-metre height ten weeks ahead of a November target and will deliver 186 units and 493 beds. Ten weeks of schedule recovery on a mass timber high-rise is the story. Prefabricated CLT panel erection is the mechanism developers have been promising would compress structural schedules, and this is a documented instance of it happening on a student asset at 13 stories. The team is DLR Group (design), Elford Construction, SmartLam North America (timber supply) and Coastal Ridge (management). At 493 beds across 186 units the program runs 2.65 beds per unit in studio-through-six-bedroom configurations — a wide plan mix rather than a uniform shared-bedroom product. Project cost, delivery date and the timber premium versus a concrete alternative were not disclosed.

stories.headline: UCF Carries 4,338 Beds Under Construction as ACC Adds 898 More
stories.text: Yardi Matrix's August 2026 national student housing report puts the University of Central Florida at 4,338 beds under construction, second only to Arizona State. National preleasing reached 89.1 percent in July at an average $930 per bed. Inside that pipeline, American Campus Communities is building Crest on University, an 898-bed community at 12099 University Boulevard adjacent to the main UCF entrance. The $85 million project started in 2025 and targets fall 2027, working to roughly $94,700 per bed — less than half the per-bed cost of the University of Arizona's institutional Catalina project above, which is the clearest supply-cost spread in this edition. The demand-side counterweight is not encouraging in the near term: roughly 3,000 UCF financial aid cases remained under review weeks into the fall semester, with students reporting difficulty covering rent. Delayed disbursement is a collections problem for every operator in Orlando this term, not a leasing problem. Northmarq separately reports permitting and construction activity declining across the broader Orlando multifamily market.
