stories.school_name: University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill
stories.headline: UNC Names Jackson Hall in First New Residence Halls in 20 Years
stories.text: UNC-Chapel Hill will name one of two new residence halls for Blyden and Roberta Jackson. The pair will add roughly 730 beds and are the first new residence halls built at Carolina in two decades, with work underway on the site of the former Jackson Hall on North Campus. Carolina Housing has published active construction impacts around Residence Hall One adjacent to the Cobb and Stacy halls, confirming the site is in live construction rather than design. Twenty years without a new residence hall on a campus of Carolina's size means the 730 beds are replacement-and-catch-up capacity, not net growth against enrollment — the university has not published a net bed figure or the count of beds taken offline by the former Jackson Hall demolition. Project cost, delivery date and whether either hall carries a P3 structure have not been disclosed. Read alongside the Carolina North developer solicitation in the P3 section, the university is running institutional housing construction and a private development partner search simultaneously.

stories.headline: Stanford Files for 2,500 Beds, 500 Homes and 1.8M SF in Two-Decade Expansion
stories.text: Stanford submitted a permit application to Santa Clara County seeking nearly 2 million square feet of academic space, 2,500 student beds and about 500 units of faculty and staff housing over the next two decades. The university identified a workforce housing site near El Camino Real and Quarry Road, across from the Palo Alto Transit Center. Reporting differs on the housing split: one account puts 500 apartments across from the downtown Palo Alto train and bus station plus another 500 homes at Stanford Research Park, while the application headline figure is at least 500 homes in total. The discrepancy is unresolved in the coverage and should not be treated as settled. This is Stanford's latest attempt at a general use permit after its previous application collapsed in 2019 over affordable housing and traffic mitigation terms. A twenty-year entitlement horizon with 2,500 beds attached is the single largest bed authorization sought in this edition, but it is an application, not an approval, and Santa Clara County's conditions are where the actual deal will be made.

stories.headline: Metro Council Approves Vanderbilt Innovation Neighborhood on 40 Acres
stories.text: Nashville's Metro Council gave final approval to Vanderbilt's Specific Plan rezoning covering roughly 40 acres on the west side of campus. The long-term mixed-use district is slated to include housing, retail, research and lab space alongside expanded greenspace. The approval passed by voice vote with no audible opposition after months of negotiation with Hillsboro-West End neighbors — a notable outcome for a district of this scale. The concession that closed it: amendments lowering the tallest building zone near West End Avenue and Natchez Trace to 30 stories. A 30-story ceiling on a negotiated downzone is still among the most permissive university-adjacent entitlements granted in the Southeast this year. No housing unit count, bed count, phasing schedule or development partner has been published. For Nashville underwriting purposes, the relevant fact is that 40 acres adjacent to Vanderbilt now carries Specific Plan zoning with vertical capacity, which resets the land basis on every competing parcel in the Hillsboro-West End submarket.

stories.headline: Lawrence Approves $50M in Bonds for 341-Unit West Campus Project, 4-1
stories.text: The Lawrence City Commission voted 4-1 to approve an economic development incentive for The Crossing, a 341-unit market-rate apartment complex on KU's West Campus near 23rd and Iowa streets, adjacent to the KU Innovation Park incubator. Developer 23 Iowa Investors, affiliated with Block Real Estate Services, now estimates project cost at $106.8 million, up from $104.4 million. The mechanism is worth understanding precisely: the city resolved its intent to issue $50 million in industrial revenue bonds purely as conduit financing, with no city credit behind them, so the developer captures a one-time sales tax exemption on construction materials. The IRBs are a tax vehicle, not a funding source. The 4-1 vote triggered a broader argument over Lawrence's economic development policy and whether incentive awards should carry affordable housing requirements — the live question for anyone planning a Lawrence incentive request in 2027. Bed count, unit mix and delivery date for The Crossing have not been published.

stories.headline: Auburn Council Approves Richland Road Rezoning Amid Lemans Square Fight
stories.text: An Auburn City Council meeting turned contentious over redevelopment of the Lemans Square and Chateau apartment complexes, and the council approved a rezoning amendment for The District at Richland Road near Shug Jordan Parkway. Unit counts, bed counts and the developer behind The District were not reported.

stories.headline: 600-Bed Waco Project Rises on Former Church Land
stories.text: Construction is underway on a 600-bed student housing complex on land Seventh and James Baptist Church sold last fall — half of its five-acre holding — with Parallel and Deven Group leading the development group and delivery targeted by summer 2028. The church is now planning a new sanctuary after its old building was demolished for the project. Separately, the Waco Plan Commission unanimously recommended approval of a 141-page downtown form-based code covering roughly 88.55 acres.

stories.headline: Berkeley Reviews 68-Unit Telegraph Project Built for Group Leases
stories.text: The Berkeley Zoning Adjustment Board reviewed an eight-story, 68-unit project above the Amoeba record store at 2455 Telegraph Avenue, blocks from UC Berkeley. The unit mix is explicitly student-oriented — 15 three-bedrooms, 10 four-bedrooms and 43 five-bedrooms, seven of them deed-restricted affordable. A second ZAB item, Evans Property Company's eight-story, 74-unit proposal at 2955 Shattuck Avenue, carries four deed-restricted very-low-income units.

stories.headline: Seattle's U District Draws Blackstone, KKR and Greystar Capital
stories.text: Blackstone, KKR and Greystar have made purpose-built student housing a core institutional holding, and the high-rise wave around the University of Washington is pulling that capital into the Pacific Northwest. The analysis credits U District upzoning and light rail access with unleashing the development wave, drawing an explicit parallel to Austin's West Campus. No transaction volume, cap rates or specific assets are cited.

stories.headline: The Grounds Hits Finishes on 229-Unit Phase One
stories.text: Exterior and interior finishes are underway on the office building and 229-unit residential component of the first phase of The Grounds, the $200 million-plus mixed-use district adjacent to Wake Forest University. No delivery date, lease-up status or preleasing figure was published in the developer's update.

stories.headline: Starwood and Trinitas Form JV, Buy 2,046 Beds Across Three Power 4 Sites
stories.text: Starwood Capital Group and Trinitas Ventures have formed a joint venture that has already acquired three development sites totaling 2,046 beds, serving the University of Oklahoma, the University of Pittsburgh and the University of Wisconsin-Madison. Newmark's student housing division brokered the transaction and arranged the venture. The distinction from this cycle's other headline student housing trades is that these are sites, not stabilized assets. Starwood is putting balance sheet behind ground-up development in three Power 4 markets simultaneously — a development-risk position, not a yield-buy — at a moment when the forward rate path has flipped to hikes. That combination is the notable part. Neither purchase price, per-site bed allocation, targeted delivery dates, construction financing nor the equity split between Starwood and Trinitas has been disclosed. With three sites and 2,046 beds, the implied average is roughly 682 beds per site, but the actual distribution across Norman, Oakland and Madison is unpublished and those are very different land-basis markets. Starwood / Trinitas Joint Venture Venture Starwood Capital / Trinitas Ventures Sites acquired 3 Total beds 2,046 Avg beds per site (derived) ~682 Markets Oklahoma; Pittsburgh; Wisconsin Broker Newmark student housing Purchase price Not disclosed Delivery dates Not disclosed Equity split Not disclosed

stories.headline: Subtext Closes on 565 S. Limestone for 520-Bed Lexington Development
stories.text: Subtext has closed on the land at 565 S. Limestone that will carry EVER Lexington, the 520-bed, 149-unit community detailed in the development section. Groundbreaking is targeted for fall 2026 with delivery in summer 2028. Land price was not disclosed, which is the figure that would let the market calibrate Lexington infill basis against the project's qualified opportunity zone treatment. A QOZ site acquisition with a fall start means the clock on the ten-year holding requirement begins with this closing, not with delivery — a structural constraint on any early exit.

stories.headline: Ann Arbor Sells Kline's Lot to Hines at $31,500 Per Unit for 450-Plus Homes
stories.text: Ann Arbor City Council unanimously approved the sale of the downtown Kline's parking lot to Hines Acquisitions for market-rate housing, priced at $31,500 per unit with a minimum of roughly $14 million. The latest proposal calls for at least 450 units plus about 10,000 square feet of commercial space. A per-unit land price that floats with density rather than a fixed purchase price is the structural feature here — the city captures upside if Hines builds more, and the $14 million floor implies a roughly 444-unit baseline. For a downtown Ann Arbor parcel within walking distance of central campus, $31,500 per unit of land basis is a datapoint worth carrying into any Michigan infill underwriting. The vote proceeded over objections: nearby businesses including The Ark and Blue Llama Jazz Club asked council to postpone finalizing the purchase agreement ahead of the Sept. 8 vote. Unit mix, bed count, whether any units will be student-oriented, and the closing date were not reported.

stories.headline: Albion Evanston Under Contract at ~$126M, or $470K Per Unit
stories.text: Albion Residential is under contract to sell the 268-unit Albion Evanston at 1500 Sherman Ave. to Draper & Kramer for about $126 million — roughly $470,000 per unit — as part of some $335 million in suburban Chicago multifamily trades. Albion built the asset after acquiring the land for about $6 million in 2017 with a $52 million Northwestern Mutual construction mortgage. This is conventional multifamily in Northwestern's market, not purpose-built student housing.

stories.headline: WVU Medicine Closes $6M Purchase of Mon County Health Department
stories.text: Monongalia County finalized the $6 million sale of the county health department property to WVU Medicine after years of on-and-off negotiations, approving a purchase agreement for a replacement site the same day. The health department's relocation and renovation is now estimated at roughly $10 million. Separately, the Morgantown Land Reuse & Preservation Agency accepted six donated parcels, five of them from the estate of Harold Berthy including four in Greenmont.

stories.school_name: University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill
stories.headline: UNC Seeks a P3 Partner for the Carolina North District; Responses Due Oct. 16
stories.text: UNC-Chapel Hill has issued a request for qualifications through the North Carolina Electronic Vendor Portal seeking a public-private development partner for the Carolina North mixed-use district. The solicitation covers housing, research, retail and civic uses on University-owned land and closes Oct. 16, 2026. This is the highest-value piece of intelligence in the edition. Carolina North is a University-controlled land assembly north of the main campus that has sat largely undeveloped through multiple planning cycles; a live RFQ with a hard close date means the university is now selecting a master developer rather than studying one. Housing is named in the scope. Acreage, program size, bed targets, the ground lease structure and the selection timeline after Oct. 16 are not stated in the public solicitation notice. Anyone intending to respond has roughly four weeks from publication and should pull the full RFQ from the eVP portal directly. Read alongside the two new residence halls now under construction on North Campus, UNC is running institutional and private housing tracks in parallel. Carolina North Developer Solicitation Solicitation RFQ — development partner District Carolina North mixed-use Portal NC Electronic Vendor Portal Closes Oct. 16, 2026 Scope Housing, research, retail, civic Land University-owned Acreage Not stated Bed target Not stated Structure Not stated

stories.headline: FSU Confirms Financing on $365M Northwest Campus Project; 1,200 Beds by 2028
stories.text: At the Aug. 28 Board of Trustees meeting, Florida State SVP Kyle Clark said financing is secured for the $365 million Northwest Campus Project, split $284.4 million housing, $40 million dining and $40 million parking. Phase one at Call Street and Chieftan Way includes a 1,200-bed residence hall and a 750-seat dining hall targeted for June 2028, plus a 930-stall parking garage opening in fall 2027. The housing component alone works to roughly $237,000 per bed — the highest institutional per-bed figure in this edition and well above the University of Arizona's Catalina at approximately $190,000. The garage delivering a full year ahead of the residence hall is the phasing detail to note: parking capacity lands in fall 2027, beds in June 2028. Financing structure — whether system revenue bonds, state appropriation, auxiliary revenue or a mix — was not specified in the reporting, and 'financing secured' is the trustees' characterization rather than a documented issuance. FSU Northwest Campus Project Total project $365M Housing $284.4M Dining $40M Parking $40M Phase one beds 1,200 Cost per bed (derived) ~$237,000 Dining seats 750 Garage stalls 930 Garage delivery Fall 2027 Housing delivery June 2028

stories.headline: Ohio State Advances $170M Residence Overhaul Inside a $1.539B Capital Plan
stories.text: Ohio State trustees advanced a $170 million overhaul of student residences and confirmed timing for demolition of the 60-year-old Jones Tower on Lane Avenue. The university reported roughly $14 billion in net assets. The housing work sits inside a 2027 Capital Investment Plan totaling $1.539 billion in facility investments and renovations, including more than $754 million in new funding for campus projects. At that scale the $170 million residence line is about 11 percent of the plan — a renovation-weighted allocation rather than a new-construction commitment. Bed counts affected, the Jones Tower replacement program, and whether any portion of the residence work will be delivered through a P3 rather than university funding have not been published. Ohio State's existing housing portfolio already operates under a long-term concession structure, so the funding path on this tranche matters.

stories.headline: KU Walks Away From a $5.1M-a-Year Master Lease on 504-Bed Naismith Hall
stories.text: The University of Kansas let its master lease on the privately owned, 504-bed Naismith Hall expire in July after determining the beds were not needed once Lewis Hall reopened. KU had been spending an average of $5.1 million per year on the building. The hall will remain closed for renovation. This is the cleanest master-lease termination case study available this year. At $5.1 million annually across 504 beds, KU was paying roughly $10,100 per bed per year to guarantee occupancy it no longer required — and it exited at the first renewal after its own inventory came back online. The owner, 1800 Naismith Drive LLC, bought the building for $28.9 million in 2024, or about $57,300 per bed, and now carries it without the university credit behind it. For anyone underwriting a university master lease as a bond-like cash flow, the operative lesson is that the institution's own capital program is the termination risk. KU continues to house students at Hawker Apartments, Jayhawker Towers and McCarthy Hall. The renovation budget and the owner's re-leasing plan have not been published.

stories.headline: Woda Cooper Starts $51M, 166-Unit Community With Columbus State
stories.text: Woda Cooper broke ground on Opportunity Pointe, a $51 million, 166-unit affordable community in downtown Columbus's Discovery District, in partnership with Columbus State Community College. Ohio Capital Corporation for Housing is providing equity and Ohio Capital Finance Corporation the construction loan. The project serves downtown workers and Columbus State students at roughly $307,000 per unit.

stories.headline: Tempe Reissues Affordable Housing RFQ; Questions Due Sept. 21
stories.text: The City of Tempe issued an updated Request for Qualifications for an affordable housing development, released Sept. 4, 2026 with questions due Sept. 21, 2026. Site, unit count, subsidy structure and submission deadline were not stated in the notice reviewed — respondents should pull the RFQ from the city directly. The reissue lands in the same market absorbing two 750-plus-bed private student deliveries this season.

stories.headline: Tennessee Hits Record 41,287 Students; Campus Services Strain
stories.text: UT Knoxville reported record fall 2026 enrollment of 41,287 students, a 2.1 percent year-over-year increase and a university high, alongside record retention and graduation rates. Student reporting describes strain on parking, class registration and campus services — the operational tell that enrollment growth has outrun capacity. UT has not published a corresponding housing capacity figure or a bed deficit.

stories.headline: UF Opens Jacksonville Graduate Campus, First Step of a $287.5M Buildout
stories.text: The University of Florida cut the ribbon Sept. 9 on a renovated graduate campus at 801 W. Bay St. in Jacksonville, a $4.6 million renovation that is the first step of a $287.5 million campus buildout with construction beginning in 2027. No housing component has been specified in the buildout program. Separately, Gainesville won a $25 million federal Choice Neighborhoods grant aimed at the East University Avenue corridor.

stories.headline: 873-Bed Aspire Reserve Opens 19 Stories Over Northgate at $108M
stories.text: Aspire Reserve began taking residents Aug. 1 at 100 Church Ave. in College Station's Northgate district, delivering 873 beds in 346 units across more than 705,000 square feet. Texas Department of Licensing and Regulation filings put the construction cost at $108 million; the tower broke ground in May 2024. The 19-story building is a joint venture of The Dinerstein Companies, Up Campus Student Living and Harrison Street. At 2.52 beds per unit across 705,000-plus gross square feet, the project computes to roughly 808 gross square feet per bed — a high-rise profile consistent with a structured-parking podium on a constrained Northgate parcel, though the filings do not break out parking area separately. The delivery is the largest single private bed addition in College Station this cycle, and it lands in the same market where the Texas A&M University System has just authorized up to $1.914 billion in FY 2027 bond capacity (see P3 section). No lease-up, occupancy or rent data for the fall term has been published by any of the three venture partners. Aspire Reserve — College Station Address 100 Church Ave. Beds / units 873 / 346 Beds per unit (derived) 2.52 Gross square feet 705,000+ Stories 19 Construction cost (TDLR) $108M Groundbreaking May 2024 First move-ins Aug. 1, 2026 Venture Dinerstein / Up Campus / Harrison St.

stories.headline: Perla Move-In Slips a Second Time; FSU Students Rotated Through Tallahassee Hotels
stories.text: Move-in at the Perla apartments in Tallahassee was pushed past its rescheduled Aug. 28 date — the second delay for the project — after construction work, inspections and final approvals ran long. Florida State students holding signed leases were placed in hotels and then reassigned to different hotels as the schedule slipped again. Some residents told WCTV they were weighing breaking their leases outright. The delay has become a lease-enforcement problem rather than a construction problem: tenants relocated twice are the population most likely to litigate or walk, and the operator has not published a firm certificate-of-occupancy date. Tallahassee absorbed roughly 1,990 new private beds last delivery season across Hub Tallahassee and The Hall. A second failed move-in date at Perla into that supply picture gives displaced students real alternatives — which is the actual downside risk here, not the hotel cost. No revised delivery date, bed count or ownership detail for Perla appears in the reporting.

stories.headline: Wolverine Village Move-In Completes on Schedule Despite Building 4 Warning
stories.text: General move-in to the $649 million Wolverine Village began Aug. 26 and finished as scheduled, closing out a delivery that carried real schedule risk. In July the University of Michigan warned that construction delays at Building 4 could force temporary reassignments; construction finished on time and all residents moved in without relocation. The complex is the first U-M housing to combine geo-exchange heating and cooling, rooftop solar and an all-electric dining hall, and is designed for LEED Platinum certification. It adds 2,300 beds to Central Campus. The contrast with two troubled private sites in the same market this month — Haven on Geddes and the Rambler crane incident below — is what is worth underwriting. Ann Arbor delivered institutional beds on time and private renovation beds late, in the same fall.

stories.headline: Haven on Geddes Renovation Failure Displaces Tenants Across 35 of 68 Units
stories.text: Students with signed leases at Haven on Geddes, 1700 Geddes Ave. in Ann Arbor, arrived to find units unavailable. A City of Ann Arbor email indicated apartments would not be ready until Sept. 14 after contractor permitting errors blocked required inspections; the city later said all outstanding certificates of occupancy had been issued. The city put the property at 68 units with 35 of them under renovation and requiring certificates of occupancy. Owner Hackberry Lane took full accountability for the delays, said it provided hotel accommodations and is covering expenses, and faulted its contractor and property manager AFI. U-M Student Legal Services reported high tenant call volume through the period. The failure mode is specific and repeatable: a mid-renovation asset where certificate-of-occupancy timing was assumed rather than sequenced. Fifty-one percent of the units sat in the renovation scope and none of them could deliver. Neither the acquisition date, the renovation budget nor the contractor's identity has been reported.

stories.headline: Tuscaloosa Sues to Shut Down The Walk Over $102,325 in Unpaid License Taxes
stories.text: The City of Tuscaloosa filed a verified complaint in Tuscaloosa County Circuit Court seeking to immediately halt business operations at The Walk, a student housing complex at 899 12th Street near the University of Alabama, over at least $102,325.02 in unpaid business license taxes. The city says the owners — Delaware entities The Walk ST LLC and The Walk DST — have not paid since April 2025 and did not file a second-quarter 2026 return. The city is asking the court to bar operations until the balance is paid and to place a lien on the property. The filing follows 22 units at the complex being declared uninhabitable by city inspectors in August over mold and bug infestation. A DST wrapper on a distressed near-campus asset with roughly 15 months of unpaid municipal taxes and an active habitability finding is a specific pattern: fractional owners with no operational control, a sponsor that has stopped remitting, and a city willing to seek an operating injunction rather than settle for a lien. Total unit count and current occupancy at The Walk were not reported.

stories.headline: Raleigh Weighs Gilbane Tower That Would Erase 86 Naturally Affordable Units
stories.text: Raleigh City Council took up rezoning case Z-14-26, moving a roughly 3.5-acre Gorman Street site west of NC State from RX-3 to RX-7-CU. Developer Gilbane would demolish the 86-unit Rhyne's Gate Apartments plus adjacent homes to build a seven-story student housing tower of about 300 units, with rezoning flexibility permitting up to 483 units. The public-benefit package is thin and worth reading closely: no on-site affordable units, an $80,000 voluntary payment to the city's Affordable Housing Fund at the roughly 300-unit program, 120 days' notice for existing tenants and $2,500 in relocation assistance each. The Planning Commission recommended approval in June 2026. The case cites NC State enrollment growth from 36,304 in fall 2020 to 39,259 in fall 2025. The gap between the 300-unit program and the 483-unit entitlement ceiling is the number to watch — a 61 percent density option retained without a corresponding increase in the affordable contribution. No bed count, construction budget or delivery date has been published.

stories.headline: Tuscaloosa Council Overrides Planning Commission on Hargrove Road Rezoning, 4-2
stories.text: The Tuscaloosa City Council voted 4-2 on Sept. 1 to rezone roughly 4.6 acres at 3311 and 3327 Hargrove Road East from SFR-1 to SFR-4, reversing a 6-3 Planning and Zoning Commission recommendation against the change. A previously rejected 24-townhome plan from developer Clay Smith and Longleaf Engineering must return to the commission with an updated traffic study before construction can proceed. The sequence — a council override of a 6-3 negative recommendation, with the traffic study deferred to a second commission review — is the procedural precedent worth logging for anyone entitling in Tuscaloosa.

stories.headline: Charlottesville Pipeline Reaches 3,185 Beds by Fall 2027
stories.text: The University of Virginia's Ivy Corridor student housing project carries a $160 million budget and is on track for fall 2027 completion, adding about 800 beds on Grounds. Three off-Grounds complexes are under construction simultaneously — Adelaide, VERVE Charlottesville and Blume on Ivy — which together will add a combined 2,385 beds by the same fall. That is 3,185 beds landing in one academic year in a market of Charlottesville's size, with the institutional and private tranches delivering concurrently rather than sequenced. Separately, Darden's 216-unit, 338-bed on-Grounds MBA complex reached full height in February and remains on track for 2027-28, with rental rates to be set by the Board of Visitors this fall and units assigned by lottery.

stories.headline: Oxford Campus Construction: Kincannon 2027, West Row in Demolition
stories.text: Two Greystar-partnered Ole Miss dormitories are moving on separate clocks. The Kincannon site is on track for August 2027 delivery, while West Row is in demolition through September ahead of an August 2028 completion. Greek house and other campus facility construction is running alongside both.

stories.headline: Crane Collapses Scaffolding at 17-Story Rambler Site
stories.text: A crane struck and collapsed scaffolding on the 13th floor of Rambler, a 17-story student high-rise under construction across from East Quadrangle in Ann Arbor and projected to open fall 2027. General contractor Turner Construction reported no injuries; the City of Ann Arbor requested a cause determination and a prevention plan.

stories.headline: Columbus Leasing Season Now Runs 8 to 12 Months Ahead of Move-In
stories.text: Off-campus leasing in Columbus's University District is running eight to twelve months ahead of occupancy, with students signing 2026-27 leases as early as December 2025 and second-years already hunting 2027-28 product. Ohio State's Off-Campus and Commuter Student Engagement office runs an off-campus housing network and an annual property-company survey with Student Legal Services and City of Columbus departments.

stories.headline: Rambler Tempe Delivers 829 Beds on Apache Boulevard
stories.text: Move-ins began July 24 at Rambler Tempe, a 14-story, 552,400-square-foot community at 1020 E. Apache Blvd. near Arizona State. LV Collective developed the project with Kayne Anderson Real Estate, delivering 289 units and 829 beds — about 2.87 beds per unit and roughly 666 gross square feet per bed, both derived from the reported figures.

stories.headline: Hub Boulder Opens With 404 Beds in Core Spaces' 6,000-Bed Slate
stories.text: Core Spaces' 2026 delivery slate includes Hub Boulder at CU Boulder, a 96-unit, 404-bed community — roughly 4.2 beds per unit. The developer says it opened about 6,000 beds nationally for the 2026-27 academic year. The national figure is the developer's own and has not been independently verified.

stories.headline: Standard at Los Angeles Completes at 1,261 Beds
stories.text: Landmark Properties' Standard at Los Angeles near USC is complete. The eight-story building holds 429 furnished units ranging from studios to five-bedroom plans, 1,261 beds — roughly 2.94 beds per unit — and more than 13,000 square feet of ground-floor retail.

stories.headline: New South Hall Opens Without a Working Mailroom
stories.text: Purdue's new South Hall opened for fall 2026 without a functioning mailroom, sending residents to neighboring Hillenbrand Hall to collect packages. Students and staff also reported the building's elevators frequently out of service. No remediation date has been published.

stories.headline: Scion and Ares Buy 2,316-Bed, Four-Community Portfolio for $435M
stories.text: The Scion Group and Ares Management acquired a four-community, 2,316-bed student housing portfolio in Texas, Tennessee and Georgia from Schenk+ for approximately $435 million. One of the assets serves the University of Georgia in Athens. The pricing works to roughly $187,800 per bed across the portfolio. It is the joint venture's second portfolio purchase of 2026, following a $910 million, 12-property transaction in May — putting the pair at about $1.345 billion of student housing acquisitions in a single calendar year. Neither a cap rate, individual asset allocation nor debt structure has been disclosed. For sellers of Power 4 portfolio product, the read is that a single joint venture has absorbed sixteen properties in four months at scale. That is a bid-side depth signal, not a pricing comp. Scion / Ares — Schenk+ Portfolio Purchase price ~$435M Beds 2,316 Communities 4 Price per bed (derived) ~$187,800 States TX, TN, GA Seller Schenk+ Prior 2026 JV buy $910M / 12 properties (May) 2026 JV total (derived) ~$1.345B Cap rate Not disclosed

stories.headline: Landmark JV Acquires 642-Bed Domain at Oxford
stories.text: Landmark Properties, in joint venture with Liberty Mutual Investments and Peninsula Investments, acquired The Domain at Oxford — a 642-bed, 216-unit community near Ole Miss, or about 2.97 beds per unit. Landmark cited record Ole Miss enrollment and an undersupplied on- and off-campus market as the thesis. The buy lands in the same window in which the Mississippi IHL Board approved phase two of the university's 850-bed housing P3 (see P3 section). An acquirer underwriting undersupply in a market where the institution has just committed to 850 new beds for 2028 is taking the view that enrollment growth outruns the institutional pipeline. Purchase price and cap rate were not disclosed.

stories.headline: UCLA Pays $8.5M for Sawtelle Co-Living Conversion
stories.text: UCLA bought a co-living building at 1775 Beloit Ave. in Sawtelle for $8.5 million in August and will convert it to graduate student housing. The purchase follows university acquisitions on Wilshire, Venice and Berryman. Bed count and conversion budget were not reported.

stories.headline: Six-Unit Tucson Asset Trades at a 7.77% Cap
stories.text: 638 E Lester LLC, an SVP Holdings affiliate, acquired the six-unit, 22-bed Lester Student Housing Apartments near the University of Arizona for $1.35 million — roughly $61,400 per bed. The sale closed Aug. 21, 2026 at a 7.77 percent cap rate, the only disclosed cap rate in this edition.

stories.headline: JPI Closes on $150M Jefferson Watts Near Duke Medical Center
stories.text: JPI acquired the $150 million, 398-unit and 42-townhome Jefferson Watts near Duke University Medical Center in July 2026, part of a broader Durham multifamily wave that also includes the 267-unit Vara Trinity Park, where construction began in March 2026. Separately, Northpoint Development is seeking to rezone 13 acres off North Roxboro Street for 248 apartments and 73 townhomes; a second neighborhood meeting was held Sept. 1. These are conventional multifamily, not purpose-built student housing.

stories.headline: IHL Approves Phase Two of Ole Miss P3: 850 Beds on 15 Acres, No University Debt
stories.text: The Mississippi Institutions of Higher Learning Board approved phase two of the University of Mississippi's student housing public-private partnership — roughly 850 beds on 15 acres at West Row, delivered through a ground lease with PRG-Oxford Properties. Completion is expected July 2028. The structure is the part worth reading. Student fees cover rent and maintenance, and the university is expressly not responsible for project debt. That is the off-balance-sheet ground-lease template institutions have been moving toward, and it puts credit risk on the developer and the fee stream rather than on state appropriation or system revenue bonds. West Row is currently in demolition through September per campus reporting, so site work and board approval are running concurrently. Total project cost, ground rent, the fee schedule and the debt terms were not disclosed in the reporting. Ole Miss Housing P3 — Phase Two Beds ~850 Site West Row, 15 acres Structure Ground lease Developer PRG-Oxford Properties Completion July 2028 Rent / maintenance source Student fees University debt exposure None per IHL approval Project cost Not disclosed Ground rent Not disclosed

stories.headline: Utah Has 900 Empty Beds Weeks After Its P3 Delivered 1,450
stories.text: More than 900 of the University of Utah's 6,946 on-campus beds are sitting vacant this fall — about 15 percent — a reversal from last year, when the system ran full with waitlists. The vacancy appeared within weeks of Trailhead, delivered through an American Campus Communities public-private partnership, adding nearly 1,450 beds. University officials attribute the swing to new off-campus supply and softer rents changing student demand. Whatever the cause, the sequencing is the lesson: a P3 sized against a waitlisted market delivered into a market that had already re-priced, and the vacancy is now a live variable in the next phase of the university's P3 housing program. For anyone underwriting a Power 4 institutional partnership, this is the cleanest available example of waitlist demand failing to survive a single delivery cycle. Neither the university nor ACC has published Trailhead-specific occupancy, the rent structure, or whether the next phase is being resized.

stories.headline: Florida Issues $245M UF Dormitory Revenue Bonds, Series 2026A
stories.text: The State of Florida Board of Governors issued $245 million in Dormitory Revenue Bonds, Series 2026A, dated Aug. 20, 2026, to finance new University of Florida housing on the site of the demolished Trusler, Simpson and Graham halls. Annual debt service runs about $17.8 million, secured by net revenues of the UF housing system — a system-revenue pledge, not a project-specific or fee-backed structure, which is the opposite of the Ole Miss ground-lease approach above. Bed count, project cost and delivery date for the replacement housing are not stated in the offering document reviewed.

stories.headline: Regents Put a 2,000-Bed Madison Hall Into the 2027-29 Budget Request
stories.text: The University of Wisconsin Board of Regents unanimously passed a 2027-29 biennial budget request on Aug. 20 that includes a $2 billion UW System capital budget funding a roughly 2,000-bed new residence hall at UW-Madison, along with demolition of Mosse Humanities. The request now goes to the state legislature after the Nov. 3 general election — the operative timing risk. This is a request, not an authorization: a 2,000-bed Madison delivery does not exist as a funded project until the legislature acts, and no delivery date, project budget or site has been published.

stories.headline: A&M System Authorizes $1.9B in FY 2027 Bond Capacity
stories.text: Texas A&M System regents authorized up to $1.914 billion in bond capacity for fiscal year 2027 — the debt envelope funding system-wide capital construction including residence hall and campus projects. The authorization is a ceiling, not an allocation; no housing-specific carve-out has been published.

stories.headline: Kentucky Opens 649-Bed Kirwan-Blanding Hall
stories.text: The University of Kentucky opened Kirwan-Blanding Hall, a 649-bed residence hall, as part of a campus transformation the university says has drawn more than $8 billion in facilities investment over 15 years. Project cost for Kirwan-Blanding specifically was not disclosed.

stories.headline: UW Tacoma Master Plan Adds 400-500 Beds, Targets Doubled Enrollment
stories.text: UW Tacoma's BIG-designed campus master plan targets growth from 5,000 to 10,000 students and adds a 400- to 500-bed traditional residence hall plus a dining hall, both slated to open in 2029. This is the Tacoma campus, not Seattle — a market with essentially no existing purpose-built student housing base.

stories.headline: IU Applications Up 9.6% to 81,000; Systemwide Enrollment Near 90,000
stories.text: Indiana University's Aug. 31 census put total systemwide enrollment near 90,000, with new undergraduate enrollment at a record 16,911 across the system. IU Bloomington took more than 81,000 applications, up 9.6 percent from last year's record, and enrolled its second-largest class ever — 43 percent of the incoming class holding a 4.0 GPA.

stories.headline: Notre Dame Opens Coyle and Grojean Halls at ~$49M Each
stories.text: Two new university-owned residence halls opened for 2026-27: Coyle Hall at 82,428 square feet and 258 beds, and Therese Mary Grojean Hall at 275 beds, replacing Fisher and Pangborn Halls at roughly $49.15 million each. Both are university-funded rather than P3 structures. The gross addition is 533 beds; the bed counts of the two demolished halls were not published, so the net figure cannot be computed.

stories.headline: USC Approaches 42,000 on Largest Freshman Class in School History
stories.text: University of South Carolina officials say total enrollment is approaching 42,000 with a freshman class of nearly 8,000 first-year students, the largest in university history. Fall classes began Aug. 18. Arkansas separately opened fall 2026 with a record incoming class above 7,100 and a record 3.87 average incoming GPA against total enrollment near 34,000.

stories.headline: Michigan Opens $649M Wolverine Village, Adding 2,300 Central Campus Beds
stories.text: The University of Michigan opened Wolverine Village for fall 2026 move-in, a five-residence-hall complex on Central Campus carrying a $649 million price tag and adding 2,300 undergraduate beds — the largest single institutional bed addition in the Ann Arbor market this cycle. The university puts the increase at roughly 25 percent of undergraduate housing capacity and says the added inventory lets it guarantee Central Campus space for first-year students. The complex includes an all-electric dining hall seating more than 800. A potential second phase remains in development and has not yet gone to the Board of Regents, so no bed count, budget or delivery date exists for Phase 2 on the public record. For off-campus owners, the relevant question is absorption: 2,300 institutional beds landing in a single fall is a supply event that private operators in Ann Arbor will underwrite against for at least two lease-ups. The university has not published a first-year live-on requirement change alongside the opening. Wolverine Village — Ann Arbor Total project cost $649M Beds added 2,300 Residence halls 5 Undergrad capacity increase ~25% Dining hall seats 800+ Phase 2 status Under development; not approved

stories.headline: Auburn Council Clears Chateau, LeMans Square Conversion Over Displacement Objections
stories.text: Auburn City Council on Aug. 18 approved conditional-use redevelopment of the Chateau and LeMans Square apartment complexes, clearing the way for larger market-rate, student-oriented product branded Charter Auburn Student Housing on two of the last large naturally-occurring affordable sites near campus. Local reporting puts roughly 238 lower-income households in the path of the conversion. That figure, not the bed count, is what makes this entitlement instructive: Auburn approved a student-housing upzoning while the displacement math was on the record, and the conditions attached to the approval are the template the next applicant in Auburn will be measured against. Neither the replacement unit count nor a construction start date has been published. Separately, the university has been adding managed inventory through master leases with private off-campus communities — see this edition's P3 section — meaning Auburn's institutional and private supply lines are moving at the same time in a market with limited entitled land near the core.

stories.headline: Columbia Advances Bedroom Moratorium in Six Neighborhoods Near USC
stories.text: Columbia City Council voted unanimously on Aug. 18 to advance an ordinance barring added bedrooms and parking expansions on multifamily homes in six historic neighborhoods around the University of South Carolina campus, citing conversion pressure from student renters. The moratorium targets the bedroom-adding strategy that underwrites small-scale student conversions — the per-bed math breaks if the bedroom count is frozen. Owners holding house-scale product in the affected districts should treat renovation-driven bed growth as unavailable until the ordinance's term and final adoption language are published; neither has been reported.

stories.headline: Texas Tech Regents Approve 19th Street Hall as Enrollment Passes 45,800
stories.text: Texas Tech opened the fall term with 45,812 students — past 45,000 for the first time — on a record 9,552 first-time-in-college class and a fifth straight year of growth. On-campus housing is running roughly 1,000 beds short of demand. Regents have approved construction of a new residence hall on 19th Street that will eventually replace the Horn/Knapp complex, for a net gain of about 1,300 beds. Because the delivery replaces existing inventory, the near-term relief is smaller than the headline number and the swing year — when Horn/Knapp comes offline before the new hall stabilizes — is the window off-campus Lubbock owners should be underwriting. No construction budget or delivery date has been published. Lubbock Demand Snapshot Fall 2026 enrollment 45,812 First-time-in-college class 9,552 Consecutive growth years 5 On-campus shortfall ~1,000 beds 19th St. hall — net gain ~1,300 beds The Wyatt (McGrath) occupancy 100% leased The Wyatt rent growth YoY 4.23%, no concessions

stories.headline: Tallahassee Absorbs 1,990 New Private Beds in One Delivery Season
stories.text: Core Spaces opened Hub Tallahassee, a 367-unit, 1,316-bed community near Florida State, one of six properties totaling about 6,000 beds the developer delivered nationally ahead of the 2026-27 year. The company says the Tallahassee build came in under budget and at least six weeks ahead of move-in. In the same season, a Portman and 908 Group joint venture completed The Hall, a 191-unit, 674-bed community with 7,689 square feet of retail and 425 parking spaces. Together the two deliveries put 1,990 private beds into the FSU market in a single lease-up. Neither developer has published lease-up or rent data for the fall term.

stories.headline: Athens Commission Backs 374-Bedroom College Avenue Project, Trestle Fix Required
stories.text: The Athens-Clarke County planning commission recommended approval of a 156-unit, 374-bedroom mixed housing project on a former concrete plant off College Avenue, with a condition requiring the developer to resolve a low rail trestle before occupancy. The full commission vote was set for Sept. 1. The trestle condition is the cost item to watch — infrastructure remediation tied to a certificate of occupancy is a schedule risk, not just a budget line. Athens commissioners separately rejected a broad accessory-dwelling-unit allowance while approving code changes permitting smaller houses, and about 150 residents turned out against the Georgia Square Mall overlay, which faces a Sept. 3 planning vote and an Oct. 6 commission vote with construction not starting before October 2027.

stories.headline: Demolition Starts on Delayed 10-Story West Mifflin Street Project
stories.text: Demolition was expected to begin the week of Aug. 24 at the 600 block of West Mifflin Street in Madison, clearing the way for a 10-story student housing development that had been stalled roughly a year. Two existing apartment buildings come down; the Wiedenbeck-Dobelin Warehouse, a designated Madison landmark, is preserved in the plan. The one-year slip between entitlement and demolition is the datapoint for downtown Madison underwriting — landmark-adjacent sites in the district carry schedule risk that does not show up in the zoning approval. Unit and bed counts for the project were not reported.

stories.headline: Carpenters Strike Halts Work at Green Street Hub Site in Champaign
stories.text: Members of Carpenters Local 243 went on strike at 201 E. Green St., the future Hub On Campus student apartment site in Champaign, protesting the use of out-of-state contractors. The action has delayed construction. Labor actions on campus-core towers are a delivery-date risk that rarely appears in pipeline reporting until a lease-up is already at stake. No revised delivery date, bed count or resolution timeline has been published.

stories.headline: $51M Opportunity Pointe Breaks Ground in Discovery District
stories.text: Columbus State and Woda Cooper broke ground on Opportunity Pointe, a $51 million, 166-unit affordable and student housing development in downtown Columbus's Discovery District. Rents are set from $480 to $1,400, with completion expected by the end of 2027.

stories.headline: Alta Plans 675-Bed SOMI Walk in Coral Gables
stories.text: Alta Development, led by Henry Pino, is building SOMI Walk, a 16-story student housing project in Coral Gables with 173 apartments and 675 beds. The University of Miami is separately running a multi-phase on-campus program that its reporting credits with adding more than 3,400 beds.

stories.headline: SK Hynix Breaks Ground on $4B West Lafayette Plant
stories.text: SK hynix ceremonially broke ground in West Lafayette on a $4 billion AI memory chip packaging facility tied to a Purdue partnership, with cleanroom operations targeted for 2028. Purdue separately opened the eight-story South Hall, adding nearly 900 beds; University Residences has grown from about 12,000 to 18,000 beds, with roughly 17,300 expected in West Lafayette this year.

stories.headline: UO Names Maple Hall, 870 Beds Due Fall 2027
stories.text: Oregon permanently named two residence halls: Cedar Hall, opened in 2023 with about 700 beds, and Maple Hall, a seven-story, 219,700-square-foot, 870-bed building under construction on East 17th Avenue for fall 2027. Maple is financed primarily through revenue bonds and housing carryforward funds.

stories.headline: Core Spaces Reports 6,000 Beds Delivered, 54,000 in Pipeline
stories.text: Core Spaces said it delivered roughly 6,000 beds across six Power 4 markets for the 2026 academic year and listed Hub Clemson in a 2027 delivery pipeline the company sizes at nearly 54,000 beds in development nationally. The pipeline figure is the developer's own and has not been independently verified.

stories.headline: Landmark Delivers 1,261-Bed Standard at Los Angeles
stories.text: Landmark Properties delivered The Standard at Los Angeles, a 429-unit, 1,261-bed community at 3900 South Figueroa St., three-tenths of a mile from USC. The eight-story building carries more than 13,000 square feet of ground-floor retail and a rooftop pool; HED designed it and Landmark Construction was general contractor.

stories.headline: CU Boulder Opens First New Hall Since 2019
stories.text: CU Boulder cut the ribbon on Code Talker Hall, a 332-bed apartment-style residence hall for non-first-year undergraduates. It is the campus's first new residence hall since 2019, all-electric and targeting LEED Gold.

stories.headline: Subtext Buys 565 South Limestone for 520-Bed EVER Lexington
stories.text: Subtext has acquired the land at 565 South Limestone in Lexington, directly across from the University of Kentucky's main pedestrian entrance, for EVER Lexington — a 520-bed, 149-unit community. The venture pairs Subtext with FrontRange Capital and Larson Capital Management. Groundbreaking is expected in fall 2026 with completion targeted for summer 2028, putting delivery into the 2028-29 academic year. The purchase price was not disclosed in the reporting. At 3.5 beds per unit, the mix reads as a bedroom-weighted, pedestrian-entrance product — the site is the constraint that matters in Lexington, where core-adjacent parcels facing the main campus gate rarely trade. EVER Lexington Address 565 South Limestone Beds / units 520 / 149 Beds per unit ~3.5 Partners FrontRange Capital; Larson Capital Groundbreaking Fall 2026 Completion target Summer 2028 Purchase price Not disclosed

stories.headline: Bloomington Housing Authority Seeks 924 Units to Block Student Conversions
stories.text: The Bloomington Housing Authority is moving to buy five apartment complexes totaling 924 units this fall, explicitly to preserve mid-level workforce housing before developers can demolish and rebuild the sites as luxury student product near the Indiana University campus. The authority plans to fund the purchase with up to $100 million in revenue bonds. A public-sector buyer bidding against student housing capital at this scale is the notable structure — 924 units taken out of the redevelopment pool changes the Bloomington supply outlook more than any single project would. Neither a purchase price nor a closing date has been published.

stories.headline: Landmark Acquires 642-Bed Domain at Oxford
stories.text: Landmark Properties acquired The Domain at Oxford, a 642-bed purpose-built student housing community about one mile south of the Ole Miss campus. Price terms were not disclosed in this report.

stories.headline: Greystar Sells 252-Unit Milo in West Raleigh
stories.text: JLL Capital Markets closed the sale of Milo, a 252-unit community on 8.13 acres at 821 Hanbury Way in West Raleigh, representing seller Greystar; the buyer was Milo Apartments LLC. JLL marketed proximity to NC State, Duke and UNC-Chapel Hill. The price was not disclosed.

stories.headline: State College Reaches $15.75M Deal for Addison Court
stories.text: State College Borough Council was set to consider a $15.75 million purchase of Arnold Addison Court from developer PrimeCore, which had considered razing the low-income senior building for student housing. The borough would lease the property back to preserve it for 40 more years, and has asked neighboring townships to contribute — Patton Township committed $5,000 on Aug. 19.

stories.headline: Hamilton County Sells Corryville Site for $3M
stories.text: Hamilton County commissioners voted Aug. 27 to sell a 3.2-acre property at 250/264 William Howard Taft Road in Corryville for $3 million to Bethany House, which will work with developer Urban Sites on an 89-unit affordable housing project in the University of Cincinnati's adjacent submarket.

stories.headline: East Chase Apartments Trade for $59M
stories.text: An affiliate of Enfield Capital Partners paid $59 million — $139,150 per unit — for the 424-unit East Chase Apartments in Louisville, acquired from Sentinel Real Estate Corp. Cushman & Wakefield brokered. Conventional multifamily, not purpose-built student housing.

stories.headline: Evanston Sells 801 Main to CityPads for $1.5M
stories.text: Evanston alders took up the $1.5 million sale of city-owned land at 801-811 Main St. and 916-918 Sherman Ave. to Chicago-based CityPads, the sole RFP respondent. The city paid $735,000 for the site in fall 2025 using Chicago-Main TIF funds. CityPads plans 64 apartments with ground-floor retail plus 15 townhomes, including 12 affordable units.

stories.headline: UT Dedicates $160M Torchbearer Hall, Phase II of RISE Housing P3
stories.text: Tennessee leadership dedicated Torchbearer Hall on Aug. 17 — a nine-story, 1,028-bed residence hall next to Circle Park delivered as Phase II of the university's RISE Real Estate housing public-private partnership. The $160 million hall took its first residents earlier in the month. The delivery lands against a fall enrollment expected to top 41,000 for the first time in university history, on more than 7,200 first-year students drawn from nearly 70,000 first-year applications. UT has framed the on-campus expansion as necessary to keep pace with that growth rather than as a replacement of existing beds. For Knoxville's off-campus market, the read is that a P3 structure is delivering institutional beds at roughly the same rate enrollment is adding demand — the university's own reporting does not indicate a live-on requirement change, so the returning-student pool remains the private market's book. Torchbearer Hall — Knoxville Project cost $160M Beds 1,028 Stories 9 P3 structure RISE Real Estate, Phase II Dedication Aug. 17, 2026 Fall 2026 enrollment 41,000+ (record) First-year students 7,200+

stories.headline: Oregon Delays Phase 2 of $235M Housing Plan Amid $65M Budget Cut
stories.text: Oregon's two-building, $235 million Next Generation Housing Development Plan has split: Phase 1, roughly 800 beds plus dining, is about a year from completion, while Phase 2 has been pushed past fall 2028. The program is funded entirely by room and board revenue through loans and bonds — a structure that ties delivery directly to occupancy. That funding model is under strain. The university detailed plans to cut $65 million after a decline in out-of-state enrollment, projecting 1,888 nonresident first-year students, roughly 400 to 500 fewer than the prior year, with formal budget proposals due in October.

stories.headline: Auburn Adds Managed Beds Through Master Leases After Hall Closure
stories.text: Auburn University has secured master leases with private off-campus apartment communities to expand its managed housing stock following a Cambridge Hall closure caused by water damage, according to reporting that also ties the move to zoning updates reshaping off-campus housing near campus. Master leasing is the fastest institutional response to a sudden bed loss and the most direct competitive signal a private owner can get: the university becomes the counterparty rather than the competitor. The communities involved, lease terms, bed counts and durations were not disclosed in the reporting.

stories.headline: FSU Trustees Take Up Campus Master Plan Amendment
stories.text: The FSU Board of Trustees Finance and Business Committee considered an action item at its Aug. 27 meeting to amend the university's Campus Master Plan, alongside approval of the 2026-27 Fixed Capital Outlay Budget. Master plan amendments are the earliest public signal of an institution's housing and land intentions, and they move before any RFP. The agenda does not specify the substance of the amendment; the housing implications cannot be determined from the posted document alone.

stories.headline: Syracuse to Phase Out South Campus With Three New Halls
stories.text: Three new North Campus residence halls — on Waverly Avenue, Comstock Avenue and at 544 University Place — are scheduled for completion in August 2027 and will eventually phase out South Campus housing. Construction has closed Comstock between Waverly and Marshall for the academic year. Bed counts for the three halls were not published.

stories.headline: Vanderbilt Advances Peabody, Central Neighborhood Colleges
stories.text: Vanderbilt updated construction on the Peabody Residential College, which will house roughly 187 first-year students, and on the Central Neighborhood Residential Colleges project adding three residential colleges that open in phases beginning in 2028-29.

stories.headline: OU Opens 580-Bed South Hall on Sixth Straight Record Class
stories.text: Oklahoma welcomed a record 6,437 freshmen in the Class of 2030, its sixth consecutive record year, and opened South Hall this fall with about 580 new beds. The university separately launched a partnership with Housr to centralize off-campus housing search for students.

stories.headline: Core Spaces Breaks Ground on 2,201-Bed Northgate Tower Pair
stories.text: Core Spaces has started construction on Hub College Station, a 2,201-bed, 570-unit development spread across two seven-story buildings in the Northgate District, the single largest purpose-built student housing start recorded in the College Station market this cycle. Delivery is scheduled ahead of the 2028–29 academic year. Pacific Life provided construction financing. Treehouse Construction is general contractor and Antunovich Associates is design architect. The bed count implies roughly 3.9 beds per unit, a shared-bedroom-weighted mix consistent with Core's Hub product in other Power 4 markets. The start lands in the same month College Station's council rezoned roughly 47 acres elsewhere in the city for multifamily and middle housing, and while Teeple Partners broke ground on a second student-oriented phase along the Innovation Corridor — three separate supply events inside a single submarket inside a single month. College Station Pipeline Snapshot Hub College Station — beds 2,201 Hub College Station — units 570 Buildings / stories 2 @ 7 stories Delivery AY 2028–29 Oaks Reserve (Teeple) — units 312 Oaks Reserve master plan 53 acres / ~1,000 units Aug. 13 council rezonings 12.43 ac + ~35 ac

stories.headline: Wolverine Village Opens at $649M — First Central Campus First-Year Housing Since 1963
stories.text: The University of Michigan has opened Wolverine Village, the first Central Campus residence hall complex built for first-year students since Oxford Houses delivered in 1963. The reported project cost is $649 million. The scale of the delivery is a function of how far the university's housing coverage had slipped: coverage cited in reporting on the opening fell from 40 percent of enrollment in 2004 to 28 percent in 2023. University Housing now expects the largest on-campus resident population in its history this fall, with more than 10,000 undergraduates moving in between Aug. 26 and Aug. 30. A second phase is already assembled. Reporting cites a $75 million acquisition of 49 properties for the follow-on site — a land-banking pattern worth watching for private operators underwriting Ann Arbor, where institutional bed additions of this size directly compress the off-campus absorption runway. Ann Arbor Supply Watch Wolverine Village cost $649M Prior Central Campus first-year hall 1963 U-M bed coverage 2004 → 2023 40% → 28% Phase 2 land assembly $75M / 49 properties Fall move-in window Aug. 26–30

stories.headline: Ole Miss Pushes $1.3 Billion Building Program as Kincannon Tops Out
stories.text: The University of Mississippi reports 170 construction projects underway with a combined value of roughly $1.3 billion. On the housing side, the north building at the Kincannon site has reached its fifth and top floor, with occupancy set for August 2027; modular units for the south building are due to be installed within six weeks, according to trade coverage of the program. Demolition has begun at West Row Student Housing, clearing the way for an August 2028 delivery. Taken together, the two sites give Ole Miss a staggered two-year on-campus bed schedule — relevant for anyone underwriting Oxford off-campus product with 2027 or 2028 lease-ups.

stories.headline: Torchbearer Hall Delivers 1,024 Beds; Second P3 Phase Follows This Fall
stories.text: Tennessee has opened Torchbearer Hall, a nine-story, 1,024-bed suite-style residence hall adjacent to Circle Park, as part of its fall 2026 facilities slate. The university says a second phase of roughly 1,020 public-private partnership beds remains on schedule to open this fall as well. That is on the order of 2,000 institutional beds landing in Knoxville within a single academic year, driven by rising enrollment and undergraduate demand to live on campus. Private owners in the Cumberland Avenue corridor should expect the freshman and sophomore capture rate to move against them for the 2026–27 and 2027–28 lease-ups. Knoxville Institutional Beds, Fall 2026 Torchbearer Hall beds 1,024 Stories 9 Second P3 phase beds ~1,020 Combined AY 2026–27 add ~2,044

stories.school_name: University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill
stories.headline: UNC Fences Jackson Hall for Demolition Ahead of 730-Bed Replacement
stories.text: North Carolina has fenced off Jackson Hall and the North Campus Recreation Complex ahead of demolition, clearing the site for two new residence hall buildings totaling more than 730 undergraduate beds. Construction is estimated to finish in fall 2028, with a groundbreaking ceremony planned once the site is cleared. The teardown removes an administrative building rather than beds, so the project is a net add to North Campus inventory on a 2028 timeline — late enough that Chapel Hill private deliveries in 2026 and 2027 lease into an unchanged institutional supply picture.

stories.headline: Georgia Tech Opens 862-Bed Peterson Hall, Its First Traditional Dorm in Nearly 70 Years
stories.text: The 862-bed Bud and Val Peterson Hall has opened on the west side of the Georgia Tech campus along Northside Drive, built to Passive House standards and targeting LEED Gold. The $117 million project was approved by the University System of Georgia Board of Regents in February 2023, with $102.3 million financed through bonds issued by Georgia Tech Facilities Inc. in August 2024. The bond structure is the detail worth noting: roughly 87 percent of project cost carried on an affiliated-foundation issuance rather than a private P3 balance sheet, a structure the USG system has favored for on-campus first-year product. (Aug. 2024) $102.3M Bond share of cost ~87% Regents approval Feb. 2023 Sustainability Passive House / LEED Gold target

stories.headline: Auburn Council Clears Two-Year Redevelopment of LeMans Square, Chateau Apartments
stories.text: The Auburn City Council has approved a two-year redevelopment of the LeMans Square and Chateau apartments near campus. Construction is tentatively set to begin in June 2027, with new tenants targeted for 2029. Residents raised displacement concerns at the hearing, and Mayor Ron Anders has said he is seeking solutions for potentially displaced low-income tenants. The entitlement is approved; the political risk has shifted to the relocation question, which is the variable most likely to affect the construction start date.

stories.headline: Athens Planners Table Mall Overlay That Would Double Bedroom Density
stories.text: Athens planners held off on the biggest density question in front of them this cycle. On Aug. 6 the Athens-Clarke County Planning Commission tabled a Leaven Group request for a special overlay at Georgia Square Mall that would lift the allowable multifamily standard from 25 bedrooms per acre to 50 — a straight doubling. A 550-bedroom building proposed at 660 W. Broad St. was heard at the same session. A tabling is not a denial, but the pairing matters: Athens is being asked to approve a density doubling at a regional mall site and a 550-bedroom infill building in the same hearing cycle. Separately, the county commission removed the 1,000-square-foot minimum floor area rule while voting 7–3 to keep kitchen-equipped accessory dwelling units banned, with one commissioner citing concern that student housing operators would exploit an ADU allowance.

stories.headline: College Station Rezones ~47 Acres for Multifamily and Middle Housing
stories.text: College Station's council rezoned 12.43 acres at Rock Prairie Road and Old Wellborn Road to multifamily for student housing on Aug. 13, and rezoned roughly 35 acres at Victoria Avenue and William D. Fitch Parkway to multifamily and middle housing. Council also recommended a $0.530254 tax rate, between the no-new-revenue rate of $0.506934 and the voter-approval rate of $0.537862, with a public hearing set for Aug. 27. Council separately declined, for now, to tighten impervious-cover rules in the Bee Creek basin after staff noted redevelopment near campus under the new middle-housing regulations could push impervious cover from 55 percent to 75 percent — a deferred entitlement risk rather than a resolved one.

stories.headline: Pitt Starts Enabling Work on 450-Bed Hall, Its First Since 2013
stories.text: Enabling work began in June at Fifth and Ruskin avenues on Pitt's first new residence hall since 2013. The city Planning Commission approved the nine-story, 450-bed L-shaped building on July 28, with an anticipated fall 2028 opening. Oakland's constrained land supply makes a 450-bed institutional add material to the submarket, though the 2028 timing leaves two full lease-up seasons before the beds compete.

stories.headline: Perla's 614 Beds Slip to Aug. 28; FSU Students Housed in Hotels
stories.text: Delivery delays at Perla, a seven-story, 614-bed community across from Florida State, pushed move-in from Aug. 21 to Aug. 28 and left students in nearby hotels including Hotel Indigo. Construction crews were still on site as leases were scheduled to begin. The operator's remedy package — 200 percent per-day rent credits, a $50 daily food per diem, Uber gift cards and storage reimbursement — is a useful data point for anyone modeling delay-risk reserves on a 2026 or 2027 delivery. On a 614-bed asset, a week of doubled per-day credits plus per diems is a real first-year NOI event, and it arrives before a single rent check clears.

stories.headline: Oregon Names $160M, 870-Bed Maple Hall in Next Generation Housing Phase 1
stories.text: Oregon announced Aug. 18 that its previously unnamed residence hall north of Hayward Field is now Cedar Hall, and that the hall currently under construction will be named Maple Hall. Maple Hall is an estimated $160 million, seven-story, 870-bed building in Phase 1 of the Next Generation Housing Development plan, targeted for fall 2027. At roughly $184,000 per bed on the stated figures, Maple Hall is a useful institutional cost comparable for Big Ten on-campus underwriting.

stories.headline: Arizona Takes Four Dorms Offline as Enrollment Slides
stories.text: The University of Arizona has taken Kaibab-Huachuca, Manzanita-Mohave, Graham-Greenlee and Babcock offline for 2026–27, leaving on-campus inventory at about 5,300 beds against roughly 5,299 projected residents. One off-campus operator said the university failed to fill even its reduced capacity — the clearest demand-side warning in this edition.

stories.headline: Lawrence Annexes ~288 Acres; 300 More Acres on Monday's Agenda
stories.text: Lawrence commissioners voted 5–0 to approve annexation and a comprehensive plan amendment for roughly 288 acres southwest of Sixth Street and K-10 for Wichita developer Phil Bundy's Beacon Landing project, including 23.5 acres of high-density apartments alongside 126.7 commercial, 87 single-family/duplex and 51 open-space acres. Requests to annex another 300-plus acres — 177 west of K-10 and 137 near the airport — were set for the planning commission's Monday agenda.

stories.headline: Landmark Signals Zone Map Amendment Across 15 Lexington Parcels
stories.text: Landmark Properties, through McBrayer PLLC, has signaled intent to pursue a zone map amendment to redevelop 15 properties across South Broadway, West Maxwell Street, Spring Street and Pine Street, with a neighborhood meeting set for Aug. 25 at the Lexington Public Library. The filing lands as UK's growth pushes students into a tight downtown rental market — the university now reports more than 8,500 on-campus beds — sharpening the local fight over high-density student product.

stories.headline: Renovation Delay Puts ~350 Illinois Students in Temporary Housing
stories.text: Bathroom renovation work at Trelease Hall ran past the start of the term, leaving an estimated 350 Illinois students in temporary quarters for the first month of the fall semester. About 100 residents from the sixth and seventh floors were moved into Wassaja Hall, which in turn pushed some Wassaja returners into private off-campus apartments. Data limitation: the publication date is corroborated by search attribution and internal evidence, but the article body could not be retrieved directly.

stories.headline: Landmark JV Buys 642-Bed Domain at Oxford
stories.text: A Landmark Properties joint venture has acquired the Domain at Oxford, a 216-unit, 642-bed community spanning more than 37 acres roughly one mile south of the Ole Miss campus. Yardi Matrix identifies Shore to Shore Properties as the seller; the seller had taken a $42 million loan from The RMR Group in 2024. The eight-building, low-density configuration — roughly 5.8 units per acre — is the kind of basis that supports either a heavy value-add program or a longer land play, and it trades into a market where Ole Miss is simultaneously delivering institutional beds at the Kincannon and West Row sites. Domain at Oxford Units / beds 216 / 642 Buildings 8 Site 37+ acres Distance to campus ~1 mile Prior debt (RMR Group, 2024) $42M Seller Shore to Shore Properties

stories.headline: Ivy Capital Pays $40.7M for 1,178-Bed Gainesville Asset
stories.text: The Collier Cos. sold the Crossing at Santa Fe, a 337-unit, 1,178-bed community in Gainesville, to New York-based Ivy Capital for $40.7 million — about $34,500 per bed. The buyer plans interior renovations and amenity upgrades; the asset is among Ivy Capital's largest holdings.

stories.headline: Scion Refinances 10,454-Bed Portfolio With $556M Fannie Facility
stories.text: Walker & Dunlop arranged a $555.6 million floating-rate Fannie Mae credit facility refinancing a 14-property, 4,295-unit, 10,454-bed Scion Group portfolio — roughly $53,100 per bed of proceeds. Collateral includes Lark Central Florida in Orlando, a 416-unit, 995-bed UCF community reported 88.9 percent preleased for fall 2026.

stories.headline: Alden Street Capital Takes 627-Bed New Brunswick High-Rise
stories.text: TSB Realty brokered the sale of SoCam 290, a 627-bed, 233-unit student housing high-rise near Rutgers' New Brunswick campus, delivered in 2005 and fully leased at closing. Alden Street Capital was the buyer; TSB Capital Advisors arranged acquisition financing. Price was not disclosed.

stories.headline: UMD-Affiliated Venture Buys College Park Shopping Center for $53M+
stories.text: Terrapin Development Company, created by the University of Maryland and the UMD College Park Foundation, purchased the College Park Shopping Center for more than $53 million in partnership with Northpond Partners. The property sits less than 500 feet from campus; the buyers say near-term operations will not change.

stories.headline: UC Investments' ~$50M Westwood Retail Buy Claims First Tenant
stories.text: A 22-year Westwood tenant is out: the village's Urban Outfitters has closed in the wake of a roughly $50 million retail portfolio purchase by UC Investments, the office managing the UC system's $190 billion pool. The buyer has not stated its intentions for the properties, which leaves the more consequential question open — whether this is a retail repositioning next to UCLA or the front end of a longer-dated development assemblage.

stories.headline: Turnbridge Adds 320-Unit Skyhouse Raleigh on $62M ACORE Loan
stories.text: Skyhouse Raleigh, a 320-unit downtown tower, has traded to Turnbridge Equities, financed with a $62 million ACORE Capital first mortgage. Northmarq marketed the asset for World Wide Group. The buyer's stated thesis rests on a thin forward pipeline — roughly 300 downtown units under construction with nothing expected to deliver before late 2027 — which is what supports the planned unit renovation program.

stories.headline: Kentucky Opens 649-Bed Kirwan-Blanding Hall in $81M Greystar P3
stories.text: Kentucky has cut the ribbon on the new Kirwan-Blanding Hall, a 649-bed, 222,635-square-foot residence hall delivered through an $81 million public-private partnership with Greystar. That works out to roughly $125,000 per bed and about 343 gross square feet per bed. The university says roughly 90 percent of first-year students live in residence halls and that returning-student demand is rising — the demand case that has made UK one of the most consistent P3 issuers in the SEC. The opening also lands in the same month a Lexington zone map amendment fight over 15 parcels near campus began, underscoring how institutional supply and private entitlement risk are moving together in this market. Kirwan-Blanding Hall Beds 649 Gross square feet 222,635 P3 project cost $81M Cost per bed ~$125,000 GSF per bed ~343 Partner Greystar

stories.headline: Madison Completes 15-Story Garage Redevelopment With 700+ Beds and a Bus Terminal
stories.text: The 15-story mixed-use redevelopment of the State Street Campus Garage has been completed through a public-private partnership with Mortenson Development, delivering more than 700 student housing beds, a 410-stall public garage and a city-owned regional bus terminal on the site of the 1964 Lake Street garage. The residential component was scheduled to open Aug. 24; the bus terminal follows in October. Two structuring details stand out. Under an agreement with UW-Madison, 100 beds are reserved at affordable rates for qualifying students and have already been filled for fall. And the project was financed in part with revenue from Tax Incremental District 50 — a municipal TIF contribution supporting a beds-plus-transit-plus-parking stack, and a template other campus-adjacent cities will be asked to copy. State Street Campus Garage Redevelopment Stories 15 Student beds 700+ Beds reserved at affordable rates 100 (filled) Public parking stalls 410 Transit City-owned regional bus terminal Public financing TID 50 revenue Certification target LEED Silver

stories.headline: UT Regents Agenda Includes Ground Lease Enabling Arena and Adjacent Student Housing
stories.text: The UT System Board of Regents' Aug. 12–13 agenda covered a short-term ground lease of about five acres north of East MLK Jr. Boulevard, between Robert Dedman Drive and I-35, with The 2033 Higher Education Development Foundation. The lease enables utility relocation and infrastructure for a future multipurpose arena and an adjacent student housing complex. This is early-stage intel rather than a project approval: a short-term lease for enabling work is the step that precedes a development agreement. Anyone tracking Austin should treat the housing component as identified but unsized — no bed count, cost or delivery date has been published.

stories.headline: TCU Tops Out 2,500-Bed Campus Community for Fall 2027
stories.text: TCU, American Campus Communities and The Beck Group have topped out an on-campus residential community delivering more than 2,500 beds for fall 2027, designed with Robert A.M. Stern Architects as part of a $500 million campus master plan. The project uses a third-party fee-based development structure with TCU retaining institutional ownership. Development advisor Brailsford & Dunlavey describes the program as four communities — first-year halls, sophomore suites and upperclassmen townhomes — framing the diversified bed mix as support for long-term enrollment expansion and retention. Fee-for-service with university ownership continues to displace equity-ownership P3 structures on flagship-adjacent campuses.

stories.headline: UConn Opens First Permanent Hartford Housing at Full Occupancy
stories.text: UConn has opened 64 Pratt St., its first permanent student housing in Hartford, at full occupancy with about 200 undergraduates in apartment-style units. The project was developed with Lexington Partners, Shelbourne Global Solutions and LAZ Investments, with UConn holding a master lease to operate it as a residence hall — a structure that transfers occupancy risk to the university rather than the ownership group. Officials describe it as the outcome of a long-term branch-campus investment plan that began with a 40-student pilot dorm last fall.

stories.headline: Cincinnati Details $326M, 1,300-Bed Block 1/Block 2 Development
stories.text: The University of Cincinnati reported progress on its $326 million, 1,300-bed Block 1/Block 2 student housing development at East McMillan and Vine streets, opening fall 2027 — about $251,000 per bed on the stated figures. The same back-to-school update covers a $200 million Welcome Gateway Building and a $304 million STEM facility replacing Crosley Tower.

stories.school_name: Virginia Polytechnic Institute and State University
stories.headline: Virginia Tech Visitors Meet Aug. 24–26 With 1,200-Bed Program in Motion
stories.text: Virginia Tech's Board of Visitors holds its quarterly meeting Aug. 24–26 in Blacksburg, continuing a multiyear on-campus housing investment strategy that includes an approved four-residence-hall capital project adding roughly 1,200 beds. Watch this meeting for phasing or budget actions on that program.

stories.school_name: University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill
stories.headline: UNC to issue master developer RFQ for Carolina North — 2,200 beds in phase one, plus new halls at the Jackson Hall site
stories.text: C hancellor Lee Roberts said UNC-Chapel Hill is about to issue a request for qualifications for a master developer for Carolina North, the university's 230-acre expansion tract, with a first phase planned to include roughly 2,200 student beds split between graduate and undergraduate housing. Roberts also confirmed new residence halls at the Jackson Hall site and a density increase at the Parker/Teague quad on main campus. For P3 and master-developer teams, this is the single most actionable item in this edition. A 230-acre horizontal development with a 2,200-bed first phase puts Carolina North in the same procurement tier as the largest campus expansion programs in the country, and the graduate/undergraduate split implies a mixed unit-type program rather than a single first-year hall typology. Roberts has referenced Carolina North repeatedly through the spring; the shift here is from intent to procurement. Carolina North — Confirmed Program Site 230 acres Phase 1 beds ~2,200 (grad + undergrad) Procurement Master developer RFQ (pending) Main campus Jackson Hall site halls; Parker/Teague density up
