stories.headline: Vanderbilt's 43-acre Innovation District clears second reading with height and traffic conditions; final vote Sept. 1
stories.text: M etro Council approved the specific-plan rezoning for Vanderbilt's 43-acre Innovation District on second reading Aug. 5, attaching an amendment from Councilman Tom Cash that adds height limits, traffic calming measures and construction-period protections for surrounding neighborhoods. Third and final reading is set for Sept. 1. At full build the plan contemplates up to 6.1 million square feet of research, housing, retail and open space near West End Avenue, with buildings reaching as high as 475 feet. Neighborhood opposition has focused squarely on height and density, and the conditions attached at second reading are the price of moving forward — a pattern worth studying for anyone entitling large mixed-use university-adjacent districts in Nashville. Conditions on height, traffic and construction impacts were the cost of second-reading passage — the emerging Nashville template.

stories.headline: Ann Arbor rezones downtown block to PUD for 10-story, 285-unit tower near campus
stories.text: Ann Arbor City Council held a public hearing and second-reading vote on rezoning 0.84 acres at 301-319 W. Huron St. and 102-106 S. First St. to a planned unit development, enabling a 10-story, 285-unit residential tower with a coffee shop and rooftop bar at grade and above. Fifteen percent of the units are committed as affordable at 60% of area median income — the affordability trade that has become standard practice for downtown Ann Arbor PUD approvals. The site sits within walking distance of central campus, and while the project is not purpose-built student housing, in this submarket unit absorption is inseparable from University of Michigan demand.

stories.headline: Utah opens $155M, 1,447-bed Trailhead hall, pushing campus capacity toward 7,000 beds
stories.text: The University of Utah is welcoming students this week to Trailhead, a two-wing, six-story residence hall totaling 349,342 square feet and 1,447 beds. Early move-in began Aug. 14 with general move-in Aug. 19. The $155 million project lifts the university's total student housing inventory to nearly 7,000 beds. Run the math and Trailhead pencils to roughly $107,000 per bed and about $444 per square foot of delivered cost — a useful public benchmark for anyone underwriting large on-campus product in the Mountain West. The outdoor-recreation programming and dining component reflect the amenity arms race in first-year housing; for Salt Lake City's off-campus owners, a single-year add of nearly 1,450 university beds is a real absorption event. Trailhead — Delivered Cost Total cost $155M Beds 1,447 Gross SF 349,342 Implied ~$107k/bed · ~$444/SF Campus total after ~7,000 beds

stories.headline: Georgia Tech opens 862-bed Peterson Hall, its first traditional residence hall in nearly 70 years
stories.text: Georgia Tech cut the ribbon on the eight-story Bud and Val Peterson Residence Hall on the west side of campus, adding 862 beds for first-year students along with a 24-hour market, fitness space and esports rooms. It is the institute's first new traditional residence hall in nearly seven decades — a striking data point on how long large public campuses can go without adding conventional first-year capacity, and how quickly that changes once enrollment growth forces the issue. Atlanta's off-campus student operators should expect first-year demand to shift on campus for 2026-27.

stories.headline: Oregon pauses phase two of East Campus housing on enrollment and budget concerns
stories.text: The University of Oregon has put phase two of its East Campus housing expansion on hold. The five-story residence hall planned for 17th and Moss, targeted for 2028, is paused pending lower enrollment projections and a broader budget review. Phase one — an $160 million, 870-bed hall — remains on schedule for fall 2027. This is the counter-signal to the record-enrollment stories driving most of this edition's on-campus deliveries. Enrollment-driven demand cuts both ways, and Oregon is the second flagship in recent weeks to defer committed housing capacity rather than push through a soft demand forecast. Off-campus owners in Eugene get a reprieve on 2028 supply; developers should read it as a reminder that university phase-two commitments are options, not obligations.

stories.headline: New luxury student housing planned near Miami's Coral Gables campus
stories.text: A new luxury student housing development is planned near the University of Miami's Coral Gables campus, adding to a Coral Gables pipeline that already includes purpose-built product oriented to UM students. Program specifics beyond the luxury positioning and campus-adjacent siting were not disclosed in the initial report — bed count, unit mix, developer capital structure and delivery date remain unconfirmed, and this item should be treated as an early-stage announcement rather than an underwritable pipeline addition.

stories.headline: NRP Group breaks ground on 336-unit community near Ohio State's airport campus
stories.text: The NRP Group started construction on a 336-unit upscale multifamily community near the Ohio State University Airport, north of the main Columbus campus. The project is conventional market-rate rather than purpose-built student housing, but it lands in a submarket where graduate and upper-division Ohio State demand is a meaningful share of the renter pool. Columbus continues to absorb one of the heavier multifamily pipelines in the Big Ten footprint.

stories.headline: Morrison Avenue opens 128-bed Hilltop Auburn — fully preleased 90 days after groundbreaking
stories.text: Morrison Avenue opened Hilltop Auburn for the 2026-27 academic year, a 128-bed Class A community serving Auburn University. The detail that matters for underwriters: the property was fully preleased by October 2025, under three months after breaking ground — roughly two full lease-up cycles ahead of typical purpose-built assumptions. Small-format infill in a supply-constrained SEC market continues to clear faster than pro formas allow, which is as much a statement about Auburn's bed shortage as about the sponsor's execution.

stories.headline: Gilbane and Coleraine start 756-bed Norman project with Santander, Fifth Third construction debt
stories.text: Gilbane Development, partnered with Coleraine Capital Group, broke ground on a 298-unit, 756-bed purpose-built student housing community on 33 acres less than a mile from the University of Oklahoma campus, targeting fall 2028 delivery. Santander Bank and Fifth Third Bank are providing construction financing. Two regional bank balance sheets underwriting a two-year student housing construction loan in a non-coastal SEC market is a live read on where bank credit is open this cycle. Norman Project Snapshot Program 298 units / 756 beds Site 33 acres, <1 mi to campus Sponsors Gilbane Dev. / Coleraine Construction lenders Santander, Fifth Third Delivery Fall 2028

stories.headline: Notre Dame breaks ground on $130M Colfax Corner innovation hub in downtown South Bend
stories.text: Notre Dame, Ancora and the City of South Bend broke ground on Colfax Corner, a roughly $130 million to $135 million innovation hub downtown that the partners project will bring more than 400 high-skilled jobs and generate more than $750 million in direct economic impact. The capital stack includes a South Bend Innovation Development District bond and a $30 million Lilly Endowment grant. The project is not housing, but the financing structure — TIF-style district bond plus philanthropic equity plus university sponsorship — is the same toolkit increasingly used to make university-adjacent mixed-use pencil in secondary markets.

stories.headline: Bloomington plan commission approves Hopewell South plat 8-1
stories.text: Bloomington's plan commission voted 8-1 on Aug. 10 to approve the primary plat for the 98-home Hopewell South project after the applicant withdrew a waiver request — the concession that appears to have unlocked the vote.

stories.headline: MAC on Fifth breaks ground in downtown Knoxville
stories.text: Leaders broke ground at 200 W. Fifth Ave. on MAC on Fifth, a five-story mixed-use project with 144 residential units, 2,300 square feet of retail and 14 workforce-housing units — downtown supply arriving as UT enrollment sets records.

stories.headline: Fort Worth commission approves TCU project, denies tree and signage waivers
stories.text: The Fort Worth Urban Design Commission approved a TCU project while rejecting requested waivers for tree removal and signage — a reminder that design-review bodies will split the difference rather than grant a full waiver package.

stories.headline: 265-bed Berkeley student building completes as move-ins begin
stories.text: A 265-bed purpose-built student housing property near UC Berkeley has completed construction with move-ins underway for the 2026-27 year, adding to a Berkeley pipeline where entitlement timelines routinely exceed construction timelines.

stories.headline: CU Boulder opens Code Talker Hall, adding 332 beds
stories.text: CU Boulder celebrated the opening of Code Talker Hall, adding 332 beds to campus inventory for the fall term — modest capacity relative to the flagship deliveries elsewhere this edition, but incremental supply in a chronically tight Boulder market.

stories.headline: Lawrence weighs annexing ~300 acres west of the trafficway
stories.text: The Lawrence City Commission is set to consider annexing nearly 300 acres west of the South Lawrence Trafficway. Separately, city analysis pegs westward growth as requiring at least $85 million in new infrastructure — the cost side of any land play out there.

stories.headline: UC Regents buy 16-property, 182,000-square-foot Westwood Village portfolio for $49.8M
stories.text: T he University of California Regents acquired a 16-property, roughly 182,000-square-foot Westwood Village portfolio for $49.8 million from Anderson Holdings, the family real estate company tied to the namesake of UCLA's Anderson School of Management. The seller had assembled the holdings over decades in the commercial core immediately adjacent to campus. The university has not announced whether it views the portfolio as an income investment or a land bank for future development, and that ambiguity is the story: at roughly $274 per square foot for entitled village commercial frontage, a university buying 16 contiguous-market properties in one trade changes who controls the redevelopment optionality in Westwood. Private capital pursuing student housing or mixed-use in the village now has a public institution as its principal competitor for sites. Westwood Village Portfolio Price $49.8M Properties 16 Building SF ~182,000 Implied ~$274/SF Buyer / Seller UC Regents / Anderson Holdings

stories.headline: Marcus & Millichap brokers $16.5M sale of two Clemson student assets out of Pierce Education Properties
stories.text: Marcus & Millichap brokered the $16.5 million sale of The Den at Clemson East and West, 146 units combined, with Pierce Education Properties as seller and a South Carolina-based buyer taking over. The trade pencils to roughly $113,000 per unit. A national student housing owner exiting to a regional buyer is the pattern to watch in smaller SEC and ACC markets, where local operators can underwrite management intensity that institutional platforms increasingly price away from.

stories.headline: IPA markets 188-bed Panoramic Northside at Berkeley, already 89% preleased
stories.text: Institutional Property Advisors is exclusively marketing Panoramic Northside, a 72-unit, 188-bed purpose-built student housing property on Shattuck Avenue serving UC Berkeley. The asset was delivered for the 2026-27 academic year and is already 89 percent preleased; Panoramic Interests is the seller. A brand-new Berkeley asset coming to market at near-stabilized occupancy is the cleanest available test of exit pricing for West Coast infill student product this cycle — guidance and pricing were not disclosed.

stories.headline: Athens land play near UGA returns nearly sixfold in under a year; infill trading near $967k/acre
stories.text: An Athens property company that paid $600,000 for an East Broad Street parcel near the UGA campus in August 2025 subdivided it and sold the two resulting tracts for a combined $1,050,450 on July 31, 2026. Local brokerage analysis puts infill land near campus at roughly $967,000 per acre. Subdivision arbitrage at this scale — buy whole, sell in parts — only works where land pricing per acre is rising faster than carry, and the Athens print says it is.

stories.headline: U District student building trades for $5.7M after 2023 land buy at $1.6M
stories.text: A student housing building at 4729 21st Ave. N.E. sold for more than $5.7 million per King County records. Seller Gatsby 5 LLC had acquired the site in 2023 for $1.6 million and scraped the existing structure to rebuild — a full build-to-sell cycle completed inside three years.

stories.headline: Security Properties pays $55.1M for Seattle-area apartments
stories.text: Security Properties acquired a Seattle-area apartment property for $55.1 million, adding to the firm's recent run of Puget Sound multifamily buying. Unit count and per-unit pricing were not disclosed in the report.

stories.headline: Student housing drives the Baton Rouge apartment boom
stories.text: Local reporting attributes the current Baton Rouge apartment construction and transaction cycle largely to student housing demand around LSU — useful context for the competing near-campus proposals now circulating, including a Denver developer's recent entry.

stories.headline: Tempe affordable housing coalition issues co-developer and GC RFQs on Apache Boulevard, responses due Sept. 7
stories.text: T he Tempe Coalition for Affordable Housing has issued a request for qualifications for a co-developer for new multifamily affordable communities at 1409 and 2101 E. Apache Blvd., along with a separate RFQ for a general contractor to handle rehabilitation across its existing portfolio. Proposals are due Sept. 7, 2026. Both Apache Boulevard sites sit on the light-rail corridor serving Arizona State's Tempe campus — a submarket where affordable and student demand overlap heavily and where ASU's continued enrollment growth keeps pressure on the rental stock. For developers with LIHTC capability, this is a rare shot at co-development on entitled corridor sites next to one of the largest enrollment bases in the country. The three-week response window is short; teams without an existing Arizona affordable partner will struggle to qualify. TCAH Procurement — Key Facts Sites 1409 & 2101 E. Apache Blvd. Scope A Co-developer, new affordable multifamily Scope B GC, portfolio rehabilitation Proposals due Sept. 7, 2026

stories.headline: UT Regents act on short-term ground lease enabling arena and student housing complex north of MLK
stories.text: The UT System Board of Regents took action at its August 12-13 meeting on a short-term ground lease covering roughly five acres north of E. Martin Luther King Jr. Blvd., leased to The 2033 Higher Education Development Foundation for site-enabling improvements ahead of a future multipurpose arena and student housing complex. The lease is procedural, but the structure is the intel: UT is routing site-enabling work through an affiliated foundation entity rather than the system's own capital program, which typically signals a larger third-party-financed development to follow. Program size, bed count, delivery timing and the eventual development partner are all unconfirmed in the board materials. Developers tracking Austin should treat this as the earliest visible step in what would be one of the largest campus-adjacent mixed-use programs in the SEC footprint.
stories.source: UT System Board of Regents Agenda Book (Aug 12-13, 2026)

stories.headline: WVU to take full ownership of University Place under comprehensive P3 settlement
stories.text: West Virginia University will assume full ownership of University Place as part of a comprehensive settlement with local developers, ending years of litigation over the downtown Morgantown public-private housing project. The settlement does not affect the separate University Park at Evansdale agreements or developer Ryan Lynch's interests there. Separately, Fitch Ratings assigned an AA- rating to WVU improvement revenue bonds in late July — a credit backdrop that makes university takeout of a distressed P3 asset materially easier to finance. For the P3 market, University Place remains the cautionary case study on structuring risk transfer that survives a demand miss.

stories.headline: Kentucky opens 649-bed Kirwan-Blanding Hall, an $81M partnership with Greystar
stories.text: The University of Kentucky held a ribbon-cutting for Kirwan-Blanding Hall at 1140 University Drive, a 649-bed residence hall delivered through an $81 million public-private partnership with Greystar. The name carries over from the twin towers that stood on the site for decades before demolition. At roughly $125,000 per bed, the project is a current benchmark for SEC on-campus P3 delivery cost, and it extends what is now one of the longest-running university housing partnerships in the country into another asset generation.

stories.headline: Minnesota closes Bailey Hall, its only St. Paul residence and dining hall, for 2026-27
stories.text: The University of Minnesota is closing Bailey Hall at 1458 Cleveland Ave. N. — a fixture since 1949 and the only residence and dining hall on the St. Paul campus — for the 2026-27 academic year, reassigning students to other halls. The university says all first-year housing guarantees will still be met and frames the closure as an accelerated start to St. Paul campus housing revitalization. What the university has not disclosed is a replacement program, budget or timeline; until it does, the beds are simply out of inventory, and St. Paul-side off-campus operators pick up the displaced demand.

stories.headline: Fitch assigns AA- to WVU improvement revenue bonds
stories.text: Fitch Ratings assigned an AA- rating to West Virginia University improvement revenue bonds in late July. For P3 counterparties, the rating is the practical measure of how much housing risk the university can absorb onto its own balance sheet — directly relevant given WVU's simultaneous move to take full ownership of University Place. Series size, pricing and use of proceeds were not detailed in the rating summary reviewed.

stories.headline: Oxford clears up to $125M in revenue bonds for 850-bed West Row phase two on the Ole Miss campus
stories.text: T he Oxford Board of Aldermen held a public hearing Aug. 4 and approved a resolution authorizing issuance of Public Finance Authority Student Housing Revenue Bonds — the PRG-Oxford Properties LLC West Row Project, Series 2026 — in an amount not to exceed $125 million. The proceeds fund construction of an approximately 850-bed student housing facility on the University of Mississippi campus. The bond issue advances the second phase of the Greystar/Provident public-private partnership at Ole Miss, one of the most closely watched on-campus P3 programs in the SEC. With phase one delivered under the same structure, the Series 2026 execution will be a live read on tax-exempt student housing credit appetite this fall — and on how much on-campus supply Oxford's small but historically supply-constrained market will absorb. West Row Phase II Snapshot Bond authorization Up to $125M Beds ~850 (on campus) Sponsor Greystar / Provident P3 Issuer Public Finance Authority

stories.headline: Up Campus files 10-story, 725-bed tower for downtown Lexington's High Street corridor
stories.text: Chicago-based Up Campus Student Living filed a zone change and development plan July 23 for a 10-story student apartment complex on East High Street in downtown Lexington — 238 units and 725 bedrooms over underground parking, a short walk from the University of Kentucky campus. The Urban County Planning Commission is expected to vote in mid-September. The filing lands in a Lexington market that keeps attracting institutional student capital: Article Student Living closed on the 280-bed Signature Apartments this month (see Acquisitions), and the 1,060-bed Latitude Lexington delivered on the same Angliana corridor. A downtown high-rise entitlement at this scale would be a meaningful test of the city's appetite for dense student product outside the traditional campus fringe. A 725-bed downtown high-rise filing tests how much dense student product Lexington will entitle beyond the campus fringe.

stories.headline: Planning Commission unanimously approves Pitt's 420-bed Fifth Avenue residence hall
stories.text: Pittsburgh's Planning Commission voted unanimously to approve the University of Pittsburgh's nine-story, 420-bed first-year residence hall at Fifth and Ruskin avenues in Oakland. The building replaces a surface parking lot surrounding the Music Building and advances Pitt's push to pull more first-year demand on campus. The approval came the same session the commission kicked off the first phase of Pittsburgh's citywide zoning code overhaul — a rewrite developers active in Oakland will want to track closely.

stories.headline: Affinius originates $176.6M construction loan for 1,395-bed Place at Alafaya near UCF
stories.text: Affinius Capital originated a $176.6 million construction loan to Beachwold Residential for The Place at Alafaya, a four-building development near the University of Central Florida totaling 484 units, 1,395 beds and 1,301 parking spaces, anchored by a 16,000-square-foot standalone clubhouse and resort-style amenity package. It is one of the largest student housing construction financings of the summer — a data point that pencils out to roughly $126,600 per bed in debt proceeds in a market where UCF's enrollment base continues to support big-format garden and mid-rise product. Place at Alafaya Snapshot Construction loan $176.6M (Affinius) Program 484 units / 1,395 beds Parking 1,301 spaces Sponsor Beachwold Residential

stories.headline: Columbia council takes up 305-unit Theory Sterling rezoning at University and College
stories.text: The Columbia City Council took up a rezoning request for Theory Sterling, a 305-unit student housing development proposed at University and College avenues on the doorstep of the University of Missouri. The plan would demolish University Place Apartments and several other student-occupied buildings — a net-supply nuance underwriters should note, since gross new beds overstate the market-level add. The item moved alongside nearly $40 million in unrelated utility bonds on the same agenda.

stories.headline: Bryan P&Z advances 'Langley' boutique student mid-rise toward September council vote
stories.text: The Bryan Planning and Zoning Commission on Aug. 6 unanimously recommended approval of Langley, a six-story boutique student housing development near Texas A&M featuring underground parking and positioned for students seeking a quieter alternative to the Northgate high-rise cluster. A second townhome-style project advanced at the same meeting. Both head to Bryan City Council in September — further evidence that College Station's spillover entitlement activity is migrating across the city line into Bryan.

stories.headline: Core Spaces closes financing, breaks ground on 1,656-bed Hub Athens Dougherty
stories.text: Core Spaces closed construction financing and broke ground on Hub Athens Dougherty, a 536-unit, 1,656-bed purpose-built community at 295 E. Dougherty St. in downtown Athens, delivering in 2028 with more than 47,000 square feet of amenities and 16,000 square feet of retail. Construction is led by a Core Spaces/Juneau joint venture with Mallory & Evans, JNS Realty and Northworks Architects on the team. The deal is also a public-private story: structured with Athens-Clarke County through a land swap, developer contributions toward affordable housing elsewhere in the county, and a roughly 400-space public parking deck. The site replaces the former Hotel Abacus while preserving the historic Foundry building and relocating the circa-1829 Hoyt House — a template for how large-format PBSH is getting entitled in historic college downtowns.

stories.headline: Landmark's 826-bed Narrative at Columbia opens in USC's emerging stadium district
stories.text: Narrative at Columbia, a 197-unit, 826-bed cottage-style community developed by Landmark Properties with Peninsula Investments at 1050 Idlewild Blvd. near Williams-Brice Stadium, welcomed its first residents Aug. 1 ahead of the 2026-27 year. The site sits 1.3 miles from the University of South Carolina campus and adjacent to USC's planned $1 billion stadium district development — a location bet on where campus gravity moves next. Landmark is already building its next Columbia project, the 825-bed The Walk on Shop Road on the former The State newspaper site, opening for 2027-28.

stories.headline: Tuscaloosa code crackdown hits student housing: mold condemnations at The Walk, 600+ violations at Legacy
stories.text: Weeks before fall move-in, a Tuscaloosa city inspector declared six units uninhabitable over mold at The Walk, a four-story luxury student building at 12th Street and 9th Avenue directly behind the rebuilt Julia Tutwiler Hall; units stay offline until professional remediation clears a third-party air-quality test. Across town, the City Council again tabled a resolution to condemn 13 buildings at the 224-unit Legacy at Country Club Apartments — cited for more than 600 code violations — giving the Nashville-based owner two more weeks to secure repair financing before the matter returns Aug. 18. For owners of aging Tuscaloosa product, enforcement risk is now a line item.

stories.headline: Competing apartment-and-hotel plans pitched around Bloomington convention center
stories.text: Two development teams presented competing proposals to the Bloomington Redevelopment Commission for the blocks around the convention center, including Concord Hospitality's plan pairing a host hotel at College Square with 200 mixed-income apartments at Second Street and College Avenue. Downtown Bloomington sites at this scale rarely trade — whichever plan advances will shape the supply picture on the west edge of the Indiana University demand shed.

stories.headline: Purdue dedicates $149M, 896-bed South Hall
stories.text: Purdue cut the ribbon on South Hall, an eight-story, 252,500-square-foot residence hall on MacArthur Drive, bringing beds added to West Lafayette on-campus capacity to roughly 1,900 since the 3rd & West opening in 2025; more than 18,500 students will live in University Residences this fall.

stories.headline: Moody's assigns Aa2 to USC bonds funding $185M residence hall pipeline
stories.text: Moody's assigned an Aa2 rating to USC's Series 2026 Higher Education Revenue Bonds — the program funding the $185M new residence hall pipeline — citing enrollment growth, stable operations and 40% five-year growth in cash and investments.

stories.school_name: University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill
stories.headline: UNC board clears commercial paper vehicle backing Carolina Housing expansion
stories.text: The UNC System Board of Governors approved authorization for UNC-Chapel Hill to use special obligation bond commercial paper financing — the vehicle designated to support the Carolina Housing expansion — alongside four new capital projects system-wide.

stories.headline: Core Spaces' $220M, 2,195-bed Hub Raleigh opens on Hillsborough Street
stories.text: Hub Raleigh — 12 stories, 665 units and 2,195 beds at Hillsborough Street and Cox Avenue — opened for first move-ins, instantly the largest residential address on the corridor at roughly one million square feet.

stories.headline: Charlottesville works through code changes developers say cut buildable volume
stories.text: Charlottesville's Planning Commission held a July 28 work session on Development Code changes, including technical zoning definitions developers argue reduce buildable volume; a June review drew calls to eliminate the city's student housing designation outright.

stories.headline: 673-bed SOMI Walk tower rises at South Miami Metrorail for fall 2028
stories.text: SOMI Walk, a 16-story, 673-bed tower designed exclusively for University of Miami students, is under construction steps from the South Miami Metrorail station, with private baths in every bedroom and a fall 2028 opening.

stories.headline: Article Student Living buys 280-bed Signature Apartments near UK, 100% preleased
stories.text: Article Student Living acquired Signature Apartments, a 150-unit, 280-bed Class A community at 840 Angliana Ave. serving University of Kentucky students, from Columbus-based Homestead Cos. The 2024-vintage asset came fully preleased for fall 2026 — and marks Article's second investment on the same street after its 1,060-bed Latitude Lexington joint venture with Barings. Two institutional entries on one corridor in two years says Lexington has graduated onto the core-plus student housing map.

stories.headline: Terrapin Development JV pays $53M for fully leased College Park Shopping Center
stories.text: Terrapin Development Co., the University of Maryland-affiliated developer, and Chicago-based Northpond Partners acquired the College Park Shopping Center at Hartwick Road and Route 1 for $53.05 million. The 75,000-plus-square-foot downtown retail center is fully leased, and the buyers say no redevelopment is imminent — but a university-affiliated entity controlling a full block of Route 1 frontage near campus is land banking in all but name.

stories.headline: Winterhaven Terrace trades for $15.7M near UA and Banner-UMC
stories.text: IPA brokered the $15.7 million ($163,542/unit) sale of Winterhaven Terrace, a 96-unit asset near the University of Arizona and Banner-University Medical Center, to a buyer expanding an existing Tucson portfolio.

stories.headline: Green Street Realty takes Champaign's Country Fair center for $4.38M
stories.text: Green Street Realty CEO Chris Saunders bought the Country Fair Shopping Center at Springfield and Mattis for over $4.38 million after nearly four years on market; the dominant Campustown operator plans a long-term reposition with the City of Champaign.

stories.headline: Trinsic closes $7M Durham land assemblage for 339-unit Aura 75
stories.text: Trinsic Residential paid nearly $7 million for 11.84 acres at 8116 Highway 751 and 102 Wayfield Ave. — the final parcels for its 339-unit Aura 75 project — with construction to start after permitting and a capital-partner closing, delivering 2028.

stories.headline: Louisville releases student housing P3 RFP — phase one targets ~1,000 beds, Stage 1 responses due Aug. 28
stories.text: T he University of Louisville has released a request for proposals for a student housing public-private partnership, with phase one focused on up to roughly 1,000 new apartment- and suite-style beds. The procurement is moving fast: written questions are due Aug. 11, 2026 — tomorrow — and Stage 1 responses are due Aug. 28. Brailsford & Dunlavey is serving as the university's development advisor. This is the most actionable piece of intel in this edition for P3 developers. A compressed two-and-a-half-week Stage 1 window suggests the university wants a shortlist before the fall board cycle, and the apartment/suite program mix points toward upper-division retention rather than first-year capacity — a different underwriting profile than the mega first-year halls dominating recent SEC and Big Ten procurements. UofL Housing P3 — Key Dates Phase 1 program Up to ~1,000 beds Written questions Aug 11, 2026 Stage 1 responses Aug 28, 2026 Advisor Brailsford & Dunlavey

stories.headline: Tennessee opens $160M, 1,028-bed Torchbearer Hall as enrollment tops 40,000
stories.text: UT Knoxville completed the $160 million, nine-story Torchbearer Hall, which houses 1,028 students beginning this fall — the second phase of the university's public-private partnership with RISE Real Estate. The delivery lands as UT enrollment crosses 40,000, a run of growth that has kept Knoxville among the tightest student housing markets in the SEC. For the P3 market, Torchbearer is proof of concept that the RISE partnership can deliver large first-year product on schedule — and for off-campus owners, it is a reminder that UT intends to keep absorbing more of its own demand growth on campus even as enrollment climbs.

stories.headline: Purdue trustees approve 10-year capital plan with 500-student Indianapolis residential hub
stories.text: Purdue trustees approved a 10-year capital projects plan running through 2037, headlined by a 302,000-square-foot Indianapolis Health, Science & Engineering Hub with a residential component housing up to 500 students in pod-style units. Trustees also received the first major update to the 50-year West Lafayette master plan, which notes more than 3,500 beds added on campus since 2018 plus 1,420 housing units in the Discovery Park District — a rare case of a university publishing its own long-run supply roadmap.

stories.headline: USC Next advances: McBryde demolition clears site for 1,000-bed Commons at Carolina
stories.text: USC's summer facilities roundup under the USC Next master plan confirms two McBryde buildings were demolished to make way for The Commons at Carolina residence hall, which together with a new Honors College residence wing will add more than 1,000 beds to the heart of campus by fall 2028. The Russell House expansion and Civil Rights Center also received Phase I board approval — the on-campus counterweight to Columbia's active off-campus pipeline.

stories.headline: Arizona first-year enrollment reportedly down ~23% — a shock to the Tucson bed market
stories.text: University of Arizona first-year undergraduate enrollment is expected to fall nearly 23% to roughly 5,800 this fall, sources told the Arizona Daily Star — a second consecutive annual decline. One local student housing owner called the drop “devastating” for near-campus rentals and Tucson businesses. The timing is uncomfortable: the decline hits just as the university adds on-campus supply and policy pressure pushes first-years into university beds, squeezing the off-campus market from both sides. Figures are pre-census and unofficial. A ~23% first-year decline, colliding with new on-campus supply, squeezes Tucson's off-campus market from both sides.

stories.headline: Cincinnati expects 55,000+ students on 11th straight record year; dorm construction accelerates
stories.text: The University of Cincinnati expects more than 55,000 students and over 8,000 new students this fall — its largest freshman class and 11th consecutive record year — driven in part by a new tuition-free program for Ohio families earning under $75,000. University leaders say multi-million-dollar dorm construction is underway to absorb the growth. Tuition-subsidy-driven enrollment is a demand tailwind developers can underwrite; the question is how much of it UC intends to house itself.

stories.headline: Florida launches $2B, 10,000-bed housing overhaul as 2,217-bed first phase breaks ground
stories.text: C onstruction is underway on a four-building, 680,000-square-foot redevelopment of the former Trusler, Simpson and Graham hall sites at the University of Florida — 2,217 beds in total, with two buildings opening in fall 2028 and the remaining two later that year. Balfour Beatty Campus Solutions is developing the project under UF Housing & Residence Life's 10-year capital plan, with construction executed through a 65:35 design-build joint venture between Balfour Beatty U.S. Buildings and Gainesville-based Stellar Group. The bigger story is the program behind it: the replacement halls are Phase 1 of a 10-year, $2 billion-plus initiative to add roughly 10,000 beds across UF's 2,000-acre campus by the end of the decade — and Board of Trustees Chair Mori Hosseini has publicly pushed to compress that timeline to as little as five years. For private developers underwriting Gainesville, the pace and sequencing of this on-campus pipeline is now the single biggest supply variable in the market. The 2,217-bed replacement is Phase 1 of a $2B-plus push to add 10,000 on-campus beds — possibly within five years. UF Housing Program Snapshot Phase 1 4 buildings / 2,217 beds Developer Balfour Beatty Campus Solutions Program $2B+ / ~10,000 beds Phase 1 delivery Fall–late 2028

stories.headline: Champaign drafts new RU2 district to unlock mid- and high-rise housing next to UIUC
stories.text: C hampaign is preparing a district-wide upzoning of the University Neighborhood, rezoning properties into a newly created RU2 — University Neighborhood 2 — district designed to support mid-rise and high-rise apartment development near the University of Illinois campus. The Plan Commission hearing originally set for July 15 was rescheduled to August 5 after the commission failed to reach quorum, with City Council consideration currently slated for August 4. A new by-right zoning district for taller residential product near campus is the kind of structural entitlement change that reprices land. Anyone holding or underwriting sites in the Campustown orbit — where the Green Street corridor has absorbed successive waves of high-rise supply — should be tracking the district boundaries and dimensional standards as they emerge from the August hearings. A new by-right district for mid- and high-rise product near campus is the kind of change that reprices land. RU2 Rezoning Snapshot District RU2 — University Neighborhood 2 Intent Mid- & high-rise apartments Plan Commission Aug 5 (rescheduled) City Council Aug 4

stories.headline: Up Campus' 683-bed University District proposal stalls with no return date
stories.text: Up Campus Properties' proposed 269-unit, 683-bed student housing complex at West Eighth Avenue and Worthington Street in Columbus' University District will not go before city reviewers this month, and there is no timeline for its return. A June 25 review board found the project inconsistent with neighborhood planning standards — a reminder that even in a market as deep as Ohio State's, design review remains a live entitlement risk for large-format private product.

stories.headline: Camp Eight pitches 155-unit student project on Craig Street, a block from Pitt's planned residence hall
stories.text: Camp Eight Capital is pursuing a seven-story, 155-unit student housing development at 143 Craig Street in Oakland, converting a former Carnegie Mellon building site one block from Pitt's planned Fifth Avenue residence hall. The Craig Street corridor is quietly becoming one of Oakland's busiest development strips, with university and private projects now advancing in parallel.

stories.headline: 262-unit Dean Lexington rezoning hits Planning Commission alongside downtown master plan amendment
stories.text: The Lexington-Fayette Urban County Planning Commission took up a zone map amendment July 23 for The Dean Lexington, a six-story, 75-foot mixed-use building with 262 dwelling units proposed by South Broadway Project Owner LLC at 1021–1069 S. Broadway near the UK campus. The same agenda carried multiple residential rezonings and an amendment to the Downtown Area Master Plan — a busy docket in a market a recent study says needs 4,700+ additional student beds.

stories.headline: Charlottesville: The Mark's approval is final — no revote, city attorney rules
stories.text: Charlottesville's city attorney has confirmed that Council's 3-2 May decision granting a Certificate of Appropriateness for The Mark — Landmark Properties' seven-story, roughly 700-person luxury student housing project at 7th and Delevan Streets in Fifeville — is legally final under Virginia law and the city development code, and cannot be reopened or revoted despite continued neighborhood pressure. The ruling closes the entitlement chapter on one of the most contested student housing approvals in the UVA market this cycle.

stories.headline: Ann Arbor Planning Commission clears 300+ units at former University Inn site
stories.text: The Ann Arbor Planning Commission approved redevelopment of the former University Inn site on Stadium Boulevard, pairing a six-story apartment complex with three three-story townhouse buildings for more than 300 total units. The updated proposal was enabled by the city's TC-1 transit corridor rezoning — an early proof point for that upzoning — and now heads to City Council for final approval.

stories.headline: $80M West Campus student housing permit filed at 900 W. 23rd St.
stories.text: A construction permit was filed with the Texas Department of Licensing and Regulation for an $80 million ground-up off-campus student housing project at 900 W. 23rd Street in Austin's West Campus district, with an estimated construction window of November 2026 through July 2029. The filing ranked among the five most expensive projects submitted in the Austin metro that week — fresh evidence that the nation's densest student housing submarket is still adding pipeline.

stories.headline: Alpha Residential plans 245 units in Knoxville's stadium district
stories.text: Pennsylvania-based Alpha Residential proposes a seven-story, 245-unit apartment building with ground-floor retail and a 263-space garage on Patton Street in downtown Knoxville's stadium district, about a mile from the UT campus, and hopes to break ground within six months pending Design Review Board approval.

stories.headline: Townes at North Lake pulled minutes before Northport council vote
stories.text: The developer behind the proposed Townes at North Lake residential development in Northport (Tuscaloosa metro) withdrew the project from the City Council agenda minutes before its second reading, after the Planning and Zoning Commission recommended against approval. A resubmission remains possible.

stories.headline: Fayetteville mayor breaks 4-4 tie on 36-acre west-side rezoning
stories.text: Fayetteville's City Council deadlocked 4-4 before Mayor Molly Rawn broke the tie to approve rezoning about 36 acres northwest of Deane Solomon Road and Vanike Drive for residential development up to eight units per acre. A bill of assurance bars multifamily on the Deane Solomon parcel, so quadplexes and single-family product — not student housing — are expected.

stories.headline: Quarterra's $400M, 796-unit University Village project goes vertical near UW
stories.text: Major vertical construction is underway on the $400 million, 796-unit University Village luxury apartment community near the University of Washington, developed by Quarterra and MacNaughton on a four-acre parcel with 25,000 square feet of retail; completion is targeted for Q3 2028.

stories.headline: Berkeley conversion adds 79 student housing units in 60 days
stories.text: A six-story, 79-unit downtown Berkeley apartment building was converted to off-campus student housing operated by FOUND Study in just 60 days, within walking distance of the UC Berkeley campus — a conversion-speed data point for operators eyeing adaptive reuse near supply-constrained flagships.

stories.headline: Coca-Cola sells 5 Midtown acres to Georgia Tech for $31.3M campus expansion
stories.text: C oca-Cola sold roughly five acres of its Midtown Atlanta corporate campus along North Avenue to the Board of Regents of the University System of Georgia for $31.3 million, with the transaction closing July 15. Georgia Tech, whose Bobby Dodd Stadium sits within walking distance of the parcel, calls the property a “strategic addition to our core campus” to support enrollment growth — though a specific use has not yet been determined. Flagship land banking on this scale matters for private developers: five contiguous acres on North Avenue is one of the last large assemblages on Tech's eastern edge, and whether it becomes academic space, housing or a P3 site will shape the Midtown student housing map for a decade. North Avenue Parcel Snapshot Price $31.3M Size ~5 acres Seller / buyer Coca-Cola / USG Board of Regents Closed Jul 15, 2026

stories.headline: F6 Partners buys 300-plus-bed pedestrian portfolio at Oklahoma State
stories.text: F 6 Partners acquired a 300-plus-bed portfolio of townhouse-style student housing assets roughly 0.1 miles from the Oklahoma State campus in Stillwater, executed through its value-add F6 Student Housing Fund. The firm cited OSU's growing enrollment and constrained new supply as the underwriting thesis — a pattern increasingly visible in secondary Power Four markets where replacement cost pricing keeps new construction thin. Pedestrian-to-campus townhouse product is a scarce format at most Power Four schools, and portfolio-scale acquisitions of it are rarer still. Watch whether F6's fund continues assembling in overlooked Big 12 markets where per-bed pricing remains well below SEC and Big Ten comparables. Stillwater Portfolio Snapshot Scale 300+ beds, townhouse-style Distance ~0.1 mi from OSU campus Buyer F6 Partners (F6 SH Fund) Strategy Value-add, Power 4 focus

stories.headline: Seven-property IU edge-of-campus portfolio heads to September auction
stories.text: A generational estate portfolio of seven income-producing multi-unit rental properties at the edge of the Indiana University campus — on Eagleson, Highland, Swain and Atwater avenues — goes to live and simulcast auction September 3, with online bidding open since July 20. Estate-driven dispositions of this kind are one of the few ways to assemble near-campus Bloomington scale in a single trade.

stories.headline: Harvest pays $163M for 25-acre Palo Alto campus, weighs housing conversion
stories.text: Harvest Properties acquired the 24.5-acre R&D campus at 3825–3875 Fabian Way in Palo Alto for $163 million from Alexandria Real Estate Equities and is weighing converting part of the Stanford-adjacent site to housing — a large land position in one of the country's most housing-starved university markets.

stories.headline: Sterling Park trades in Norman with loan assumption
stories.text: MMG Real Estate Advisors arranged the sale of Sterling Park, a 142-unit apartment complex in Norman, home of the University of Oklahoma, in a deal involving assumption of the property's existing loan; buyer and seller were not disclosed. Loan-assumption executions remain a telling financing-market signal at current rates.

stories.headline: 15-unit Penrith Apartments trades for $3M in Seattle's U District
stories.text: Marcus & Millichap arranged the $3 million sale of the 15-unit Penrith Apartments in Seattle's U District near the University of Washington — a small-cap pricing comp in a submarket where towers now dominate the pipeline.

stories.headline: Arizona breaks ground on $250M, 1,300-bed Catalina P3 backed by $270M bond close
stories.text: T he University of Arizona broke ground July 22 on The Catalina, a $250 million, 1,300-plus-bed residence hall on roughly three acres including the former Palm Shadows Apartments site. The project is structured as a public-private partnership with Mortenson as developer and builder, Gensler as architect, and the Collegiate Housing Foundation financing, owning and operating the community under a long-term ground lease, with completion scheduled for fall 2028. The capital stack closed earlier this month: the Arizona Industrial Development Authority issued approximately $270 million in Student Housing Revenue Bonds for the CHF-Arizona LLC project, with RBC Capital Markets running the financing. It is one of the largest tax-exempt student housing bond executions of 2026 — and a live pricing benchmark for every university weighing CHF-style 501(c)(3) ownership against balance-sheet delivery. The Catalina Snapshot Cost / bonds $250M / ~$270M tax-exempt Beds 1,300+ Structure CHF ground-lease P3, Mortenson Delivery Fall 2028

stories.headline: Mizzou names candidate sites as developer solicitation moves past RFI stage
stories.text: M issouri's commercial development program is advancing: MU officials are now accepting proposals from commercial developers to build student housing, hotels and restaurants forming a year-round commercial hub, after last October's RFI drew a strong developer response. New in this round is a named list of potential sites — the Hearnes Center, the softball stadium, areas east and west of downtown Columbia, MU Health Care facilities and land near Brooks Hall. For development teams tracking SEC procurement, the site list converts a vague opportunity into an underwritable one. The Dispatch flagged Mizzou's year-end RFP timeline in Edition 10; the named parcels suggest the university is sequencing toward formal solicitations on schedule. Hearnes Center, the softball stadium and land near Brooks Hall are now named candidate sites — the opportunity is underwritable.

stories.headline: Penn State approves 2.5% housing-rate rise, advances Pollock renewal phase
stories.text: Penn State trustees approved 2027–28 housing and dining rates — a 2.5% increase at University Park, the lowest aggregate increase in nine years — and outlined the third phase of the Housing and Food Services capital plan in the Pollock Housing Area: Hiester and Shulze halls reopen after renovation while Porter and Shunk go offline, with $20 million budgeted for systemwide facility renewal. On-campus rate growth this modest keeps pressure on off-campus operators' rent premiums in State College.

stories.school_name: University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill
stories.headline: UNC converts Baity Hill to undergrad beds, leaving grad students without on-campus option
stories.text: UNC-Chapel Hill is ending graduate and family housing at Baity Hill and transitioning the apartments to undergraduate use, leaving graduate students with no on-campus alternative. The move is part of the university's push to expand undergraduate bed capacity amid record enrollment — and it pushes a graduate renter cohort with steady, year-round demand squarely into the Chapel Hill off-campus market.

stories.headline: SMU's largest-ever class arrives as applications surge 60% post-ACC move
stories.text: SMU will welcome its largest first-year class this fall — more than 1,800 students in the Class of 2030, drawn from 44 states and 38 countries — after applications rose nearly 60% over two years following the move to the ACC. Sustained class-size growth at a landlocked private campus is a durable tailwind for the University Park and East Dallas rental markets.

stories.headline: CU Boulder holds class size steady as Colorado stares down enrollment cliff
stories.text: CU Boulder drew more than 71,000 first-year applications for fall 2026, and the provost expects an incoming class near last year's 7,884 despite a slight dip in out-of-state applicants — even as Colorado faces a projected 14% drop in high school graduates by 2041. Flagship demand is holding while the statewide demographic base erodes.

stories.school_name: Virginia Polytechnic Institute and State University
stories.headline: Virginia Tech budgets for $5.4M tuition shortfall on grad enrollment slide
stories.text: Virginia Tech leaders adjusted the 2026–27 operating budget for $5.4 million less in tuition and fees due to lower-than-projected graduate enrollment — driven largely by declines in international graduate students — with a similar impact projected from fall 2025 to fall 2026. Graduate-oriented rental product in Blacksburg should be underwritten accordingly.

stories.headline: Landmark's 817-bed Station at Oxford goes vertical as aldermen weigh early concrete pours
stories.text: O xford's Board of Aldermen takes up a request Tuesday from Landmark Construction for early concrete pours at the Oxford Station project on Oxford Way — the site of Landmark Properties' 817-bed The Station at Oxford student housing development — with pours slated to begin July 24 and run through October 2026. The request, on the board's July 21 agenda, is the clearest signal yet that vertical construction is ramping up on one of the largest private student housing projects in the Oxford pipeline. A pour schedule running into October implies structure will climb through the fall semester — a meaningful pace marker for competitors underwriting deliveries into the Oxford market, where entitlement fights over student density have historically slowed private product. How the board handles the early-hours request will also be a useful read on the city's current posture toward active student housing construction downtown. An approved pour window of July 24 through October would put structure in the air through the fall semester. Oxford Station Snapshot Project The Station at Oxford Developer Landmark Properties Beds 817 Pour window Jul 24 – Oct 2026

stories.headline: Beachwold lands $176.6M for 1,395-bed Place at Alafaya — Orlando's largest private residential construction loan
stories.text: B eachwold Residential closed on a $176.6 million construction loan originated by Affinius Capital and arranged by JLL for Phases I and II of Place at Alafaya, a Class A, four-building, 484-unit, 1,395-bed student housing development a 15-minute walk from the UCF campus. JLL calls it the largest private residential construction loan in Orlando's history — a marker of how much institutional debt capital is willing to commit to the UCF market at scale. Phase I, at roughly 809 beds, is slated to deliver ahead of the 2028–29 academic year, with Phase II's 586 beds following before 2029–30. Plans include a 16,000-square-foot clubhouse and direct campus shuttle service, positioning the project as amenity-forward purpose-built product in one of the country's largest-enrollment university markets. Place at Alafaya Snapshot Loan $176.6M construction Lender / arranger Affinius Capital / JLL Scale 484 units / 1,395 beds Delivery Ph. I 2028 • Ph. II 2029

stories.headline: Core Spaces breaks ground on 2,201-bed Hub College Station, Northgate's largest student project
stories.text: Core Spaces celebrated the groundbreaking of Hub College Station, a two-building, 570-unit, 2,201-bed community in the Northgate District steps from Texas A&M — the largest new student housing development in Northgate — with roughly 60,000 square feet of amenities and delivery targeted ahead of the 2028–29 academic year. Pacific Life provided financing on the $130 million project, Core's first ground-up student deal in Texas; A&M preleasing hit 77.6% in May with average rent per bed up 0.7% year-over-year to $861. Hub College Station Snapshot Scale 570 units / 2,201 beds Cost / lender $130M / Pacific Life Delivery Ahead of 2028–29

stories.headline: New Brunswick advances $1.5B Fourward Hill redevelopment near the train station
stories.text: The New Brunswick Housing Authority approved plans to advance Fourward Hill, a $1.5 billion mixed-use redevelopment of the city's Fourth Ward that would replace the Schwartz Homes and Robeson Village apartments with roughly 2,000 units — including 400 to 500 partially subsidized workforce housing units — within walking distance of New Brunswick Station and the Rutgers campus core. The project is one of the largest residential redevelopments proposed in a Big Ten college town this cycle.

stories.headline: Urbana ends months-long fight, approves contested Main Street project 4-1 in round four
stories.text: After the vote was pushed back three times, Urbana's City Council approved the contested 32-unit apartment development at 413–419 W. Main St. along Boneyard Creek on a 4-1 vote July 13, with amendments requiring tree preservation and six months' notice to existing tenants. Developers Derek and Melissa Brashear said the project will add walkable downtown housing and tax base; opponents argued it conflicts with the comprehensive plan amid the area's housing shortage.

stories.headline: Miami-Dade zoning board clears ~300-bed Vox on Red steps from UM
stories.text: The Miami-Dade Community Zoning Appeals Board on July 9 approved rezoning of the 2.89-acre site at 6280 SW 57th Ave. for Treo Group's Vox on Red, a six-story, 117-unit student housing project penciling roughly 300 beds within walking distance of the University of Miami and SMART Plan transit corridors. The approval advances one of at least three private student housing projects currently in the works around UM — a market long constrained by Coral Gables-area entitlement friction.

stories.headline: CCI underway on eight-story, 353-bed 290 Lumpkin near UGA
stories.text: CCI Real Estate has begun construction on 290 Lumpkin, an eight-story, 353-bed student housing development near the University of Georgia campus, developed in partnership with the Georgia Baptist Mission Board and slated for completion in summer 2027. The project includes 243 furnished units, a 356-space parking deck and ground-floor retail, with preleasing set to begin this fall for the 2027–28 academic year.

stories.headline: Subtext's 12-story VERVE Charlottesville to deliver 1,332 beds adjacent to UVA in summer 2027
stories.text: Subtext's 12-story VERVE Charlottesville, at Stadium Road and Jefferson Park Avenue, will deliver 1,332 beds across 463 units adjacent to UVA Grounds in summer 2027, with 25,000 square feet of amenities and a $6.8 million contribution to the Charlottesville Affordable Housing Fund. The delivery will rank among the largest single additions of purpose-built student supply in the Charlottesville market this cycle.

stories.headline: Core Spaces pitches 717-bed tower on Lexington's South Broadway
stories.text: Core Spaces, operator of two Hub communities near UK, has proposed a seven-story, 278-unit building with 717 bedrooms at 532 South Broadway — replacing the Clean Sweep Car Wash — plus a 750-space garage at 300 Cedar Street, with a Planning Commission vote set for August. A study cited in the same roundup finds Lexington needs 22,549 more housing units, including 4,739 for students, as UK enrollment growth strains nearby neighborhoods.

stories.headline: Trinitas, Harrison Street refinance 530-bed Atmosphere Tempe via PGIM bridge
stories.text: TSB Capital Advisors arranged a floating-rate bridge loan through PGIM to refinance Atmosphere Tempe, a 252-unit, 530-bed student housing high-rise serving ASU, on behalf of Trinitas Ventures and Harrison Street Asset Management.

stories.headline: State College opens neighborhood meetings on zoning overhaul
stories.text: State College is holding July neighborhood meetings on its comprehensive zoning overhaul, which aims to balance student housing and long-term resident housing; feedback goes to borough council in mid-August with a possible vote by year-end — a rewrite worth tracking for anyone underwriting State College sites.

stories.headline: CCI begins leasing 95-bed 740 Techwood near Georgia Tech
stories.text: CCI Real Estate began leasing 740 Techwood, a five-story, 95-bed student housing development near Georgia Tech backed by $18 million in construction financing, with completion expected ahead of the 2027–28 academic year.

stories.headline: Landmark, CrossHarbor start 1,002-bed The Mark Eugene by UO
stories.text: Landmark Properties, in partnership with CrossHarbor Capital, began construction on The Mark Eugene, a 1,002-bed community 0.1 miles from the University of Oregon campus on the former PeaceHealth hospital site, with delivery anticipated for the 2028–29 academic year.

stories.headline: Onelin advances two 22-story towers at former University Inn site near UW
stories.text: Onelin Capital opened community outreach on plans to demolish the University Inn at 4140 Roosevelt Way NE — three blocks from the UW campus — and build two 22-story residential towers totaling roughly 467 units with ground-floor retail. Onelin paid about $27 million for the hotel site.

stories.headline: PCCP-Dinerstein JV takes down 1,128 beds near Texas A&M, rebrands as Sterling College Station
stories.text: A joint venture between PCCP LLC and The Dinerstein Cos. acquired two adjacent student housing communities totaling 350 units and 1,128 beds near Texas A&M — formerly 2818 Apartments and Parkway Place — and is rebranding the combined asset as Sterling College Station. The partners plan kitchen, bath, amenity and common-area upgrades across the property, a classic value-add repositioning play. The trade lands in a College Station market with visible momentum on both sides of the ledger: preleasing at A&M hit 77.6% in May, and Core Spaces just broke ground on 2,201 beds in Northgate. Buying existing beds at a discount to replacement cost while new supply prices at the top of the market is the thesis in a sentence. Sterling College Station Snapshot Scale 350 units / 1,128 beds Buyer PCCP + Dinerstein JV Assets 2818 Apts + Parkway Place Plan Value-add rebrand

stories.headline: Northeastern pays $169M — $241K per bed — to take out P3 partners at 723-bed East Village
stories.text: N ortheastern University paid $169 million, roughly $241,429 per bed, for East Village, a 17-story, 723-bed dormitory tower at 291 St. Botolph St. in the Fenway. The building was developed under a public-private partnership with Phoenix Property Co. and Lincoln Property Co., making the sale a full university buyback of privately developed P3 student housing. For P3 developers and their capital partners, the deal is a clean exit comp — and a signal that universities in supply-constrained coastal markets are willing to pay institutional pricing to bring privately built beds onto their own balance sheets. The asset sits in Boston College's broader metro market rather than adjacent to the BC campus. East Village Snapshot Price $169M ($241,429/bed) Asset 17 stories / 723 beds Seller Phoenix + Lincoln (P3) Buyer Northeastern University

stories.headline: LV Collective buys land for 1,022-bed Rambler near LSU
stories.text: Austin-based LV Collective purchased part of the land needed for its planned 1,022-bed, seven-story Rambler-branded student housing development between Burbank Drive and Gourrier Avenue near LSU (the El Cid/Embassy Courts site), with construction targeted to start at the end of 2026.

stories.headline: Four Mile, Midloch pay $38.25M for Louisville's Frontgate Apartments
stories.text: Four Mile Capital, in partnership with Midloch Investment Partners, paid $38.25 million for the 212-unit Frontgate Apartments in Louisville — a conventional multifamily trade that serves as a market pricing comp rather than a dedicated student housing deal.

stories.headline: IPA arranges $32M lender-owned disposition in Tucson at $106K per unit
stories.text: Institutional Property Advisors arranged the $32 million sale of Peaks at Redington, a 301-unit Tucson apartment community, to Greenwater Real Estate Management at $106,312 per unit in a lender-owned disposition — a distress-pricing data point for the Tucson market.

stories.headline: Greystar, Penn State and JLC close on 1,500-bed University Drive P3
stories.text: G reystar, Penn State and JLC Infrastructure closed on University Drive, a roughly 1,500-bed public-private student housing development on university-owned land at Penn State, with four residence halls delivering across 2027 and 2028. The financial close moves one of the Big Ten's largest active on-campus P3s from paperwork into production. The structure — an institutional developer-operator paired with an infrastructure investor on university land — has become the template for large on-campus deliveries, and the University Drive close gives the P3 market a fresh, current execution comp at a flagship with deep enrollment demand. It lands the same month State College opens public meetings on a comprehensive zoning overhaul that will shape the off-campus supply picture around it. University Drive P3 Snapshot Beds ~1,500 (4 halls) Partners Greystar + JLC Infra. Structure P3 on university land Delivery 2027–2028

stories.headline: Mizzou narrows RFI field, will issue developer RFPs for student housing sites by year-end
stories.text: A fter a developer RFI process launched in September 2025, the University of Missouri has narrowed its focus to student housing, hospitality and mixed-use opportunities on nonessential university property, including public-private partnership and long-term ground lease structures. The university says it plans to engage directly with developers and launch formal RFPs for select sites by the end of the year. For developers tracking SEC procurement pipelines, this is a live window: site selection is happening now, and direct engagement ahead of the RFP stage is explicitly on the table. Mizzou joins a growing list of flagships monetizing land through ground-lease and P3 structures rather than balance-sheet development. Formal RFPs for select Mizzou sites are expected by year-end — a live procurement window for student housing developers.

stories.headline: Pitt presents nine-story, 420-bed first-year hall to city Planning Commission
stories.text: Pitt and design firm VMDO presented the City Planning Commission with plans for a nine-story, L-shaped, 420-bed first-year residence hall at Fifth and Ruskin avenues, replacing a surface parking lot as Oakland undergraduate enrollment climbs toward the university's 22,000 goal by 2028. The project extends Pitt's multi-year push to add university-controlled beds in a neighborhood where private developers are also circling sites.

stories.headline: Arizona breaks ground on 1,300-bed Catalina under tax-exempt P3 structure
stories.text: The University of Arizona broke ground July 14 on The Catalina, a nine-story, 1,300-plus-bed apartment-style dorm with a dining hall at Speedway and Campbell, opening fall 2028. The project is delivered via a P3 with Mortenson Development and the nonprofit Collegiate Housing Foundation, which will finance, own and operate the residence hall under a tax-exempt structure with a path to future university ownership.

stories.headline: UF advances $443M, 2,200-bed first-year housing complex
stories.text: The University of Florida is moving forward with a four-building, $443 million multi-phase housing complex adding roughly 2,200 beds for first-year students by 2029, replacing the demolished Graham, Simpson and Trusler halls. The project — approved by both the Board of Trustees and the Board of Governors — will also house a new ground-floor Disability Resource Center facility serving more than 8,000 students annually.

stories.headline: Flintco opens bidding on OU First-Year Housing Phase 2 early site package
stories.text: Flintco LLC, on behalf of the University of Oklahoma, is soliciting qualified firms — including temporary tower crane work — for the Building A early site package of OU First-Year Housing Phase 2 in Norman, with bids to be opened July 30. The notice confirms Phase 2 of OU's First-Year Housing Master Plan, three buildings replacing Walker Center, is moving into construction procurement.

stories.headline: UK's $450M building boom includes 649-bed Kirwan-Blanding P3 hall opening this fall
stories.text: The University of Kentucky has nearly $450 million in capital projects underway, headlined by the 214,000-square-foot, 649-bed Kirwan-Blanding residence hall opening fall 2026 through a public-private partnership to support enrollment growth and high on-campus housing demand, with additional facilities delivering through 2027.

stories.headline: Clemson council to cast decisive final vote on 555-bed Pine Street student housing tower
stories.text: C lemson City Council is set to cast a final, and likely decisive, vote on a 555-bed student housing complex at 201 Pine Street, capping a stop-and-start entitlement fight that has run for weeks. The project, which would raze an existing apartment complex near North Clemson Avenue and Hedgerow Lane and replace it with the larger tower, first cleared council on a narrow 4-3 vote — only to be rejected 4-3 at the very next meeting, an unusual reversal that left developers and neighbors alike unsure how the final tally would land. The back-and-forth reflects a familiar tension in the Clemson market: council members are weighing steady enrollment-driven demand for beds close to campus against long-standing resident concerns over density and traffic along the Pine Street corridor. A final approval would clear the way for demolition and a construction start later this year; a second rejection would send the site back to the drawing board after months of carrying costs on land already under contract. A prior 4-3 approval was followed by a 4-3 rejection at the very next meeting — leaving the project's fate down to a single vote.

stories.headline: Ann Arbor advances two major rezonings in a single week near campus
stories.text: A nn Arbor's city council and planning commission cleared two significant rezoning actions within 24 hours of each other this month, signaling a busy entitlement pipeline heading into the fall semester. Council gave preliminary approval to a ten-story mixed-use complex across from the Delonis Center at Huron and First streets, over objections from residents opposed to the building's height and the loss of an existing entertainment venue on the site; a final vote is expected at the next council meeting. A day later, the city's Planning Commission recommended approval of a major expansion at Woodbury Gardens Apartments and Townhomes, where the developer plans to raze one parcel and construct three seven-story multifamily buildings alongside a five-story parking garage, adding more than 300 units. That proposal now heads to the full council for a final vote — arriving the same month the University of Michigan's regents approved a $3.1 billion FY27 budget that raises undergraduate tuition 3% and room and board roughly 6% for the fall term.

stories.headline: Fayetteville council leaves 36-acre multifamily rezoning on first reading amid pushback
stories.text: Fayetteville's City Council considered rezoning roughly 36.2 acres near North Deane Solomon Road and West Vanike Drive from single-family and commercial use to RMF-12 multifamily and RSF-8, but left the item on first reading after resident opposition, with debate set to continue July 21. The same meeting authorized $191.22 million in city bonds and passed a Fayetteville-University of Arkansas memorandum of understanding covering roadway and sidewalk maintenance near campus.

stories.headline: Auburn schedules hearing on 1.15-acre South Donahue Drive rezoning near campus
stories.text: The Auburn City Council will hold a public hearing July 21 on rezoning roughly 1.15 acres at 1117 South Donahue Drive — just off campus — from the South College Corridor District to the Comprehensive Development District, the latest in a string of small-parcel rezonings feeding the Auburn student housing pipeline.

stories.headline: Champaign permits two new multifamily buildings on Fields South Drive
stories.text: Wells and Wells Construction pulled permits for two new multifamily buildings at 2409 and 2411 Fields South Drive in Champaign, each valued at roughly $2.34 million, adding to the broader multifamily pipeline several miles from the Urbana-Champaign campus core.

stories.headline: Oxford aldermen overturn Planning Commission, approve six-bedroom variance near campus
stories.text: The Oxford Board of Aldermen overturned a Planning Commission denial and approved a zoning variance allowing a six-bedroom home on University Avenue, despite the area's Neighborhood Conservation Overlay bedroom-limit standards designed to curb dense student rentals — a decision that could invite more variance requests testing the overlay's limits.

stories.headline: USA Today: Pitt's record growth reshapes Oakland with new dorms
stories.text: A USA Today feature profiles the University of Pittsburgh's expansion strategy amid record enrollment, anchored by the approved roughly 450-bed Fifth and Ruskin residence hall targeting LEED Gold certification. The piece also details Pitt's continued reliance on affiliate and block-lease housing arrangements and long-range Campus Master Plan proposals, including a possible conversion of William Pitt Union upper floors to student housing.

stories.headline: College Station rezones 7.2 acres for multifamily, launches townhome pilot
stories.text: College Station's City Council unanimously rezoned 7.2 acres on Harvey Mitchell Parkway South, between Dartmouth Street and Earl Rudder Freeway, from General Commercial to Urban Residential/Multi-Family land use. The same meeting approved a new townhome development incentive pilot program, part of a broader council push toward denser housing types near Texas A&M.

stories.headline: Subtext to break ground on 221-unit Senate Street complex amid Columbia boom
stories.text: St. Louis-based developer Subtext — also behind VERVE Columbia near USC — plans to break ground this summer on a seven-story, 221-unit apartment complex with a 198-space garage at 931 Senate Street, adding to a wave of downtown Columbia development near campus.

stories.headline: Astria Tempe tower tops out near ASU
stories.text: Layton Construction topped out the 27-story Astria Tempe student and multifamily tower near Arizona State University, one of several active projects highlighted in AZBEX's weekly Valley development roundup.

stories.headline: New York developer eyes 155-unit Craig Street project in Oakland
stories.text: Camp Eight Capital has proposed a seven-story, 155-unit apartment building at 143 North Craig Street, replacing a former CMU administrative building within walking distance of Pitt and CMU; a Development Activities Meeting was slated for July 13, the same day Pitt separately prepares to present its own nine-story residence hall project to the city's Planning Commission.

stories.headline: JPI plants $150M flag near Duke with 440-home Jefferson Watts community
stories.text: Multifamily developer JPI acquired a 12.6-acre site on Hillsborough Road near Duke University Medical Center to build Jefferson Watts, a $150 million, 440-home community; groundbreaking is planned for this month with delivery targeted for 2028.

stories.headline: Treo Group wins rezoning for 117-unit "Vox on Red" near UM
stories.text: Developer Treo Group won rezoning approval for a six-story, 117-unit student housing complex called Vox on Red, on a roughly 2.6-acre site on Red Road just west of the University of Miami's main campus.

stories.headline: BYU breaks ground on 11 new married-student buildings at Wymount Terrace
stories.text: Church-owned BYU is razing nine 1962-era buildings on the south section of Wymount Terrace, its on-campus married-student housing district, to make way for 11 new energy-efficient apartment buildings — part of a broader push tied to LDS Church leadership's emphasis on marriage among BYU students. Construction began in July and is expected to take about two years.

stories.headline: Monongalia County fast-tracks West Run rezoning ahead of new state timeline
stories.text: The Monongalia County Commission voted 2-0 to rezone seven parcels along West Run Road in Morgantown from R-1 residential to C-2 general commercial, moving quickly ahead of a new state-mandated 30-day rezoning timeline.

stories.headline: L3 Campus, Declaration Partners form partnership, make first joint UF investment
stories.text: L 3 Campus and Declaration Partners Real Estate announced a new partnership to invest in student housing nationally, with their first joint acquisition bringing L3 Campus's University of Florida portfolio to nearly 1,400 beds. The tie-up pairs L3's campus-market operating platform with Declaration's balance sheet, a structure increasingly common as institutional capital looks for scaled entry points into purpose-built student housing. The Gainesville deal gives the venture an immediate foothold in one of the SEC's largest and fastest-growing student housing markets, and positions the partnership to pursue additional acquisitions as it builds out its national footprint. L3 / Declaration UF Snapshot Combined UF portfolio ~1,400 beds Partnership L3 Campus + Declaration Deal type JV + 1st joint buy

stories.headline: UT trustees lock up 5.6-acre Maplehurst site with five-year holding agreement
stories.text: T he University of Tennessee's Board of Trustees approved a five-year holding and option agreement with the University Financing Foundation covering the 5.6-acre, 199-apartment Maplehurst property on Hill Avenue, just off the Knoxville campus. The structure lets UT control the site's long-term future without an outright purchase, buying time to finalize plans for a mixed-use innovation district combining residential, retail and academic/tech space. The move dovetails with the university's broader campus housing strategy: trustees separately approved a FY2026-27 budget setting aside more than $235 million for on-campus housing redevelopment, funding design work to replace North Carrick, South Carrick and Reese Hall with new residence halls adding roughly 1,500 beds. Maplehurst Site Snapshot Site 5.6 acres / 199 units Structure 5-yr holding & option Counterparty Univ. Financing Fdn. Planned use Mixed-use innovation dist.

stories.headline: Columbia College auctions nine near-downtown properties for about $2 million
stories.text: Columbia College sold nine properties — 21 units, a vacant lot and a building — near downtown Columbia through Atterberry Auction & Realty Group, netting roughly $2 million. A nearby resident voiced concern that private equity buyers could convert the single-family properties into larger apartment buildings.

stories.headline: College Station revisits sale of key Northgate parking lot as prior bids resurface
stories.text: College Station is weighing options again for a 1.57-acre city-owned surface lot at 301 Patricia Street in the Northgate district, near Texas A&M, while trying to preserve the district's character. Prior development bids on the table include $13.5 million from Capstone Collegiate Communities and $10.5 million from Pinnacle/Rountree.

stories.headline: Landmark, CrossHarbor acquire Eugene site, break ground on 1,002-bed project
stories.text: Landmark Properties and CrossHarbor Capital acquired a 2.62-acre site at 1290 Alder Street in Eugene — including a parking deck with ground-floor retail — to develop The Mark Eugene, a 1,002-bed student housing community near the University of Oregon on the former PeaceHealth Hospital site; JLL arranged the land sale and construction financing.

stories.headline: Goodman Real Estate sells two Seattle-area communities for $172M
stories.text: Goodman Real Estate sold Baldwyn Apartments (235 units, Seattle's Northgate neighborhood) and CRU at Willows 124 (195 units, Redmond) for a combined $172 million, with CBRE representing the Seattle-based seller.

stories.headline: USC trustees advance USC Next master plan, name 900-bed McBryde hall "The Commons at Carolina"
stories.text: T he University of South Carolina's Board of Trustees approved its 2026-27 budget and advanced several USC Next master plan projects, including a Russell House student union expansion and a new civil rights center. The board also formally named the 900-bed residence hall on the former McBryde site "The Commons at Carolina," one of the largest additions to on-campus housing capacity in the university's recent history. The Russell House project alone represents a $250 million overhaul funded through state institution bonds and a new $150-per-semester student fee, replacing the aging west wing and Thomson Building with a larger ballroom and expanded dining and student-organization space.
