Together, the approvals signal a sustained wave of campus capital investment in Columbia, arriving the same summer Subtext is breaking ground on its own 221-unit project a short walk from campus. A new $150-per-semester student fee helps fund the university's largest student-life capital project of the year.

stories.headline: UT budgets $235M-plus to replace three residence halls with 1,500 new beds
stories.text: UT's Board of Trustees approved its FY2026-27 operating budget, which sets aside more than $235 million for on-campus housing redevelopment. The funding enables design work to replace North Carrick, South Carrick and Reese Hall with new residence halls adding roughly 1,500 beds — part of the same budget cycle that also approved a new bioinformatics program.

stories.school_name: University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill
stories.headline: UNC hires 'place vision' consultants for Carolina North as System enrollment tops 256,000
stories.text: UNC-Chapel Hill hired Gehl's Blaine Merker and Michael Van Valkenburgh Associates' Gullivar Shepard, working with Executive Director of Real Estate Development Tiffany Lacey, to craft a 'place vision' guiding the long-planned Carolina North expansion. The move comes as panelists at Bisnow's Triangle Student Housing Conference flagged the UNC System's record 256,000 enrollment — up 3.4% from 2024 — as outpacing housing supply, with construction costs up roughly 7% year-over-year across the Carolinas and UNC-Chapel Hill beginning construction this summer on its first new residence hall in decades.

stories.headline: Rutgers approves $6.2B budget, 4% room-and-board increase for 2026-27
stories.text: Rutgers' Board of Governors approved a $6.2 billion operating budget for FY2027, including a 3% tuition increase and a 4% increase in housing and dining charges, from $15,332 to $15,945, for the 2026-27 academic year.

stories.headline: Nebraska regents approve $386M plan to replace Selleck with 1,700-bed hall
stories.text: The University of Nebraska Board of Regents approved a $386 million plan to demolish Selleck Quadrangle and four adjacent 1950s-era buildings on UNL's City Campus, replacing them with a new 1,700-bed student housing complex built in two phases opening in 2030 and 2032.

stories.headline: UM seeks hospital use in 217-page Coral Gables campus agreement rewrite
stories.text: The University of Miami filed a 217-page package of amendments to its 30-year development agreement with Coral Gables, seeking hospital use on campus, a higher campus floor-area ratio, rezoning of adjacent parcels to university-campus designation, and conveyance of a 5.52-acre site to the city for a new park.

stories.headline: UofL approves record $1.96B budget as enrollment heads toward all-time high
stories.text: The University of Louisville's Board of Trustees approved a record $1.96 billion FY2027 budget — a 9.4% increase — including $9 million in added institutional financial aid, as the university anticipates record enrollment of roughly 25,400 students for fall 2026.

stories.headline: State College advances zoning rewrite as council weighs student-housing impact on downtown heights
stories.text: S tate College Borough Council voted to advance draft language for a comprehensive rewrite of its zoning and subdivision ordinances, teeing up one of the more consequential land-use overhauls the University Park market has seen in years. The draft would raise allowable downtown building heights to as many as nine stories and cut parking minimums — changes explicitly designed to incentivize new housing construction near Penn State's flagship campus. Council members split during debate over how the changes would affect the balance between purpose-built student housing and long-term, non-student housing supply downtown, a tension that has shaped State College zoning fights for years. The drafts now head to the borough's planning commission for review, with neighborhood meetings scheduled for July and August and a public hearing tentatively set for November — giving developers a multi-month window to weigh in before any final vote. The ordinance ties directly into density, height and parking — the entitlement levers that determine what's buildable near campus.

stories.headline: LV Collective's eight-story West Main tower clears appeal window, advances to site plan review
stories.text: A student-housing project long fought over in Charlottesville took a decisive step forward this month. Following the city's June 16 certificate of appropriateness approval for LV Collective's eight-story building on West Main Street, no appeals had been filed as of noon on June 18 — the deadline that would have sent the project back to review. That clears the way for the Texas-based developer to move into site plan review, the next major hurdle before permitting. The project sits beside The Standard near the university and has drawn sustained neighborhood pushback over scale, with the developer having already trimmed the design following resident objections. With the appeal window closed, it becomes one of the more advanced purpose-built student housing projects in the Charlottesville/UVA pipeline. No appeals were filed by the noon deadline, clearing West Main Street's eight-story tower for site plan review.

stories.headline: Fifeville student-housing fight persists as officials weigh zoning code changes near UVA
stories.text: Opposition to "The Mark," a student-housing project in Charlottesville's Fifeville neighborhood, has continued past two community meetings, with activists and at least one city councilor signaling the fight is far from resolved. City officials are now considering amendments to Charlottesville's zoning code specific to student housing near campus — a response that could reshape entitlement terms for future purpose-built projects in the corridor.

stories.headline: Austin's new density bonus programs take effect, reaching into West Campus corridor
stories.text: Austin's citywide Density Bonus (DBC) program and an updated Downtown Density Bonus took effect this month, offering developers added building height in exchange for affordable units — incentives that extend into zoning cases near the University of Texas's West Campus corridor. The programs give purpose-built student housing developers a new density lever to weigh against the market's existing University Neighborhood Overlay framework.

stories.headline: FSU trustees approve $3.22B budget with $455M tied to Northwest campus housing project
stories.text: Florida State's Board of Trustees approved a $3.22 billion operating budget for fiscal year 2026-27, including $455 million earmarked for capital projects. A portion of that funding is tied to the Northwest campus student housing, dining and parking project, a 1,200-bed development steadily advancing through the university's capital planning process.

stories.headline: 740 Techwood opens pre-leasing steps from Bobby Dodd Stadium
stories.text: CCI Real Estate has opened pre-leasing applications for 740 Techwood, a 64,000-square-foot, five-story, 55-unit community carrying roughly 95 beds a half-block from Bobby Dodd Stadium. Move-ins are expected for fall 2027, adding a small but tightly located infill project to the Georgia Tech-adjacent supply pipeline.

stories.headline: Auburn council clears 118-acre Noble Hall Plantation restoration
stories.text: Auburn City Council unanimously approved annexations and rezonings covering roughly 118 acres for the Noble Hall Plantation project, a restoration paired with limited residential development led by Jolly Development and the Auburn University Real Estate Foundation.

stories.headline: Seven Madison development proposals head to Plan Commission in July
stories.text: Multiple multifamily projects near UW-Madison and the city's east side — including 163 affordable units near the former Oscar Mayer plant and a 124-unit mixed-use building — are set for Plan Commission review in July.

stories.headline: Daily Texan column ties UT endowment to West Campus landlords, flags stalled overlay reform
stories.text: A Daily Texan column examined UT's investment ties — via UTIMCO and Blackstone — to West Campus student-housing landlords, and flagged the delayed University Neighborhood Overlay density-bonus reforms that continue to shape campus-area development economics.

stories.headline: Lawrence approves $35.3M in industrial revenue bonds for northwest apartment complex
stories.text: Lawrence's City Commission voted 3-1 to approve industrial revenue bonds valued at roughly $35.3 million — a one-time sales-tax exemption on construction materials — for a $37 million, 131-unit townhome-style complex near Wakarusa Drive, developed by Omaha-based Metonic Real Estate Solutions.

stories.headline: Ames Council hears rezoning for 4899 Everest Ave. subdivision
stories.text: The Ames City Council held a hearing on a rezoning and master-plan amendment for The Bluffs, a residential subdivision at 4899 Everest Avenue; the project is general-market residential and not confirmed as student-housing specific.

stories.headline: WVU-adjacent East End Village needs financing reset 'or radically change'
stories.text: The 73-acre East End Village TIF district near WVU's downtown campus — envisioned to draw over $100 million in investment and 300-plus market-rate apartments — remains stalled by rising interest costs and a property dispute; a county development official said the project must move forward or change substantially by fall.

stories.headline: Landmark, CrossHarbor break ground on 1,002-bed Eugene project
stories.text: Landmark Properties and CrossHarbor Capital broke ground on The Mark Eugene, a 272-unit, 1,002-bed student-housing community less than a mile from the University of Oregon — the first phase of a two-phase project ultimately totaling 2,275 beds.

stories.headline: SB 79 takes effect, loosening density limits near future Westwood transit stops
stories.text: California's SB 79 took effect this month, easing development restrictions around major transit stops — including two future D Line stations near UCLA — and opening the door to higher-density housing in Westwood.

stories.headline: BYU builds new married-student housing as Park Plaza redevelopment advances nearby
stories.text: BYU is constructing new married-student housing at Wymount Terrace, while Cole West's separate Park Plaza redevelopment near campus — demolishing a 44-unit 1965 building at 910 N. 900 East — remains in early-stage discussions with city officials.

stories.headline: Tailwind Group adds 1,300-plus beds with two Norman acquisitions
stories.text: T ailwind Group acquired two student-housing communities in Norman — The Overlook (796 beds) and The 2900 Student Apartments (516 beds) — adding more than 1,300 beds in a single stroke near the University of Oklahoma. The deals mark Tailwind's third and fourth acquisitions of 2026, continuing the operator's pattern of concentrated buys in Big 12/SEC football markets. Both properties are slated for renovation starting this fall. Norman Portfolio Snapshot The Overlook 796 beds The 2900 Student Apts 516 beds Total beds added 1,312+ 2026 deal count 4th (Tailwind)

stories.headline: Hackberry Lane pays $16.9M for four Fayetteville student properties
stories.text: A n affiliate of Hackberry Lane, a Brooklyn-based firm focused on off-campus student housing, purchased four multifamily properties in Fayetteville — Whitham Cottages, North Cedar Townhomes, Hughes Townhomes and Deane Sang Townhomes — totaling 44 units for $16.9 million, or roughly $384,090 per unit. The deal was financed with a $13 million loan from Alliant Credit Union, giving the buyer a scattered-site foothold in one of the SEC's tightest student-housing markets. Fayetteville Portfolio Snapshot Price $16.9M Units 44 Price / unit $384,090 Financing $13M (Alliant CU)

stories.headline: Athens-Clarke County opens $2.7M affordable housing funding round
stories.text: Athens-Clarke County will distribute nearly $3 million in SPLOST funding for affordable housing infrastructure — roads, sidewalks and sewer lines — with proposals due July 24 from nonprofit and private developers working near the UGA market.

stories.headline: The Hall CP changes hands near College Park's future Purple Line stop
stories.text: A College Park food hall near the Hotel at the University of Maryland transferred its liquor license to new owner The Lakelander Group; the site sits near a future Purple Line stop and the new Discovery House graduate-housing development.

stories.headline: Pitt buys former Hemingway's building steps from Litchfield Towers
stories.text: The University of Pittsburgh purchased the Forbes Avenue property that housed Hemingway's Cafe for more than 40 years, located adjacent to Litchfield Towers — near the block where Pitt's Campus Master Plan proposes a new "Tower D" to expand first-year student housing.

stories.headline: USC trustees approve Phase I of $250M Russell House student union overhaul
stories.text: T he University of South Carolina's board of trustees approved Phase I of a $250 million overhaul of the Russell House student union on June 19, funded through state institution bonds and a new $150-per-semester student fee — one of the largest campus-life capital projects moving through the Columbia market this year. The plan replaces the aging west wing and Thomson Building with a larger ballroom, more student-organization space and expanded dining capacity, positioning the university to compete for enrollment growth with upgraded on-campus amenities that indirectly reinforce demand for surrounding student housing. A new $150-per-semester student fee helps fund the university's largest student-life capital project of the year.

stories.headline: 40-plus capital projects underway at Illinois this summer
stories.text: The University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign is running more than 40 active facility and infrastructure capital projects this summer, including residence hall restroom renovations and phases III and IV of the Illini Hall replacement and Altgeld Hall renovation — a heavy construction season underscoring the university's ongoing campus reinvestment.

stories.headline: Charlottesville hears calls to strip student-housing fee designation
stories.text: At a June 23-25 Planning Commission listening session on Development Code changes, former commissioner Genevieve Keller and Preservation Piedmont's Jean Hiatt called for eliminating the student-housing designation that gives projects like The Mark reduced affordable-housing fees, citing impacts on historically Black neighborhoods near UVA — a potential shift that would raise costs on future purpose-built projects.

stories.headline: KU tops out stadium bowl steel on Gateway District P3
stories.text: The University of Kansas, Edgemoor/Sunflower Partners and the Clark-JE Dunn joint venture celebrated topping out more than 1,200 tons of structural steel for the east stadium bowl — part of Gateway District Phase 2, a P3 that will deliver a 162-room hotel, 450 beds of student housing, and retail, office and restaurant space alongside the reconstructed stadium, with full district completion targeted for 2028.

stories.headline: Manhattan approves STAR Bond, TIF districts for $297.6M Edge District
stories.text: The Manhattan City Commission approved a STAR Bond district and a TIF district to help finance the Kansas State University Foundation-led Edge District (Edge 3.0), an estimated $297.6 million mixed academic, commercial and entertainment development at Champions Gate across from Bill Snyder Family Stadium, also covering the Bilbrey Event Center and K-State Indoor Track facility seating.
stories.source: City of Manhattan / local news coverage

stories.headline: UT Knoxville trustees hold tuition flat in FY27 budget tied to campus growth plans
stories.text: UT's Board of Trustees approved its FY2027 budget, holding in-state tuition flat while raising minimum staff wages to $18/hour — action that followed the board's earlier approval of major campus growth and housing projects.

stories.headline: Daily Texan opinion piece pushes UT toward retrofits over new construction
stories.text: A Daily Texan opinion column questioned the pace of UT's campus construction and argued for retrofitting existing buildings over continued new-building expansion amid the university's growth-driven capital plans.

stories.headline: Neighbors press Vanderbilt on scale of 43-acre Innovation District
stories.text: The Hillsboro-West End Neighborhood Association is asking Vanderbilt to consider reduced building heights and scale for its proposed 43-acre, multi-building Innovation District ahead of Metro Council's Aug. 4 second reading.

stories.headline: State College council advances comprehensive zoning rewrite as Penn State plans enrollment growth
stories.text: S tate College Borough Council voted unanimously Monday to advance a draft comprehensive zoning ordinance and subdivision and land development ordinance to the planning commission for review—one of the more consequential land-use actions in the University Park market in recent memory. Council framed the rewrite as an effort to balance student demand against long-term resident housing as Penn State signals plans to grow enrollment at University Park. For purpose-built student housing developers, the draft code's treatment of density, height and parking near campus will function as a direct entitlement lever on what becomes buildable. The unanimous referral opens a formal review window before council takes final action. Council advanced the draft unanimously for planning-commission review amid Penn State's planned University Park enrollment increase.

stories.headline: 320-unit, 960-bed 'Theory Sterling' twin towers head to Columbia planning commission
stories.text: A roughly three-acre, 320-unit student-housing project branded Theory Sterling went before Columbia's Planning and Zoning Commission, proposing two towers at University and College avenues near the University of Missouri. At about 960 beds, the development would add meaningful purpose-built supply to the Columbia market. The proposal is the latest in a string of student-housing projects pitched near Mizzou's campus, testing the city's appetite for high-density vertical product at a prominent gateway intersection. Theory Sterling Snapshot Beds ~960 Units 320 Site ~3 acres Towers 2

stories.headline: LV Collective scales West Main tower to 8 stories for Charlottesville review
stories.text: Texas-based LV Collective's proposed student-housing building on a West Main Street parking lot beside The Standard went before Charlottesville's Board of Architectural Review on June 16 for a Certificate of Appropriateness. After months of neighborhood pushback, the developer scaled the design from 11 to 8 stories—six on the Westhaven-facing side.

stories.headline: Vanderbilt's 40-acre West End innovation district clears first council reading
stories.text: A bill enabling Vanderbilt's 40-acre innovation neighborhood cleared its first reading before Nashville's Metro Council, with a second reading set for Aug. 4. The plan blends housing with research facilities on land near the university's West End edge—an early but watchable entitlement step for a major mixed-use district.

stories.headline: Fifeville residents vote 72-0 against 'The Mark' near UVA
stories.text: Residents packed First Baptist Church on June 22 to oppose The Mark, a seven-story, 180-unit project (~730 tenants) aimed largely at UVA students in the Fifeville neighborhood. A community straw vote came back 72 against and zero in favor, with another meeting scheduled for June 24—signaling sustained entitlement risk on the site.

stories.headline: Lawsuit seeks to halt $600M TIF for OU-area entertainment district
stories.text: Residents filed suit seeking an injunction against roughly $600 million in public TIF funding for the Rock Creek Entertainment District near the University of Oklahoma arena—a project that includes a housing component. The litigation adds entitlement and financing risk to the Norman development.

stories.headline: JLL arranges $63.75M refi for 820-bed Vista Starkville
stories.text: JLL secured a $63.75 million refinancing through QuadReal for The Vista Starkville, an 820-bed community serving Mississippi State that was 97% occupied. The deal lands as MSU reports record enrollment of 23,563.

stories.headline: IU trustees approve FY27 budget and two housing projects
stories.text: The Indiana University Board of Trustees approved its FY2027 operating budget and policy revisions at a June 12 meeting, advancing two student-housing projects—a Willkie Quad renovation in Bloomington and a new Indianapolis residence hall.

stories.headline: Houston ranks among lowest-preleased student markets
stories.text: Houston remained among the nation's lowest-preleased student-housing markets in the June National Student Housing Report, with preleasing at 28.1% as of March 2026—a soft-absorption flag for underwriters in the market.

stories.headline: PCCP–Dinerstein JV buys 1,128-bed Sterling College Station near Texas A&M
stories.text: A joint venture between PCCP and The Dinerstein Companies acquired two adjacent purpose-built communities near Texas A&M, combining them into the 350-unit, 1,128-bed Sterling College Station. The buyers have a renovation program planned—a value-add play in one of the SEC's deepest enrollment markets. The trade was among the larger College Station student-housing deals reported in June, pairing scale with a repositioning business plan. Sterling College Station Beds 1,128 Units 350 Market College Station, TX Plan Value-add reno

stories.headline: Scion Group to acquire Student Quarters' ~$1.5B, ~13,000-bed platform
stories.text: T he Scion Group announced June 10 that it will acquire Student Quarters' operating platform—roughly $1.5 billion and about 13,000 beds across 21 markets. Among the included assets is Lofts on 8th in Tempe, serving Arizona State University. The transaction is one of the largest operator consolidations of the cycle, extending Scion's national management footprint across multiple Power-conference markets in a single stroke. Scion / Student Quarters Platform value ~$1.5B Beds ~13,000 Markets 21 ASU asset Lofts on 8th

stories.headline: Noble 2500 at UT Austin folded into Scion–Student Quarters deal
stories.text: Scion's acquisition of the Student Quarters platform includes Noble 2500, a 117-unit, 243-bed community serving the University of Texas at Austin—extending Scion's reach into one of the country's largest enrollment markets.

stories.headline: Hackberry Lane closes six acquisitions, adds Fayetteville beds
stories.text: Hackberry Lane closed six student-housing acquisitions across Gainesville, FL and Fayetteville, AR, adding roughly 400 beds of townhome, cottage and boutique apartment product. The buys lift its owned portfolio to about 2,000 beds since 2023.

stories.headline: Tailwind buys 732-bed Milestone Stillwater, its third in market
stories.text: Tailwind Group acquired the 732-bed Milestone Stillwater near Oklahoma State, with a renovation and full rebrand beginning fall 2026. It is Tailwind's third Stillwater asset since 2020, deepening the operator's concentration in the market.

stories.school_name: University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill
stories.headline: UNC taps Ayers Saint Gross for 230-acre Carolina North master plan
stories.text: T he UNC Board of Trustees selected Ayers Saint Gross to lead master planning for the 230-acre Carolina North campus expansion and named an advisory committee to guide the effort. The first phase is slated to include student and family housing. A master-planning award at this scale is high-value early intel for developers tracking the Chapel Hill market, signaling a multi-year pipeline with a defined housing component well ahead of any solicitation.

stories.headline: Penn State places students in supplemental housing amid Fall 2026 overcapacity
stories.text: Penn State University Park moved students into supplemental housing as on-campus demand exceeded capacity for Fall 2026, underscoring continued enrollment-driven pressure on the State College housing market—and reinforcing the demand backdrop behind the borough's zoning rewrite.

stories.headline: State College advances sweeping zoning overhaul as Penn State eyes 10,000-student freshman classes
stories.text: S tate College Borough Council has advanced a new comprehensive zoning ordinance to review agencies, setting up one of the most consequential land-use rewrites in the University Park market in years. Council members framed the overhaul around mounting concerns over student housing supply and affordability as Penn State signals intent to expand enrollment. Borough officials noted the university is committed to growing University Park enrollment, with discussion of pushing freshman classes toward 10,000 students per year. Officials acknowledged that purpose-built student housing developers are the principal parties seeking to build under the revised code—making the ordinance's density, height and parking provisions a direct lever on future PBSH feasibility. The referral to review agencies begins a formal comment window before council takes final action. For developers underwriting State College sites, the rewrite is a gating entitlement variable: terms governing by-right density near campus could materially reshape what is buildable.

stories.headline: IU trustees approve $60M Willkie Quad renovation, partner on 448-bed Indianapolis hall
stories.text: T he Indiana University Board of Trustees on June 12 approved a comprehensive housing package spanning two campuses. At IU Bloomington, the university will invest $60 million to fully renovate the 752-bed Willkie Quadrangle—a 1965-vintage residence hall—overhauling student rooms and renewing elevators, roofs, and mechanical, electrical, plumbing and life-safety systems. Completion is targeted for 2029. In Indianapolis, IU will partner with a private developer to construct and operate a new 448-bed residence hall at 441 W. Michigan St., extending purpose-built capacity to the urban campus. The developer-led structure signals appetite for P3-style delivery on the Indianapolis footprint. IU Housing Package Willkie Quad reno $60M / 752 beds Indianapolis hall 448 beds (P3) Willkie completion 2029

stories.headline: Core Spaces plots 3,500-plus beds across three Green Street projects at Illinois
stories.text: C ore Spaces, the developer founded by three University of Illinois alumni, is preparing a major expansion of its Champaign footprint, targeting more than 3,500 purpose-built beds delivered between 2028 and 2031. The pipeline builds on the firm's 1,577-bed Hub Champaign Green Street high-rise and adds two further Green Street projects totaling roughly 2,000 beds in Campustown. The concentration of new supply on a single corridor is notable for underwriting: a 3,500-bed wave over three delivery years will test absorption and rent durability in the Urbana-Champaign submarket, even against Illinois's enrollment base. More than 3,500 beds aimed at a single Campustown corridor between 2028 and 2031.

stories.headline: Clemson council passes first reading of 555-bed Pine Street project on razor-thin vote
stories.text: C lemson City Council approved the first reading of a proposed Pine Street student-housing complex on a contentious split, with the measure clearing 3 in favor and 3 against—one abstention counted as a yes. The project would deliver about 555 beds across 159 units, plus roughly 6,000 square feet of retail and 200-plus parking spaces in the downtown core. The divided vote underscores the entitlement risk attached to downtown Clemson density. A first reading is only the opening procedural step; the slim margin signals subsequent readings could draw amendments or conditions before final approval. Pine Street Snapshot Beds ~555 Units 159 Retail 6,000 sf Parking 200+ First reading 3-3, abstention = yes

stories.headline: Fayetteville rezones two N. Hall Ave. parcels for infill near campus
stories.text: Fayetteville City Council approved rezonings at 800 and 1002 N. Hall Ave.—adjacent to the University of Arkansas and Leverett Elementary—shifting both from single-family to Urban Neighborhood zoning on 7-1 votes. The change supports infill housing and neighborhood commercial uses near campus, over resident objections citing density and traffic.

stories.headline: Pitt set to begin site work on 450-bed first-year residence hall
stories.text: Site preparation on the University of Pittsburgh's planned 450-bed first-year residence hall at Fifth and Ruskin was slated to begin June 15, days after Pitt presented the plan to the city's Zoning Board of Adjustment on June 11. The university is concurrently ending its Hampton Inn student-housing lease this summer following a zoning ruling.

stories.headline: Maryland's 741-bed Discovery House delivers first new grad housing since 1995
stories.text: Discovery House, a 741-bed graduate community developed by Mosaic Partners, opens in August 2026—the first new university-affiliated graduate housing at the University of Maryland since 1995. The community is part of a $148.75 million project with Campus Apartments, with rents ranging from $995 to $1,790 per month. Discovery House Beds 741 (grad) Project cost $148.75M Rents $995–$1,790/mo Opens Aug 2026

stories.headline: USC's McBryde replacement heads to Columbia design review with 1,036 beds
stories.text: The University of South Carolina's plan to replace the McBryde dormitory and add a wing to the Honors College residence hall goes before Columbia's Design and Development Review Commission on June 26. The project would bring 1,036 new student beds near Thomas Cooper Library by 2028. University Architect Derek Gruner outlined the plan at a June 20 trustees meeting, noting the new beds could allow the deteriorating existing stock to be retired.

stories.headline: Arizona shrinks newest dorm to nine stories, keeps 1,300-bed count
stories.text: The University of Arizona's first-year housing development at Speedway and Campbell will rise nine stories—down from an originally planned 19—while still housing 1,300 students and including a dining hall. The Collegiate Housing Foundation is funding the project and will recoup costs over roughly 50 years through student fees. Opening is targeted for fall 2028.

stories.headline: Luxury student housing spreads near Michigan, sharpening affordability debate
stories.text: High-end student housing is proliferating near the University of Michigan—projects including Vic Village North/South, VERVE, Saga and The Legacy—as developers push private-bedroom units paired with wellness and amenity space. The wave is drawing mixed reactions and raising affordability questions across the Ann Arbor and East Lansing campus markets.

stories.headline: Communities press for affordable housing in Stanford growth plan
stories.text: Stanford is refining its General Use Permit application—comprising 2.275 million square feet of academic space and 3,150 housing units/beds—ahead of Santa Clara County Board of Supervisors review, with an estimated 20-year buildout. Surrounding communities are pushing for a larger affordable-housing commitment as a condition of approval.

stories.headline: Koelbel closes financing on 65-unit Boulder County affordable project
stories.text: Koelbel and Company closed financing on the 65-unit Spine Road income-restricted rental project in Gunbarrel. Construction begins this month with completion targeted for Q4 2027.

stories.headline: Evanston council takes final vote on 30-unit Emerson Street project
stories.text: Evanston City Council was set to take final action June 22 on a five-story, 30-unit apartment at 1103-05 Emerson St.—three units affordable—replacing two 19th-century buildings near Northwestern.

stories.headline: IU trustees pass 2027 budget, hold $118M in cuts
stories.text: IU's 2027 budget maintains $118 million in cuts to offset lost state and federal funding, leaning on IU Foundation funds and athletics revenue. The $60M Willkie and Indianapolis housing projects were approved within the same meeting.

stories.headline: Vanderbilt to sell up to $430M in tax-exempt bonds
stories.text: Vanderbilt plans to sell up to $430 million of tax-exempt bonds through a Tennessee local-government agency in July to fund capital projects, with BofA as book-running senior manager.

stories.headline: Oregon to cut ~$65M, close two residence halls
stories.text: University of Oregon trustees approved a $1.55B operating budget but flagged roughly $65M in cuts amid declining out-of-state enrollment and tuition revenue, including the closure of two residence halls. Trustees requested an amended plan by Dec. 15.

stories.headline: UW regents lift 2026-27 cost of attendance
stories.text: UW regents approved 2026-27 first-year cost of attendance in June, with resident undergraduate tuition rising 3.3%—a marginal lift to total cost of attendance that includes housing.

stories.headline: PCCP, Dinerstein JV lands 1,128 beds near Texas A&M as Sterling College Station
stories.text: A joint venture between PCCP and The Dinerstein Companies acquired two adjacent purpose-built communities totaling 1,128 beds across 350 units on 44 acres roughly 2.5 miles from Texas A&M. The assets have been combined and rebranded as Sterling College Station, with a comprehensive renovation and operational-improvement program planned. The trade is one of the larger College Station student-housing deals of the cycle, pairing scale with a value-add business plan in one of the SEC's deepest enrollment markets. Sterling College Station Beds 1,128 Units 350 Site 44 acres Distance ~2.5 mi to A&M

stories.headline: Balfour Beatty buys 288-bed Clemson Village for $26M
stories.text: Balfour Beatty Communities acquired Clemson Village, a 96-unit, 288-bed community serving Clemson, from Blue Vista for $26 million—about $270,833 per unit. The purchase marks Balfour Beatty's second ACC-market student-housing acquisition.

stories.headline: Tailwind adds 732-bed Milestone Stillwater, its third in market
stories.text: Tailwind Group acquired the 732-bed Milestone Stillwater near Oklahoma State, with a full rebrand and renovation beginning fall 2026 and completing spring 2027. The deal is Tailwind's third Stillwater asset.

stories.headline: Rockpoint acquires 97-unit Wilshire Margot in Westwood near UCLA
stories.text: Boston-based Rockpoint acquired Wilshire Margot, a 97-unit Westwood mid-rise near UCLA, from NMS Residential, with plans for a value-add repositioning in supply-constrained West Los Angeles. The trade ties to student demand near UCLA (fall 2025 enrollment ~46,678) and follows the recent Axiom Westwood student-housing sale.

stories.headline: NY investor buys 65-unit Mansfield complex near UConn for $14.15M
stories.text: Carriage House Townhomes, a 65-unit, 17-building complex at 183 Huntington Lodge Road in Mansfield near UConn, sold for $14.15 million to a New York investor, with the deed filed in June.

stories.headline: U District office complex trades for $27M after $157M peak basis
stories.text: Seattle's two-building Roosevelt Commons office complex in the U District (4311 11th Ave NE / 4300 Roosevelt Way NE) sold for $27 million per King County records—a steep markdown from a prior $157 million basis, underscoring repricing pressure on aging office near campus that could invite conversion interest.

stories.headline: Arizona dorm loses 10 floors, gains 100 beds under CHF financing structure
stories.text: A revised plan for a new University of Arizona dorm trims 10 floors but adds about 100 beds, reflecting a redesign under its nonprofit financing partner. The Collegiate Housing Foundation—an Alabama-based nonprofit developer—purchased the Palm Shadows property from Mortenson in 2026. Under its agreement with the university, the project will be financed through student-housing revenue over roughly 40 years. The structure is a textbook nonprofit/63-20-style P3: the university avoids direct balance-sheet debt while CHF amortizes the project against a long-dated housing-revenue stream—an increasingly common delivery model across the Big 12.

stories.headline: Kansas advances $75M residence hall, P3 solicitation expected late 2026
stories.text: The University of Kansas's $75 million residence hall is in final design, with a public-private partnership solicitation anticipated in late 2026 and construction to follow developer selection. The forthcoming RFP is high-value intel for developers tracking the Big 12 P3 pipeline. P3 solicitation anticipated late 2026, construction to follow developer selection.

stories.headline: USC board names 900-bed 'Commons at Carolina,' advances USC Next plan
stories.text: USC trustees approved their 2026-27 budget June 19, advancing USC Next master-plan projects. The board named the 900-bed former McBryde-site residential building 'The Commons at Carolina,' approved purchase of 12.6 acres adjacent to Founders Park for parking and possible future development, and adopted a tuition freeze alongside a $133 average housing increase for fall 2026.

stories.headline: Mizzou's 960-Bed Theory Sterling Tower Advances to Columbia Council
stories.text: Columbia's Planning and Zoning Commission voted unanimously to forward Theory Sterling Mizzou to the City Council, clearing a key hurdle for one of the largest purpose-built projects proposed near the University of Missouri in years. The plan calls for roughly 320 units and about 960 beds across two towers rising as high as eight stories at the intersection of University and College avenues, on the eastern edge of campus. The 2.91-acre assemblage would require demolishing the existing University Place Apartments along with a neighborhood barber shop and a block of graduate housing — a clearance package that has become a flashpoint in the broader debate over density and displacement in Columbia's central corridor. With P&Z's endorsement secured, the decisive vote now shifts to the Council. For developers underwriting the Mizzou market, the project's scale is notable against a backdrop of record preleasing: the campus ran near the top of the national leaderboard for the 2026–27 cycle, and a 960-bed addition is a meaningful supply signal for owners pricing new starts in the submarket. Theory Sterling Mizzou — Project Snapshot Units ~320 Beds ~960 Towers / max height 2 / 8 stories Site 2.91 acres Location University & College Ave. Status P&Z → City Council

stories.headline: Ann Arbor Approves 285-Unit, 10-Story Tower on West Huron
stories.text: The Ann Arbor Planning Commission approved both the rezoning and site plan for a ten-story, 285-unit apartment building at 315 West Huron Street, advancing one of the larger downtown residential projects in the University of Michigan market. The mixed-use plan pairs the residential program with ground-floor retail and a rooftop bar, reinforcing the downtown core's push toward vertical density. The dual approval — rezoning and site plan in a single action — removes a major entitlement contingency and positions the project to move toward construction. For investors tracking Ann Arbor, the decision signals continued municipal appetite for height in the downtown district serving one of the Big Ten's strongest enrollment bases. "Ten stories and 285 units approved in a single action — rezoning and site plan cleared together on West Huron."

stories.headline: $94.9M UCF Project Tops Out in Orlando
stories.text: Project teams marked the topping out of a five-story student housing building in Orlando's Quadrangle office park serving the University of Central Florida. The $94.9 million development is led by Deven Group in partnership with Castle Lanterra, and the milestone signals vertical completion of the structure ahead of interior buildout in one of the country's largest enrollment markets. UCF Quadrangle — Snapshot Cost $94.9M Stories 5 Developer Deven Group Capital partner Castle Lanterra

stories.headline: Gilbane Reaches Financial Close on 756-Bed OU Community
stories.text: Gilbane Development, alongside Coleraine Capital Group and with financing from Santander and Fifth Third Bank, reached financial close on a 298-unit, 756-bed purpose-built community on a 33-acre site about 0.7 miles from the University of Oklahoma. The team broke ground in June 2026 with completion targeted for fall 2028. Gilbane cited OU enrollment growth of 10.1% in 2025 as a core demand driver. OU Purpose-Built — Snapshot Units / beds 298 / 756 Site 33 acres Lenders Santander, Fifth Third Delivery Fall 2028

stories.headline: UC Builds Largest-Ever Housing Project: $326M, 1,300+ Beds
stories.text: The University of Cincinnati is constructing a $326 million, 546,606-square-foot residence hall complex — designated Block 1 and Block 2 — near its Uptown campus. The buildings topped out this spring and will add more than 1,300 beds, with occupancy targeted for fall 2027. UC has framed the complex as its largest housing project to date.

stories.headline: Theory Sterling Would Clear University Place Apartments
stories.text: The Theory Sterling Mizzou plan would span 2.91 acres and require demolishing University Place Apartments, a barber shop and graduate housing to make way for 305–320 units near campus — the teardown package now central to the project's community debate.

stories.headline: P&Z Deadlocks 3-3 on Rock Quarry's The Retreat
stories.text: Columbia's Planning and Zoning Commission split 3-3 on The Retreat, a 194-unit student housing proposal on 32.7 acres near Rock Quarry Road, after residents raised traffic and safety concerns. The tie means the project advances to the City Council with no recommendation.

stories.headline: Traffic Worries Stall 194-Unit Retreat Plan
stories.text: The Retreat at Columbia — 194 units on 32.7 acres with 731 parking spaces north of Gray Oak Drive — stalled on the tie vote as commissioners and neighbors flagged traffic load and single-entrance access risks along Rock Quarry Road.

stories.headline: Student Quarters Lands $63.8M Refi on Vista Starkville
stories.text: Student Quarters secured $63.8 million in refinancing — a three-year floating-rate loan originated by QuadReal and brokered by JLL — for The Vista Starkville, an 820-bed community a half-mile from Mississippi State and Davis Wade Stadium. The recap follows The Scion Group's pending acquisition of Student Quarters' operating business, expected to close in Q3, with MSU at a record 23,563 enrollment.

stories.headline: Lane Partners Adds 400 For-Sale Units to Parkline Plan
stories.text: Lane Partners has revised its Parkline plan for the 64-acre former SRI campus near Stanford in Menlo Park, adding nearly 400 for-sale units atop the 800 rentals already planned. The shift moves the research-campus site decisively toward a housing-led redevelopment.

stories.headline: 640-Bed 'Blume on Ivy' to Open Near UVA in 2027
stories.text: Up Campus Student Living is building Blume on Ivy, a 10-story, 231-unit, 640-bed luxury student building at 2117 Ivy Road in UVA's Ivy Corridor on the former Truist Bank site. Leasing opened in spring 2026 ahead of a fall 2027 delivery, amid local debate over luxury student supply and neighborhood displacement.

stories.school_name: Virginia Polytechnic Institute and State University
stories.headline: Construction Set to Begin on VT Residence Halls
stories.text: A Virginia Tech facilities notice announced the start of construction on the university's New Residence Halls project in Blacksburg. The notice confirms the project's transition from approval into active site work this summer. (Month and year confirmed via the notice; the exact day is inferred from the notice slug, not page-confirmed.)

stories.headline: Residents Press Back on Two Columbia Proposals
stories.text: Residents voiced concerns over two proposed Columbia student housing developments — Theory Sterling and the Rock Quarry Road project — as both moved through Planning and Zoning review, underscoring the entitlement friction now attaching to large campus-adjacent projects in the Mizzou market.

stories.headline: Rock Quarry Neighbors Cite Single-Entrance Risk
stories.text: Neighbors voiced fears over The Retreat plan on Rock Quarry Road, pointing to added traffic and the safety risk of a single-entrance design on the 32.7-acre site — the concerns that ultimately deadlocked the commission vote.

stories.headline: Rockpoint Buys 97-Unit Westwood Building Near UCLA for $61.5M
stories.text: Boston-based Rockpoint has acquired Wilshire Margot, a 97-unit apartment building in Westwood near UCLA, from NMS Residential for roughly $61.5 million. The trade pencils to about $634,000 per unit, a marker for institutional pricing on infill multifamily in one of Los Angeles's densest university submarkets. For owners tracking the UCLA market, the deal is a read on continued institutional appetite for well-located Westwood product even as broader transaction volume stays selective — and on the willingness of larger sponsors to underwrite premium per-unit bases in supply-constrained, demand-rich campus corridors. Wilshire Margot — Trade Snapshot Price ~$61.5M Units 97 Implied / unit ~$634,000 Buyer Rockpoint Seller NMS Residential

stories.headline: UW Tacoma Picks Maslow's for $115M P3 Housing Expansion
stories.text: The University of Washington has selected Maslow's Campus Communities as its development partner for a $115 million public-private student housing and dining project at UW Tacoma. The selection moves the long-discussed expansion into active development and represents one of the more significant P3 awards in the Pacific Northwest this year. The combined housing-and-dining program, targeted to open in late 2029, is a high-value intel point for operators tracking university partnership pipelines: it pairs a public institution's residential demand with a private developer's balance sheet, the structure increasingly favored by enrollment-growing campuses that prefer to keep new beds off their own books. UW Tacoma P3 — Snapshot Investment $115M Partner Maslow's Campus Communities Program Housing + dining Target opening Late 2029

stories.school_name: Virginia Polytechnic Institute and State University
stories.headline: VT Board Approves Four New Halls, Preserves Living-Learning
stories.text: At its June 2–3 meeting, the Virginia Tech Board of Visitors approved four new residence halls totaling roughly 1,200 beds near Duck Pond Drive, with occupancy targeted across the 2028–29 academic years. The board also voted to preserve the university's living-learning communities — programs administrators argue help attract students and sustain demand for purpose-built on-campus beds.

stories.headline: Reese Hall Closes; 1,000-Bed Torchbearer Hall Opens
stories.text: After 60 years, the University of Tennessee will close Reese Hall this summer, retiring its last all-female residence hall. It is replaced by the newly built Torchbearer Hall, a co-ed building housing 1,000 freshmen beginning fall 2026 — capacity expansion that tracks UT's climbing admissions volume.

stories.headline: Communities Press Stanford on Affordable Housing
stories.text: Surrounding-community leaders are pushing Stanford to include substantial affordable housing in its StanfordNext growth plan ahead of an August 2026 county application — a political variable that could shape the affordability mix of any new campus-edge residential supply.

stories.headline: Utah Students Question On-Campus Housing Demand
stories.text: University of Utah students raised concerns about rising housing costs, mandatory meal plans and vacant dorm rooms even as the U pursues a plan to double on-campus housing and become a residential campus — a demand-side caution worth weighing against the expansion thesis.

stories.headline: Core Spaces Stakes 3,500-Bed Claim on Champaign, Tripling Footprint by 2031
stories.text: Core Spaces, the Chicago-based developer-investor that has become the most active brand in the Big Ten purpose-built sector, has disclosed plans to add more than 3,500 student housing beds in Champaign across three new developments scheduled for delivery between 2028 and 2031 — an expansion that would materially reshape the supply curve adjacent to the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign campus. The announcement, made Tuesday, marks one of the largest single-market commitments by any operator in the current cycle and follows Core Spaces' existing Hub and oLiv-branded inventory in Champaign. The phased delivery schedule indicates a measured absorption strategy designed to stagger new beds against enrollment growth and the natural turnover of older Class B/C product near campus. Champaign Pipeline Snapshot New beds announced 3,500+ Number of projects 3 Delivery window 2028 – 2031 Developer Core Spaces Adjacent campus U. of Illinois UC

stories.school_name: Virginia Polytechnic Institute and State University
stories.headline: Virginia Tech Board Authorizes Four New Halls Totaling 1,200 Beds; Construction Begins This Summer
stories.text: The Virginia Tech Board of Visitors at its June 2–3 meeting approved construction authorization for four new five-story residence halls totaling approximately 1,200 beds along Duck Pond Drive on the south end of campus. Bids were received in early May, allowing the institution to move directly to summer 2026 construction start with a target completion that supports the 2028–29 academic year. In a separate vote, the board stepped back from an April resolution that had questioned the financial viability of the university's living-learning communities, instead reaffirming the LLP model after the provost argued the programs are a recruiting differentiator. The combined actions signal a meaningful expansion in on-campus inventory at one of the Commonwealth's fastest-growing flagship campuses. Duck Pond Drive Project New beds ~1,200 Buildings 4 (5-story each) Construction start Summer 2026 Funding mechanism Self-supporting (housing revenue)

stories.headline: Landmark Wins 7–2 Zone Change for 974-Bed Davis Park Complex Near UK
stories.text: The Lexington-Fayette Urban County Planning Commission voted 7–2 on June 3 to approve a zone change that allows Landmark Properties to proceed with a 326-unit, 974-bed student apartment complex in the Davis Park neighborhood adjacent to the University of Kentucky campus. The site plan calls for two buildings of five and six stories connected by an overhead pedestrian bridge. The split vote reflects neighborhood pushback over density and traffic but ultimately favored the developer's case that the parcel sits within walking distance of UK and is an appropriate location for purpose-built student housing under the city's current comp plan. Final site-plan approvals and building permits remain the next milestones for Landmark.

stories.headline: U. of Arizona Cuts Dorm Tower from 19 to 9 Stories, Adds 100 Beds in Redesign
stories.text: The University of Arizona has revised its planned first-year residence hall at Speedway Boulevard and Campbell Avenue, reducing the building from a 19-story tower to a nine-story structure while raising the bed count to approximately 1,400 from an earlier 1,300-bed program. The plan revision follows community design feedback and is intended to reduce visual impact on the neighborhood while preserving capacity needed to backstop incoming freshman cohorts.

stories.headline: UW-Madison Opens RFP for New Residence Hall; Proposals Due July 16
stories.text: The State of Wisconsin issued a request for proposals on May 14 for a new residence hall at UW-Madison, with all contractor proposals due July 16. University officials are targeting a 2028 completion, citing chronic capacity shortfalls driven by sustained enrollment growth that has pushed UW's residence halls to operating at or above stated capacity for multiple consecutive cycles.

stories.headline: Core Spaces Walks Away from 2,000-Bed Cincinnati Uptown Project
stories.text: Core Spaces has stepped away from its planned ~2,000-bed development on roughly eight acres at the former Hollister Recreation Center site at Vine Street and East McMillan, sitting kitty-corner to the University of Cincinnati's own $330M student housing high-rise. The original program contemplated 551 apartments and 1,996 beds. Local coverage indicates the site's future is now uncertain as the city looks for a new master developer. The withdrawal is notable in light of Core Spaces' simultaneous expansion at Illinois (above) and underscores a bifurcating capital-allocation pattern across Tier 1 markets: deeper bets where pricing and entitlements align, full exits where they do not.

stories.headline: Quarterra/MacNaughton 796-Unit U-District Tower Advances to Vertical
stories.text: Quarterra and MacNaughton have completed mass excavation and begun slab-on-grade pours on their 796-unit, three-building mid-rise at 3020 NE 45th Street in Seattle's University District, immediately adjacent to U Village. The complex rises to 7–8 stories.

stories.headline: Syracuse Continues 570-Bed Dorm Build Through Summer
stories.text: Construction on Syracuse's new 570-bed residence hall at 544 University Place (206,000 sf, six stories) continues through summer break with a 2027 target. A second dining-and-residence facility at 315 Waverly Avenue is also slated for August 2027 completion; DellPlain Hall renovations are underway.

stories.headline: Stavroff Files for 6-Story Apartment at Former Tommy's Pizza Site
stories.text: Stavroff Land & Development has requested approval to build a six-story multi-unit apartment building at 174 West Lane Avenue (corner of West Lane and Neil), proposing structured parking, leasing/amenity space, and ground-floor activation at the former Tommy's Pizza site adjacent to Ohio State's campus core.

stories.headline: Whitmer Commits $29M to 330-Unit Ann Arbor Affordable High-Rise
stories.text: The Michigan Strategic Fund has committed $29M in state support to begin construction of a 330-unit affordable high-rise at 350 S. Fifth Avenue in downtown Ann Arbor near the Blake Transit Center. The Governor's office framed the action as a workforce-housing measure but the location and program will absorb meaningful upper-division demand near the University of Michigan campus.

stories.headline: Village of Ann Arbor 600+ Townhomes/Apartments Earns Conditional OK
stories.text: The Village of Ann Arbor — a 600-plus-unit townhome and apartment scheme near Dhu Varren and Pontiac Trail — received conditional planning approval. The site sits on a former landfill, requiring environmental modifications coordinated with the Michigan DEQ before vertical work proceeds.

stories.headline: Five Cohousing Projects in the Works in Berkeley
stories.text: Seattle-based Frolic Community is conducting a feasibility study at 2400 San Pablo Avenue (the former Ohmega Salvage site) for a 30–50 unit mixed-income cohousing development. The transit-corridor site is one of five cohousing concepts currently moving through Berkeley's pipeline, signaling continued small-format experimentation in the East Bay near UC Berkeley.

stories.headline: Scion and Ares Close $910M Harrison Street Portfolio — the Largest Student Housing Trade of the Cycle
stories.text: Harrison Street Asset Management has closed the $910 million sale of a 12-property, 7,578-bed U.S. student housing portfolio to affiliates of The Scion Group and an Ares Real Estate fund. The transaction is the largest single student housing portfolio trade of the current cycle and consolidates Scion's position as the most operationally scaled platform in the sector. Press materials confirm assets sit across 10 states and 12 university markets including Auburn University and Ohio State University. “This transaction reflects the durability of pricing for institutional-grade student housing in Tier 1 markets — even as broader multifamily comps remain in price discovery.” The implied per-bed average lands near $120,000, a figure consistent with cap rates in the high-4s to low-5s for assets adjacent to Power 4 campuses with strong walk scores. The capital structure pairs Scion's operating capability with Ares' equity, mirroring the Blackstone/Landmark and Brookfield-platform structures that have dominated the sector since 2024. Transaction Detail Headline price $910M Properties 12 Beds 7,578 Implied $/bed (avg) ~$120,085 States represented 10 Universities 12 (incl. Auburn, Ohio State) Buyer Scion Group / Ares Real Estate Seller Harrison Street

stories.headline: Balfour Beatty Communities Adds 288-Bed Clemson Village to Portfolio
stories.text: Balfour Beatty Communities has closed on the acquisition of Clemson Village, a 96-unit, 288-bed low-density duplex community located less than a mile from Clemson University. The asset features dedicated student-oriented programming and is the firm's first off-campus acquisition in the Carolinas. The transaction continues the steady accumulation of low-density, walk-to-campus product by operator-investors targeting steady-state cash flow rather than ground-up development risk.

stories.headline: MHN: Baylor, NAU and Tennessee Stabilize; Houston and Cornell Lag on Preleasing
stories.text: Multi-Housing News' May 2026 National Student Housing Report flags signs of stabilization in markets that had posted steep year-over-year rent declines earlier in the cycle, including Northern Arizona, Baylor University and Tennessee. On the laggard side, Houston, UT-Arlington, Cornell, Sam Houston State and UC Berkeley reported some of the lowest April preleasing levels nationally, all materially below the national average. Underwriting in those markets should explicitly contemplate a slower velocity curve for the Fall 2026 cycle.

stories.school_name: University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill
stories.headline: UNC's Roberts Unveils $300M Housing Plan: 730-Bed Replacement Dorm, 2,200-Bed Carolina North Phase 1
stories.text: Chancellor Lee Roberts has laid out the most explicit on-campus expansion plan at UNC in more than a decade: enroll an additional 500 students per year, adding 2,000 over the next four years and 5,000 across a 10-year horizon, all supported by a $300M housing investment. The headline near-term project is a new 730-bed residence hall on the current Admissions Office site, with the development pipeline anchored by a 2,200-bed Phase 1 at Carolina North — a long-dormant satellite campus the university has signaled it intends to activate. The plan represents a meaningful inflection in the University System of North Carolina's posture toward residential capacity expansion and creates an open question for off-campus operators in Chapel Hill: how much of the new 5,000-student cohort is realistically captured by the 2,930 announced beds, and what does that imply for off-campus rent growth over the planning horizon. UNC Housing Plan — Roberts Framework Total enrollment growth (10-yr) +5,000 students Annual cadence +500 / yr Stated capital commitment $300M New 730-bed hall Admissions Office site Carolina North Phase 1 2,200 beds

stories.headline: A&M Board Approves $6.8B FY27–FY31 Capital Plan; $1.5B in New Projects
stories.text: The Texas A&M Board of Regents on May 21 approved the FY27 operating budget alongside a five-year capital plan totaling $6.8 billion for FY27–FY31, of which approximately $1.5 billion are new proposed projects. Disclosed items include a satellite utility plant breakout. Specific residential program detail was not disclosed at this meeting; the package is the operative funding envelope under which any university-led housing P3 in College Station will need to be negotiated.

stories.headline: Oregon Closes Barnhart Hall as On-Campus Demand Falls 9–10%
stories.text: The University of Oregon will close Barnhart Residence Hall and Barnhart Dining Hall for the 2026–27 academic year, holding Riley Hall vacant as overflow. Housing Director Michael Griffel cited an estimated 9–10% decline in students choosing on-campus living, set against a broader $65M university budget shortfall driven by an out-of-state enrollment drop. Local coverage characterizes the move as the largest single residential capacity reduction at UO in recent memory; off-campus operators in Eugene should expect the displaced demand to compress at the high end of the comp set.

stories.headline: Stanford Sophomores Left Unassigned After First-Round Housing Selection
stories.text: Stanford's Residential & Dining Enterprises (R&DE) moved sophomores to last priority in the 2026–27 housing assignment cycle to prioritize upperclassmen, leaving a portion of the rising-sophomore cohort unassigned after the first round of selections. R&DE indicated it expects meaningful summer cancellations to absorb the gap. The decision is operationally notable for any off-campus operator marketing to second-years in the Palo Alto submarket.

stories.headline: Wake Forest Plants Charlotte Flag with Pearl District Campus Opening
stories.text: Wake Forest formally opened its permanent Charlotte campus at The Pearl innovation district on May 11. The initial footprint includes approximately 6,700 sf on the 10th floor, with the School of Medicine on the 12th floor and Wake Forest Law, Business and Professional Studies set to join inside the next twelve months. The expansion creates a new graduate-student housing demand node in uptown Charlotte that did not exist 24 months ago.

stories.headline: N.C. Gov. Stein Signs Executive Order 36 Directing Cabinet Agencies to Boost Housing Supply
stories.text: North Carolina Gov. Josh Stein on May 19 signed Executive Order No. 36 directing cabinet agencies to actively increase housing supply, affordability and access. State data cited in the order projects North Carolina will be short more than 750,000 homes by 2029. The directive is structured to ease permitting bottlenecks — relevant for both Triangle market entitlement timelines and for the operational lift behind UNC's Carolina North activation (above).

stories.headline: Charlottesville Council Revisits Short-Term Rental Rules After Graduation Surge
stories.text: The Charlottesville City Council reviewed short-term rental rule changes immediately following graduation weekend. Adjustments to STR policy are directly relevant to off-campus supply dynamics for UVA students — particularly for graduate and upper-division renters whose substitution between long-term leases and STR arrangements has tightened the local 12-month rental pool.

stories.school_name: Virginia Polytechnic Institute and State University
stories.headline: VT Board Preserves Living-Learning Programs; Provost Calls LLPs a Recruiting Edge
stories.text: The Virginia Tech Board of Visitors backed away from an April resolution that had questioned the financial impact of the university's living-learning communities. At the June meeting — the first under new leadership — the provost defended the LLP model as a recruiting attractor, foreclosing what had been an emerging risk to the residential program associated with the 1,200-bed expansion (Section 1, lead).

stories.headline: Columbia Holds FY26 Action Plan Hearing on ~$1.7M CDBG/HOME Housing Allocation
stories.text: The Columbia, Mo. City Council on May 18 held a public hearing on the FY 2026 Annual Action Plan, including approximately $1,068,090 in CDBG funds and $670,165 in HOME funds. The citywide allocation will not move the Mizzou off-campus comp set materially but is the operative gap-financing instrument for affordable adjacencies near the university.

stories.headline: Pitt Trustees Greenlight 420-Bed Freshman Residence Hall at Fifth and Ruskin
stories.text: First new residence hall since Nordenberg in 2013 — summer 2026 start, fall 2028 delivery — to anchor enrollment push toward 22,000 undergrads. The University of Pittsburgh Board of Trustees has formally approved construction of a 420-bed freshman residence hall at the corner of Fifth and Ruskin avenues, advancing the institution's first new undergraduate housing asset in more than a decade. The university said work will begin in summer 2026 with delivery targeted for fall 2028. The project is being executed by general contractor PJ Dick, with VMDO Architects and Kimmel Architecture handling design. Pitt has identified the hall as the centerpiece of a multi-phase housing strategy tied to its Plan for Pitt enrollment goal of 22,000 undergraduates on the Pittsburgh campus by 2028. University Times follow-up coverage emphasized that no new bed product has come online at Pitt since Nordenberg Hall opened in 2013, creating compounding pressure on adjacent Oakland off-campus inventory. For private developers tracking the Oakland market, the trust-approved start date locks in a 2026–2028 construction window that will pull mid-tier private inventory absorption — modeling 2028 lease-up should assume ~420 incremental on-campus freshman beds. Pitt Residence Hall — Snapshot Beds 420 Cohort Freshmen Construction Start Summer 2026 Opens Fall 2028 GC / Architects PJ Dick / VMDO / Kimmel

stories.headline: ASU Razes Three Mid-Century Dorms to Clear $400M Center Complex Site
stories.text: Best, Irish and Hayden halls — built 1940, 1951 and 1956 — demolished to make way for a 2,000–2,500-bed redevelopment. First 800 beds online fall 2028. Arizona State University has completed demolition of Best, Irish, and Hayden residential halls — three Tempe-campus dorms built between 1940 and 1956 — clearing the footprint for what ASU has positioned as its $400 million Center Complex. The replacement project is sized at roughly 2,000 to 2,500 beds and will subsume nine existing buildings across three legacy dorm compounds. Construction is scheduled to commence fall 2026 with the first 800 beds slated to deliver in fall 2028. For Tempe operators, the net add on-campus is meaningful given the displacement of legacy beds during construction; modeling should account for short-term off-campus absorption during the 2026–2028 build window followed by a step-function on-campus supply increase at delivery.

stories.headline: College Station Council Clears Path for Hub on Campus High-Rise at 603 Cherry St.
stories.text: College Station City Council on May 18 approved parking modifications and vacated sewer and utility easements at 603 Cherry Street, removing the principal procedural obstacle for a proposed Hub on Campus high-rise apartment complex adjacent to the Northgate entertainment district. The action does not constitute final site-plan approval, but the easement vacation is the entitlement step developers had been tracking publicly. The Cherry Street project would deliver into one of the densest off-campus submarkets in the country, where Hub-branded product has previously competed against Aspen Heights, The Cottages and Park West.

stories.school_name: Virginia Polytechnic Institute and State University
stories.headline: Virginia Tech to Break Ground June 8 on Four-Hall, 1,200-Bed Residence Plan
stories.text: Virginia Tech has confirmed that site work for a four-building, approximately 1,200-bed residence hall expansion will begin June 8, with the university relocating the remains of 61 individuals from the Holtzman Alumni Center columbarium to clear the development footprint. The decision has drawn family-led objections, but university spokesperson Mark Owczarski confirmed that long-range master plan documents prioritize the four-hall delivery and that work is moving on a compressed schedule. For Blacksburg operators, an on-campus delivery of this scale is the most material supply event in the market in over a decade.

stories.headline: Charlottesville Approves The Mark Student Housing in Fifeville on 3-2 Vote
stories.text: Charlottesville City Council voted 3-2 on May 4 to allow The Mark student housing development to proceed in the historically Black Fifeville neighborhood adjacent to the UVA campus. Residents from Fifeville, Westhaven, and 10th & Page have continued to organize in opposition on gentrification grounds, but the council action clears the entitlement path for the developer to advance. The narrow 3-2 margin is the key risk signal for follow-on Fifeville and 10th & Page student housing entitlements — future projects should expect substantial community-process burden.

stories.headline: Varsity Drive Project Tests Ann Arbor's New Comprehensive Land Use Plan
stories.text: The Ann Arbor Planning Commission is reviewing a proposed multifamily housing complex on Varsity Drive north of Ellsworth — one of the first rezoning applications advanced under the city's newly adopted Comprehensive Land Use Plan (CLUP). The CLUP framework was designed in part to absorb housing demand driven by University of Michigan enrollment growth, and how this site is handled will set the early procedural template for subsequent CLUP-driven density requests. Private student housing developers tracking Ann Arbor entitlement should monitor commission conditions on this first-in-class application.

stories.headline: Morrison Avenue Closes Construction Loan with Renasant for 222-Bed Hilltop Athens
stories.text: Morrison Avenue Capital Partners has secured construction financing from Renasant Bank for Hilltop Athens, a 222-bed purpose-built student housing development adjacent to the University of Georgia. CollegeTown Properties will manage the asset upon delivery. The financing is notable as a relatively rare regional-bank construction execution for purpose-built student in a tight-credit environment; debt providers willing to underwrite mid-size student deals at Athens remain concentrated and the Renasant close is a useful comp data point.

stories.headline: Austin Task Force Floats $770M Bond Package; Affordable Housing Carve-Out at Issue
stories.text: The Austin Bond Election Advisory Task Force has produced two competing 2026 bond options — a $766.53 million package and a narrowed $436 million alternative — that the City Council will weigh through May ahead of a potential election. Affordable housing is one of the named priority allocation areas. The bond is not exclusively a student housing instrument, but the scale of the proposed affordable housing component would meaningfully affect West Campus and East Riverside submarket fundamentals adjacent to UT-Austin if approved.

stories.headline: Mass Timber Student Tower Rises at 9th & High in University District
stories.text: Columbus Underground's May construction roundup features a street-level progress update on the 9th and High mass timber student housing tower in the Ohio State University District. The mass timber product type remains rare in U.S. purpose-built student housing — the 9th and High execution is one of the more visible test cases for the structural system at this scale.

stories.headline: Inn Town Lofts Delivers 56 Affordable Units in Downtown Lubbock
stories.text: Housing Trust Group and Alonzo Mourning's AM Affordable Housing have opened Inn Town Lofts — a 56-unit affordable apartment community in a long-vacant downtown Lubbock building near Texas Tech. The product is not student-specific but adds meaningfully to the Lubbock workforce/affordable supply that competes adjacent to off-campus student demand.

stories.headline: UC Advances $200M Welcome Gateway Building at Calhoun & Clifton
stories.text: The University of Cincinnati is moving forward on a 200,000-square-foot Welcome Gateway Building sitting atop a 400-space underground parking garage at Calhoun Street and Clifton Avenue. Total project cost is estimated at $200M with construction costs of $160M. Design-build selection deadline is June 30, with completion targeted December 2029.

stories.headline: DGA Breaks Ground on 121-Unit Riella on 5th in North Knoxville
stories.text: DGA Residential broke ground May 11 on Riella on 5th, a 121-unit affordable housing community along Fifth Avenue and Cooper Street just north of downtown Knoxville. While not specifically positioned as student housing, the project adds to the broader Knoxville rental supply within Tennessee's expanding submarket.

stories.headline: Champaign County Building Permits — Week of May 22-28
stories.text: The News-Gazette's weekly Champaign County building permits column for May 22-28 captures residential and multifamily activity in the UIUC market area. Worth a weekly scan for early-stage development signals in the Champaign-Urbana submarket.

stories.headline: UH Launches Interactive Map for Campus Lighting Modernization
stories.text: The University of Houston has launched an interactive public map tracking its ongoing campus lighting infrastructure project — part of broader campus modernization spending tied to the institution's residential capacity expansion plans.

stories.headline: Scion and Ares Close $910M, 12-Property Student Housing Buy from Harrison Street
stories.text: Largest U.S. student housing portfolio sale of 2026 — Auburn is among the leading-university markets in the acquired book. Harrison Street Asset Management has closed the largest U.S. student housing portfolio sale of 2026, transferring a 12-property book to affiliates of The Scion Group and an Ares Real Estate fund for $910 million. Auburn University is among the named leading-university markets represented in the portfolio. The transaction reaffirms Scion as the most active institutional accumulator of pedestrian-distance Power 4 student product and Ares as the dominant equity partner backing that buy-side strategy. For underwriters, the trade is the first 2026 benchmark of meaningful size in the student space and is likely to be cited in cap rate and per-bed pricing discussions for the next several months. Harrison Street's exit also signals continued tactical portfolio rotation by legacy institutional holders — an inflection that buyer-side dealmakers should be tracking for the next tranche of offerings. Portfolio Trade — Key Terms Headline Price $910M Properties 12 Seller Harrison Street Buyer Scion Group / Ares RE 2026 Rank #1 Largest SH Trade YTD

stories.headline: Coastal Ridge Adds 398-Bed Campus Court at Kentucky via TSB Realty
stories.text: TSB Realty has closed the sale of Campus Court — a 238-unit, 398-bed purpose-built student housing community near the University of Kentucky — to Coastal Ridge Real Estate. The transaction is the fourth asset acquired by Coastal Ridge's Value-Add Student Housing Fund. Financing was arranged by TSB Capital Advisors through J.P. Morgan. The trade gives a useful 2026 comp for value-add product in a tier-1 SEC market and signals continued fund-level appetite from Coastal Ridge for distressed-to-stabilized student plays. Campus Court — Trade Snapshot Beds / Units 398 / 238 Buyer Coastal Ridge RE Broker TSB Realty Debt J.P. Morgan via TSB Capital Advisors Fund Vehicle Coastal Ridge Value-Add SH Fund

stories.headline: Wisconsin DOA Opens Proposals for New UW-Madison Residence Hall — Responses Due July 16
stories.text: UW housing operating at 115% of designed capacity; two-site RFP names Dayton/Park (Merit Hall replacement) and Mills Street as candidates. The Wisconsin Department of Administration on May 14 issued a Request for Proposals for a new residence hall at UW-Madison, with all proposals due July 16, 2026 and a target delivery year of 2028. UW Housing is currently operating at 115% of designed capacity, with 8,987 residents housed in fall 2025 against a designed bed count of 7,749. Two specific sites have been identified for proposal evaluation: the Dayton/Park site, which would entail replacement of the existing Merit Hall, and a separate Mills Street site. For developer-operators and capital partners, the RFP is the most actionable Big Ten P3 opportunity surfaced in 2026 to date. The 115% utilization figure is the underwriting anchor and supports demand certainty; expected partners should be focused on construction cost certainty and the trade-off between Merit Hall demolition risk and the cleaner Mills Street site. UW-Madison RFP — Critical Dates RFP Released May 14, 2026 Proposals Due July 16, 2026 Target Completion 2028 Sites Identified Dayton/Park & Mills Street Current Occupancy 115% of designed capacity

stories.headline: Governor Stein Signs EO 36 to Address 750,000-Unit NC Housing Gap Through 2029
stories.text: North Carolina Governor Josh Stein has signed Executive Order No. 36 directing cabinet agencies to expand housing supply, affordability and access statewide, citing a projected gap of more than 750,000 housing units through 2029. The order specifically directs additional grants to local governments that adopt higher-density zoning policies — a meaningful pull-through for developers seeking up-zonings in Raleigh, Durham, Chapel Hill, and Winston-Salem submarkets. For NC State, Duke, and Wake Forest pipeline players, the EO is the single most actionable statewide policy tailwind to monitor in 2026.

stories.headline: Boulder Valley Comp Plan Headed for June Adoption; 35% Housing Capacity Lift in Draft
stories.text: A recommended draft of the Boulder Valley Comprehensive Plan is now in public review, with adoption hearings beginning in June. The draft would create capacity for roughly 35% more housing than the current plan, focused on land-use changes that support single-unit attached typologies — duplexes, triplexes, and townhomes. While not a purpose-built student housing instrument, the upzoning directly affects the off-campus rental ecosystem within walk-bike distance of CU Boulder and is the highest-impact 2026 land-use action for Boulder operators to track.

stories.headline: Berkeley Scales Back Corridor Upzoning; Elmwood Pushes Historic-District Designation
stories.text: Berkeley has scaled back its proposed rezoning of wealthier neighborhoods along Solano Avenue and other corridors following sustained community uproar at the Planning Commission. Separately, a parallel campaign in the adjacent Elmwood commercial strip is asking the Landmarks Preservation Commission to declare the area a historic district — a designation that, if approved, would meaningfully constrain new housing entitlements in a submarket directly adjacent to UC Berkeley. The two actions, taken together, materially raise the entitlement risk profile of Berkeley student housing development through 2026-2027.

stories.headline: Mizzou Curators Approve 4% Tuition Hike, 5.2% Housing Plan Increase for FY27
stories.text: The UM Board of Curators unanimously approved a 4% undergraduate tuition increase (3% graduate) and a 5.2% rise in the predominant Mizzou housing/dining plan to $13,807 for FY27, effective July 1, 2026. The dining/housing escalation directly raises the price umbrella under which off-campus operators in Columbia compete.

stories.headline: UH Regents Approve New Degrees and Program Consolidations
stories.text: The UH System Board of Regents on May 21 approved several new academic programs and degree consolidations across the UH system, with some changes set to start in fall 2026. The actions reinforce institutional momentum behind UH's enrollment trajectory toward 48,000.

stories.headline: UH on Track for Largest Graduating Class in History This Spring
stories.text: The University of Houston is on pace to graduate its largest class in school history this spring, underscoring the continued enrollment-growth pressure that has driven the proposed $179M freshman dorm project and broader Third Ward housing demand.

stories.headline: Rambler Plans Tallest Tower in College Station History as $125M Northgate Project Advances
