stories.text: Rambler is moving forward with the Rambler Northgate, a $125 million, 24-story purpose-built student housing tower that would become the tallest building ever constructed in College Station. The project, slated for the Northgate district adjacent to the Texas A&M campus, is programmed for roughly 300 units and 900 beds, anchoring what has become one of the most aggressive student housing development pipelines in the SEC. Construction is targeted to commence April 2, 2026, with delivery scheduled for June 7, 2028 — timing that would put the asset into service ahead of the fall 2028 academic year. The vertical build represents a significant density increase for Northgate, a district that has historically been dominated by 3- to 6-story product, and reflects the continued migration of capital into deep-supply, demand-tested A&M. The Rambler Northgate joins an already crowded pipeline near campus. With enrollment north of 77,000 and continued waitlist pressure in fall housing, College Station has emerged as one of the most active off-campus development markets in the country. Whether the market can absorb concurrent high-rise deliveries — including elevated-height product from competing operators — will be a 2027-2028 underwriting question. College Station Pipeline Snapshot Project Rambler Northgate Investment $125,000,000 Units / Beds ~300 / ~900 Height 24 stories (city-tallest) Construction Start Apr 2, 2026 Delivery Jun 7, 2028

stories.headline: Morrison Avenue Breaks Ground on 222-Bed Hilltop Athens
stories.text: Morrison Avenue Capital Partners has closed construction financing and broken ground on Hilltop Athens, a 222-bed purpose-built student housing community at 218 North Avenue, within a mile of the University of Georgia campus. The project, a mix of luxury townhomes and garden flats, is targeted for delivery ahead of the fall 2027 academic year. Hilltop Athens fits the prevailing UGA underwriting pattern — boutique-scale, walkable, premium-finish product positioned to capture upperclassmen and graduate demand. With UGA enrollment continuing to grow and the city's purpose-built supply still tight, financiers have continued to support smaller, infill projects of this profile despite a higher cost-of-capital environment. Morrison Avenue did not disclose financing terms. The closing follows a sequence of mid-spring debt closings in the Southeast — a signal that student-housing lenders, while selective, have remained open to mid-market sponsors with executed entitlements and credible delivery timelines.

stories.headline: LCD Acquisitions Refiles The Mark; Charlottesville Plan Pipeline Stays Active
stories.text: LCD Acquisitions filed Version 3 of its Development Plan for The Mark on May 7 — a 179-unit project advancing by-right under Charlottesville's Residential Mixed Use 5 (RX-5) zoning, with an in-lieu affordable housing fee of $4,470,303. The submission keeps one of the city's higher-profile by-right projects on track under the new zoning code. Separately, the city's Westhaven redevelopment plan was approved March 9 with $15 million in committed Council funding, and a series of smaller plan reviews continue across the corridor — together representing a notable concentration of near-campus and near-Downtown housing activity following the 2023 zoning rewrite.

stories.headline: Michigan Regents Greenlight $8M Site Prep for Next Phase of Wolverine Village
stories.text: The University of Michigan Board of Regents on May 15 authorized $8 million in site preparation for the next phase of the Central Campus Residential Development, advancing demolition of 51 residential structures bounded by E. Madison St., Hill St., S. Fifth Ave. and S. Division St. The action clears land for the continued buildout of the Wolverine Village P3 housing project, with Phase 1 (2,300 beds) targeted for fall delivery. Site prep includes the relocation of an historic home and additional environmental and utility scoping. The Regents' approval keeps one of the Big Ten's largest active on-campus housing P3s on schedule.

stories.headline: American Development Plans $63M, 431-Bed Conversion at JCTC
stories.text: American Development Corp. is advancing a $63 million redevelopment of the Jefferson Education Center near JCTC into a 431-bed student housing community. The plan calls for renovations beginning in late 2026 and new construction in early 2027, targeting fall 2028 occupancy. The capital stack is being assembled with private investment and applications for project-level approvals.

stories.headline: Eugene Council Clears Height Increase for UO East Campus Expansion
stories.text: Eugene City Council voted 5-3 on May 11 to amend the Fairmount/UO Special Area Study and the Eugene Code, rezoning portions of the East Campus area to allow heightened dormitories. Height limits along sections of E. 15th-19th Avenues rise from 45 to 85 feet. The package clears the way for a 5-story residence hall at Moss/Moon Lee/17th, set for delivery in 2028, and removes a land use overlay near Matthew Knight Arena.

stories.headline: LV Collective Files 1,022-Bed Burbank Corridor Project Near LSU
stories.text: Austin-based LV Collective has submitted plans for a 338-unit, 1,022-bed student housing complex along Burbank Drive near Milford Avenue, redeveloping a 4.58-acre tract bordered by Milford, Gourrier and Janet avenues, West Parker Boulevard and Burbank Drive. The site currently contains the El Cid and Embassy apartments. Filing comes as LSU enrollment continues to set records and as the system president has publicly floated the prospect of an enrollment cap citing housing constraints.

stories.headline: Berkeley Advances Corridor Upzoning
stories.text: Berkeley moved closer to approving its corridors zoning update on May 13, with proposed increases in the Elmwood, Shattuck and Solano corridors — a citywide supply story with direct relevance to UC Berkeley off-campus demand. Hearings continue.

stories.headline: Two Multifamily Projects Under Construction in Eudora
stories.text: Construction is underway on 10 Union Lofts (96-unit multifamily) and Paschal's Landing (36-unit, 30 affordable) in Eudora, just east of Lawrence. 10 Union Lofts received industrial revenue bonds and a 10-year, 75% property tax abatement; Paschal's secured $830,000 in LIHTC.

stories.headline: Northwestern's Vacant Properties Drawing Scrutiny
stories.text: Northwestern University has no current plan for repairing vacant homes it owns in Evanston, representatives said at the May 12 Northwestern University-City Committee meeting. Questions raised about NU's broader property holdings and maintenance practices as the city's housing dialog intensifies.

stories.headline: Syracuse Students Redesign 601 Park Street
stories.text: Syracuse University architecture students completed a redesign of an aging two-story bakery and apartment structure at 601 Park Street owned by Northside Futures, expanding residential and commercial uses. The project includes hands-on construction training for the cohort.

stories.headline: UCLA Pushes 800K SF Westside Pavilion Conversion
stories.text: UCLA released the environmental study for converting the former Westside Pavilion mall (10800-10850 W. Pico Blvd) into an 800,000 sq ft research and innovation campus. Adaptive reuse with new construction; phased delivery between late 2027 and 2035. Not student housing — but a material adjacent-campus footprint shift.

stories.headline: Core Spaces Closes $1.6 Billion Student Housing Fund
stories.text: A $1.6B equity raise validates institutional appetite for purpose-built student housing — and underlines that capital is still flowing to the largest, deepest-platform sponsors. Core Spaces has closed its flagship student housing fund, raising $1.6 billion from global investors — a marquee capital markets event for the sector and one of the largest dedicated student-housing equity vehicles ever assembled. The fund will continue to support new development and acquisitions across Core Spaces' platform. Core Spaces is the developer, with TPG, of the 2,195-bed Hub Raleigh project near NC State, which is scheduled to deliver in summer 2026. The fund close validates institutional appetite for purpose-built student housing at scale and signals continued allocation flow into the asset class despite a higher cost of capital.

stories.headline: University of Houston Weighs $179M Freshman Housing Spend
stories.text: The University of Houston System regents are scheduled to consider a $179 million proposal to add 1,000 beds to the main campus, lifting total housing capacity to 10,000 students. Driver: enrollment exceeding 48,000. Several regents have flagged concerns about total cost and infrastructure burden, raising the possibility of a phased authorization.

stories.headline: Berkeley Targets $80M Homekey+ Award for People's Park, BART Sites
stories.text: Berkeley is pursuing up to $80 million in state Homekey+ grants for two supportive housing projects: $45 million for 85 units at North Berkeley BART and $35 million for 110 units at People's Park. Within the broader packages: 1,100 UC Berkeley student housing units at People's Park and 743 total units at North Berkeley BART. State award timing remains the gating item.

stories.school_name: University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill
stories.headline: UNC Picks Ayers Saint Gross to Master-Plan Carolina North in Largest Expansion in School History
stories.text: The largest expansion in UNC-Chapel Hill history is now on the clock — and developers tracking ACC P3 demand have a new top-of-watchlist solicitation cycle to follow. The UNC-Chapel Hill Board of Trustees unanimously approved Ayers Saint Gross as master plan designer for Carolina North — the largest campus expansion in UNC history — and authorized three additional firms (SOM, Lord Aeck Sargent and Perkins & Will) to lead infrastructure and ancillary planning work. The selection was made from a pool of 17 proposals. Ayers Saint Gross has served as UNC's lead planner and architectural advisor for nearly 30 years. Phase 1 of Carolina North includes 2,200 student beds, plus a 720-bed dormitory on main campus — a substantial housing-led component that puts UNC squarely into the P3 conversation despite the university's historical preference for in-house delivery. The trustees' action sets up an accelerated procurement track for the master planning, with downstream RFP/RFQ activity expected to follow as scope and phasing get defined. For developers and capital partners tracking student housing P3 opportunities, the Carolina North solicitation cycle warrants close monitoring. Scale, location and UNC's brand strength make this one of the most-watched P3 setups in the ACC. Carolina North Phase 1 Snapshot Lead Master Planner Ayers Saint Gross Supporting Firms SOM · Lord Aeck Sargent · Perkins & Will Phase 1 Student Beds ~2,200 Main Campus Dorm 720 beds Proposals Received 17

stories.headline: Rutgers Study: New Jersey Housing Construction Surged Early 2020s
stories.text: A new Rutgers-based Center for Real Estate study finds New Jersey housing construction surged in the early 2020s, with implications for housing supply near major universities including Rutgers-New Brunswick. The data set is a useful market-context input for sponsors underwriting Rutgers-adjacent acquisitions and developments.

stories.headline: UT-Austin Student Initiatives Spotlight West Campus Supply Squeeze
stories.text: The Daily Texan's coverage of student-led initiatives this month raises affordability and quality concerns about West Campus student housing supply — set against a record 9,900-student incoming freshman class and 55,000 total enrollment for fall 2025. The signal: continued willingness among campus stakeholders to support density and supply additions near campus.

stories.headline: KU's Kaw House P3 Ribbon-Cutting Marks First Kansas Mass Plywood Build
stories.text: KU's Dirt Works Studio and Tenants to Homeowners completed and opened Kaw House — a compact supportive home at 613 N. Third St., Lawrence — with a ribbon-cutting on May 15. The project is the first use of mass plywood panel (MPP) construction in Kansas and a small but operationally novel university-community partnership.

stories.headline: Evanston Adopts 'Housing4All' Strategic Plan
stories.text: Evanston City Council adopted its Strategic Housing Plan ('Housing4All') in a 7-2 vote on May 12. The framework is intended to guide affordability and equity actions citywide — relevant for any Northwestern-adjacent rental supply discussion.

stories.headline: Homekey Palo Alto Transitional Housing Opens
stories.text: Homekey Palo Alto, a transitional housing complex with a $37.2M budget (~$26M state-funded), held its ribbon cutting on May 14 on city-owned property near the Mountain View border. Adjacent context for Stanford-area community housing initiatives — not Stanford student housing.

stories.headline: LSU President Floats Enrollment Cap, Cites Housing Constraints
stories.text: LSU System President Wade Rousse said in a Q&A this month that LSU may need to consider an enrollment cap given multiple years of record-breaking freshman classes and growing pains tied to a lack of freshman housing and parking. "Growth for the sake of growth may not be optimal," Rousse said — a notable demand-side signal for sponsors evaluating Baton Rouge.

stories.headline: LSU Posts Largest Graduating Class Ever
stories.text: LSU graduated more than 5,700 degrees during spring commencement (May 15-16, 2026) — its largest class ever — reflecting soaring enrollment with more than 62,000 freshman applicants this cycle vs. 18,122 in 2016.

stories.headline: Pitt Trustees Greenlight 420-Bed Freshman Tower in Oakland As Record Class Crowds Campus
stories.text: Construction starts summer 2026 at Fifth and Ruskin; fall 2028 opening targeted as application count crests 74,000. The University of Pittsburgh's Board of Trustees on May 7 approved construction of a 420-bed first-year residence hall at the corner of Fifth and Ruskin avenues, advancing the most consequential on-campus housing addition in Pitt's recent capital cycle. The project, designed by VMDO Architects with PJ Dick as builder, is scheduled to break ground this summer and open for the fall 2028 academic year. Trustees framed the decision against a record admissions cycle: Pitt received nearly 74,000 applications for the Oakland campus this fall — a university high — and the fall 2026 first-year class is expected to land near 5,200 students after a fall 2025 cohort of 5,870. To bridge the gap, the university is leaning on interim leases and a two-year housing guarantee while the new tower comes online. The approval converts what had been a stated capacity squeeze into a committed pipeline project, and is being read by local market observers as a signal that Pitt intends to absorb growth on-campus rather than push first-year demand into the Oakland off-campus market. Pittsburgh Pipeline Snapshot Project Fifth & Ruskin First-Year Hall Beds 420 (first-year) Owner University of Pittsburgh Architect VMDO Builder PJ Dick Start Summer 2026 Delivery Fall 2028 Context 74,000 applications (record); ~5,200 fall '26 freshmen est.

stories.headline: LV Collective Plans College Station's Tallest Building: 24-Story, 922-Bed Tower at Northgate
stories.text: Rambler Northgate would set a new vertical mark for the Brazos Valley; UMB construction loan and Peninsula Investments equity close the capital stack. Austin-based LV Collective and Miami-based Peninsula Investments have closed financing on Rambler Northgate, a 24-story, 922-bed, 342-unit student housing tower planned for the Northgate district adjacent to Texas A&M's campus. At a total project cost reported at roughly $125 million, the development would deliver more than 300 units and surpass anything currently standing in College Station — a city where most student product has historically capped out well below mid-rise heights. UMB Bank is providing the construction loan; Peninsula Investments is the equity partner. The unit mix runs from studios to five-bedroom configurations, targeting upperclassmen and a campus that continues to crack enrollment records in step with Texas A&M's stated growth plans (see Section III). Developers are positioning the project as a flagship for a market that has steadily absorbed new beds without spec-driven concessions. "The tallest building in College Station." — KXXV, citing developer disclosures

stories.headline: After a 3–2 Vote, Charlottesville Council Clears Path for The Mark — Reversing a December BAR Denial
stories.text: Council overturns Board of Architectural Review on LCD Acquisitions' 7-story, 189-unit student-oriented project; BZA majority simultaneously affirms half-mile-of-Grounds designation. Charlottesville's City Council voted 3-2 on May 4 to issue a Certificate of Appropriateness to LCD Acquisitions for The Mark, a seven-story, 189-unit student-oriented apartment building at 207 7th Street SW in the Fifeville neighborhood. The vote reverses the Board of Architectural Review's December 2025 denial of the certificate, removing the last major entitlement hurdle before the developer can proceed. The Council action came eighteen days after the Charlottesville Board of Zoning Appeals, on April 16, reconvened and affirmed — by a fifth-member vote — the Zoning Administrator's determination that the site falls within the half-mile of UVA's Central Grounds boundary used to govern student housing eligibility under city zoning. The combined rulings effectively end two parallel administrative challenges that had stalled the project for most of the spring. The Mark is one of the larger purpose-built private student housing additions proposed in Charlottesville in recent years, and its progression to construction will be a meaningful test of how aggressively Charlottesville's revised code is willing to absorb mid-rise student product in neighborhoods adjacent to UVA.

stories.headline: Landmark Breaks Ground on 825-Bed Mark Auburn Downtown
stories.text: Athens, Ga.-based Landmark Properties broke ground April 15 on The Mark Auburn at 141 Wright Street, a project that will deliver 825 beds across 329 units in unit configurations from studios to five-bedrooms. The site sits within Auburn's downtown core and was permitted ahead of the city's broader multi-unit moratorium (see Section III).

stories.headline: LV Collective Asks East Baton Rouge to Rezone for 7-Story, 338-Unit Project
stories.text: LV Collective Student Housing has petitioned the East Baton Rouge Planning and Zoning Commission to rezone a parcel between Burbank Drive and Gourrier Avenue near LSU for a seven-story, 338-unit student housing complex. The commission was scheduled to take up the request the week of the filing; approval would extend LV's footprint into a corridor southeast of campus.

stories.headline: Preiss + FD Stonewater Plan 528-Bed Signature on Grand in Fort Sanders
stories.text: The Preiss Company, in partnership with FD Stonewater, announced Signature on Grand — a 528-bed off-campus development at 1727 Grand Avenue in Knoxville's Fort Sanders, serving UT-Knoxville. The Knoxville project is paired with a companion Signature at Varsity site near NC State, both slated for Fall 2027 delivery.

stories.headline: UW Housing Locks Down Halls for Mifflin Weekend Amid Tight Occupancy
stories.text: UW-Madison University Housing limited residents to one guest each and locked external doors during Mifflin Street Block Party weekend. The unusually restrictive posture reflects the pressure on Madison's residence halls following several record-enrollment years.

stories.headline: Evanston Breaks Ground on $22M Mt. Pisgah and a Pocket Neighborhood
stories.text: Evanston officials broke ground May 11 on Mt. Pisgah Apartments, a 33-unit, $22M affordable building at 1813 Church Street (HODC / Mt. Pisgah Ministry), with one-, two-, and three-bedroom units rented at $650, $850 and $1,050. Construction begins next month with summer 2027 delivery. A separate pocket neighborhood of efficiency homes broke ground May 8 on Grant Street — both tied to the Envision Evanston code rewrite.

stories.headline: Syracuse Enters Heaviest Summer Construction Cycle in Recent Memory
stories.text: Syracuse University will use summer break for what officials describe as one of the most active construction periods in recent years, including ongoing work on two new residence halls at the Waverly/Comstock cluster and a Pages Cafe replacement on the dining side.

stories.headline: Utah's Trailhead Dorm Opens This Fall as Phase 1 of 5,000-Bed Push
stories.text: The University of Utah's newest residence hall, Trailhead, is on track to open for fall 2026 as the first delivery under a long-term initiative targeting up to 5,000 new on-campus beds — one of the largest stated on-campus housing pushes in the Big 12.

stories.headline: Palo Alto Races SB 79 Effective Date with Pre-Emptive Rezoning
stories.text: Palo Alto is moving to adopt a local ordinance and rezoning strategy to clarify how California's SB 79 transit-oriented housing law will apply within city limits, ahead of the statute's July 2026 effective date — a development bearing on the Stanford sub-market and adjacent transit nodes.

stories.headline: College Park 4×4 Pricing Surfaces in Op-Ed Calling for Rent Caps
stories.text: A Diamondback opinion piece cites current per-bed off-campus pricing — 4BR/4BA starting at $1,359 at Terrapin Row, $1,208 at The Varsity, and $1,406 at Union on Knox — and argues for a rent cap targeted at buildings marketed as student housing.

stories.headline: South Bend Mayor Pegs Housing Pipeline at 2,000 Units
stories.text: Mayor James Mueller cited a 2,000-unit housing pipeline across South Bend as evidence of citywide momentum, including projects in the neighborhoods adjacent to Notre Dame. The framing tracks separate Realtor.com data ranking the South Bend-Mishawaka metro the No. 1 housing market in America for spring 2026.

stories.headline: 97-Unit Berkeley Building Hits Market After $25M Foreclosure Take-Back
stories.text: The 97-unit University Park Apartments at 1709 Shattuck Avenue, blocks from UC Berkeley, has been listed for sale following a $25 million foreclosure acquisition. Prior owner Academy West Investments defaulted on $28.3 million of debt, and the resulting REO marketing represents one of the more visible distressed Berkeley-market trades of 2026 to date — a useful data point on basis for a sub-market that has historically traded at thin going-in yields.

stories.headline: LV Collective & Peninsula Close ~$125M Rambler Northgate Stack With UMB Construction Loan
stories.text: LV Collective and Peninsula Investments closed financing on Rambler Northgate, the 922-bed/342-unit College Station tower covered in Section I, at a project cost reported around $125 million. UMB Bank is the construction lender; Peninsula is the named equity partner. The capital placement is one of the larger construction financings closed in the SEC student housing pipeline in 2026 year-to-date.

stories.headline: TTU System Buys Historic English Home for Chancellor's Residence
stories.text: The Texas Tech University System Board of Regents acquired the historic English Home on 19th Street, adjacent to campus, designating the 1938 Tudor Revival property as the official chancellor's residence. A specific purchase price was not disclosed in initial coverage; the property's protected status will constrain redevelopment of the parcel.

stories.headline: Knighthead Refis Signature Music Row With $27M Loan
stories.text: Preiss and Speedwagon Capital Partners landed a $27 million loan from Knighthead Funding to refinance Signature Music Row, a 105-unit rental community at 1005 16th Avenue South, two blocks from Vanderbilt. The refi prints into a market where bridge-to-perm SOFR spreads on similar assets have remained relatively wide through Q2.

stories.headline: UT Knoxville Advisory Board Convenes on FY26–27 Budget as Enrollment Growth Strains On-Campus Capacity
stories.text: The UT Knoxville Campus Advisory Board met May 12 to advance the FY 2026-27 budget, take an update on tuition, and review Division of Student Success priorities. University communications tied the agenda directly to fall 2026 enrollment projections and to retention-driven enrollment growth that continues to pressure on-campus housing demand — the clearest public framing yet from the administration that bed-count constraints are now a budget conversation rather than a routine facilities update. For developers tracking the Knoxville off-campus pipeline (see Preiss/Signature on Grand in Section I), the Board's framing is meaningful: the university is signaling enrollment outpacing on-campus capacity, which has historically supported lease-up velocity in the Fort Sanders / Cumberland Avenue corridor.

stories.headline: Auburn Council Receives Six-Month Update on Downtown Moratorium
stories.text: Six months into a yearlong moratorium on multi-unit and student housing developments near downtown Auburn, the City Council on May 5 received updates from the commissioned studies underpinning the policy. The Mark Auburn project (Section I) was permitted ahead of the moratorium and is not affected; pending and future projects within the moratorium boundary remain on hold.

stories.headline: A&M Regents Detail $400M+ Construction Slate
stories.text: Texas A&M's Board of Regents reviewed plans totaling more than $400 million across three projects: a veterinary building, a space collaboration facility, and a player development center — components of a broader capital cycle running concurrent with the Rambler Northgate private development on the Northgate frontier (Section I).

stories.headline: Metro Planning Heads to Vote on Vanderbilt's 40-Acre Innovation Neighborhood
stories.text: The Metro Planning Commission scheduled an April 23 vote on Vanderbilt's proposed Specific Plan rezoning for a 40-acre Innovation Neighborhood between West End and Natchez Trace. The plan includes new student housing among broader mixed-use components and represents one of the largest single-university rezoning packages in Nashville in recent years.

stories.headline: Wake Forest Selects Creekside at The Grounds as Affiliate Housing
stories.text: Wake Forest University has designated Creekside at The Grounds (521 students across 229 units) as its affiliate housing property. Eligible students may apply Creekside residency toward the university's six-semester on-campus housing requirement — a private-on-campus hybrid structure that effectively pulls private inventory into the university's housing system.

stories.headline: UConn Storrs Houses Record 13,400; Housing Demand Up 11.25%
stories.text: A Daily Campus year-in-review notes UConn housed 13,400 students at Storrs in fall 2025 — a record — with housing demand up 11.25% (1,172 applications) from fall 2024 to fall 2025. The data point is consistent with a multi-year demand trajectory that has supported lease-up activity for off-campus developers in the Storrs sub-market.

stories.headline: USG Calls on USC to Guarantee Four Years of Housing
stories.text: USC's Undergraduate Student Government unanimously approved Senate Resolution 145-26 asking the university to implement a four-year housing guarantee. The resolution also pushes USC to prioritize upper-class housing development — a politically meaningful ask in a market where private off-campus product has dominated upperclassman supply.

stories.headline: Iowa Regents Approve 5% Increase to ISU Room & Apartment Rates
stories.text: The Iowa Board of Regents reviewed Iowa State agenda items at its April 22-23 meeting, including approval of ISU's 2026-27 housing and dining rate plan — a 5% increase to room and apartment rates and a 2% increase on dining. The rate move slightly compresses the comparative pricing gap with Ames off-campus product.
